entries.title: Summarize agent activity
entries.description: Reads an activity log written by motif mcp --activity-log and reports calls by tool, errors, refusals by code, and how often the agent followed the advice it was given. Nothing is sent anywhere.
entries.helpPage:
# Summarize agent activity

`activity` reads an activity log and reports how Motif's MCP server served an AI agent: the calls by tool, how many came back as errors, the refusals by code, and how often the agent followed the advice it was given.

The log exists only when the server was started with `motif mcp --activity-log <file>`; without that option nothing is written. The file stays on your machine, and `activity` only reads it. Nothing is sent anywhere.

## When to use it

Use it after an agent session to see where the agent was refused and whether it acted on each response's next step. "Followed" means the call used the tool the previous response's next step named; its arguments are not compared. The first call of a session counts as neither followed nor ignored.

## Example

```powershell
motif activity --log "C:\Motif\session-activity.jsonl" --json
```

## What it prints

The response counts all calls, the calls that came back as errors, calls per tool, refusals per refusal code, and the calls that followed or ignored the previous next step. Lines written by an older Motif that lack the next-step field are still read and counted as neither. A line that is not a log entry is skipped. When the file is missing or unreadable, the command refuses and says how to start a session that writes one.

entries.title: Describe a Corpus
entries.description: Creates an empty Corpus and records its provenance, tokenisation, and licence capabilities. Use it before adding Documents to the Corpus.
entries.helpPage:
# Describe a Corpus

`add-corpus` records a Corpus and how it was collected and tokenised. It keeps provenance and licence capabilities so later users can tell what use is permitted.

## When to use it

Use this before adding Documents to a new Corpus. State what the licence permits, including whether the material may be derived from, redistributed, or used commercially; unknown permissions should remain unknown.

## Example

```powershell
motif add-corpus --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --id "stories" --description "Published folktales" --tokeniser "motif-basic" --tokeniser-version "1"
```

## What it prints

Human output confirms the Corpus id and shows its origin, location when supplied, licence, tokenisation, and derivation note.

## Related commands

- [Add a Corpus Document](cmd:add-document) attaches a source to the Corpus.
- [List Corpora](cmd:corpora) finds recorded Corpus ids.
usage: Usage: motif add-corpus --project <fwdata> --id <id> --description <text> --tokeniser <name> --tokeniser-version <v> [--uri <url>] [--licence <text>] [--tokeniser-notes <text>] [--may-derive true|false] [--may-redistribute true|false] [--may-use-commercially true|false] [--requires-attribution true|false] [--licence-basis <text>]

entries.title: Load a Corpus bundle
entries.description: Reads a bundle from a fetching tool and loads each listed source as a Document in its Corpus. The Motif store keeps the fetched text with its provenance and licence details.
entries.helpPage:
# Load a Corpus bundle

`add-corpus-bundle` reads a bundle from a fetching tool, then reads each listed source to add its Document to a Corpus. The bundle records source locations and licences; it does not contain the source text files.

## When to use it

Use this when an outside tool has prepared a Corpus bundle and you want Motif to record its provenance in one step. Inspect the bundle and its licences before loading it.

## Example

```powershell
motif add-corpus-bundle --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --bundle "C:\Temp\stories-bundle.json"
```

## What it prints

Human output identifies the Corpus and document count, then shows its origin, licence, derivation restrictions, and accuracy-claim qualification. Motif stores the fetched text with the Corpus; it does not copy text into the FieldWorks project.

## Related commands

- [Describe a Corpus](cmd:add-corpus) creates the Corpus directly.
- [List Corpora](cmd:corpora) reads Corpora already recorded for the project.
usage: Usage: motif add-corpus-bundle --project <fwdata> --bundle <path>   (the handoff a fetching tool writes)

entries.title: Add a Corpus Document
entries.description: Reads one source file or URL into a named Corpus Document and records its origin and licence details. Use it to preserve where an individual Document came from.
entries.helpPage:
# Add a Corpus Document

`add-document` reads one source file or URL and stores its text as a Document in a named Corpus. It records the source, title, and licence without treating the Document as a FieldWorks Text.

## When to use it

Use this after creating a Corpus when you need to preserve where one article or file came from. Provide a stable Document id and the source location; include licence details for this item when they differ from the Corpus.

## Example

```powershell
motif add-document --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --corpus "stories" --doc "story-12" --source "https://example.org/story-12" --title "The River Path"
```

## What it prints

Human output confirms the Corpus and Document ids and shows the title, source, character count, content hash, and licence when supplied.

## Related commands

- [Describe a Corpus](cmd:add-corpus) records the shared provenance and tokeniser.
- [Show a Corpus](cmd:show-corpus) reads its provenance and licence capabilities.

entries.title: Set a sense gloss
entries.description: Stages the explicitly authored gloss of one sense in one writing system in a Draft. Dry Run and Trial the Draft before Finalize; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a sense gloss

Stages the explicitly authored gloss of one sense in one writing system in a Draft. Dry Run and Trial the Draft before Finalize; only a person can Apply.

To record where the gloss came from, add `--cite-source` with the work cited and, optionally, `--cite-locator` with the page or section. The [citation](term:citation) shows beside the change when the Proposal is shown or Dry Run, and does not change what the Proposal does.

entries.title: Inspect word analyses
entries.description: Lists manually approved analyses, or adds parser results from a named Assessment when current digests are supplied. It does not run PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Inspect word analyses

`analyses` reads the project's manually approved analyses. With an Assessment id and both current digests, it also returns that Assessment's parser results and says whether they still describe the project.

## When to use it

Use this command when you need to inspect analysis evidence without starting PanGloss. The Assessment form reports whether the current Selection and grammar digests match the evidence.

## Example

```powershell
motif analyses --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Without `--assessment`, the response lists manually approved analyses from a private copy of the saved FieldWorks project. With an Assessment and current Selection and grammar SHA-256 values, it reads manual facts from that Assessment's exact Baseline and includes the stored parser results. Later FieldWorks saves do not change those captured facts. If that Baseline is unavailable, the request is refused.

`projectContext` records whether the manual facts come from the saved project or a Baseline, with the represented source-save time and the exact Baseline token when applicable. The supplied digests describe whether the Assessment still matches the current Selection and grammar; they do not select a different source for its manual facts. JSON returns the same information in a structured response.

## Related commands

- [Read one word's context](cmd:word-context) includes Unknown and Disapproved analyses without an Assessment.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records parser evidence.
- [Query parse statistics](cmd:stats) reads detailed statistics for an Assessment.

entries.title: Apply with Readiness override
entries.description: Applies one Proposal using its already bound Dry Run. The optional --force option skips Readiness checks only; changes that no longer fit remain refused. MCP never applies; the CLI applies in person or in Autonomous mode, which refuses --force.
entries.helpPage:
# Apply with Readiness override

This CLI command applies a Proposal using its already bound Dry Run. The optional `--force` switch lets a person proceed (Autonomous mode refuses it) when a Readiness reason remains.

## Usage

```text
motif apply <proposalId> --project <fwdata> [--force] [--autonomous] [--message <text>] [--note] [--json]
```

After Apply has saved the project, the next Dry Run or Trial of another Proposal captures a new Baseline by itself. A save made outside Motif is different: a Dry Run is refused with `change.refresh-required` until you capture a new Baseline with `motif baseline capture` (in the window, Refresh).

## Readiness and `--force`

Without `--force`, Apply can be refused with `apply.not-ready` when its current evidence does not satisfy Readiness. A timing-only Trial supplies no Correctness Assessment. A Trial that requests Correctness can record a result with zero approved expectations; that result supplies no comparison of approved readings. In a project with no stems, inspect the recorded parse results and approved comparisons before deciding whether to proceed. Apply and the Review window read the newest Correctness Assessment of the revision that leaves the Proposal ready, checking the newest ten at most and stopping at the first ready one; an older Assessment past those ten is not read. A Trial names any grammar the parser dropped with only a warning, such as an environment it could not read. When that dropped grammar is in what the Proposal adds or edits, the Trial is not clean, and Apply is refused with `apply.dropped-grammar` until it is fixed, in the Proposal or in FieldWorks, and the Proposal is tried again. When the parser could not check for dropped grammar, or the Trial was made before the check existed, the Trial says so and is not clean; Apply is then refused with `apply.not-ready` until the Proposal is tried again.

`--force` skips the Readiness reasons for this command. It does not create or change an Assessment, and it does not bypass checks that the proposed changes still fit the current project. Changes that no longer fit, or whose fit is uncertain, remain refused.

## Mode, message and note

Every Receipt records how the Proposal was applied, `person` or `autonomous`, and a message. With no marker the mode is `person`, and the message defaults to the Proposal's label; `--message <text>` replaces it (one line, at most 128 characters). An agent declares Autonomous mode with `--autonomous` or by setting `MOTIF_AUTONOMOUS=1` in its environment, and an autonomous Apply is refused with `apply.message-required` unless it gives a `--message`; combining Autonomous mode with `--force` is refused with `apply.autonomous-force`. The window always records `person`.

`--note` also writes one Notebook record of the "Motif change" type in the same unit of work as the changes: its title is the Proposal's label, and its text is the Rationale, the Receipt reference and the message. It is off by default. A later Proposal applied with `--note` writes its own note, and the earlier note remains.

Apply is not available to MCP clients. The other Released paths are [Apply one Proposal](cmd:apply%20--proposal) and [Apply pending changes](cmd:apply%20--all-pending).

entries.title: Apply pending changes
entries.description: Applies the current pending changes to the FieldWorks project as one unit of work. A current Dry Run can waive Correctness for a judgment-only Proposal; mixed changes still need normal Readiness evidence.
entries.helpPage:
# Apply pending changes

`motif apply --all-pending` applies all changes in the current pending Draft Proposal to the FieldWorks project in one unit of work. Motif records a Receipt when it writes changes.

## When to use it

Use this command after reviewing the pending Proposal and while FieldWorks has released the project. FieldWorks should reload the project after Motif reports a write.

A Proposal made only of the bounded Notebook judgment writes can be ready without a Correctness Assessment when its current bound Dry Run shows only Notebook record, owned-text and reserved-field effects. Mixed Proposals still need normal Readiness evidence. The Apply result records whether Correctness was exempt and why; Dry Run, Preflight and Apply still apply.

When Apply is refused with `apply.not-ready`, the current evidence does not satisfy Readiness. A timing-only Trial supplies no Correctness Assessment. A Correctness result with zero approved expectations supplies no comparison of approved readings. In a project with no stems, inspect the recorded parse results and comparisons. `--force` does not skip Readiness here; only [`motif apply <proposalId> --force`](cmd:apply) does, and Autonomous mode refuses `--force` everywhere. A Trial names any grammar the parser dropped with only a warning, such as an environment it could not read. When that dropped grammar is in what the Proposal adds or edits, the Trial is not clean, and Apply is refused with `apply.dropped-grammar` until it is fixed, in the Proposal or in FieldWorks, and the Proposal is tried again. When the parser could not check for dropped grammar, or the Trial was made before the check existed, the Trial says so and is not clean; Apply is then refused with `apply.not-ready` until the Proposal is tried again.

## Example

```text
motif apply --all-pending --project <project> [--revision <r>] [--autonomous] [--message <text>] [--note] [--json]
```

## Mode, message and note

Every Receipt records how the Proposal was applied, `person` or `autonomous`, and a message. With no marker the mode is `person`, and the message defaults to the Proposal's label; `--message <text>` replaces it (one line, at most 128 characters). An agent declares Autonomous mode with `--autonomous` or by setting `MOTIF_AUTONOMOUS=1` in its environment, and an autonomous Apply is refused with `apply.message-required` unless it gives a `--message`; combining Autonomous mode with `--force` is refused with `apply.autonomous-force`. The window always records `person`.

`--note` also writes one Notebook record of the "Motif change" type in the same unit of work as the changes: its title is the Proposal's label, and its text is the Rationale, the Receipt reference and the message. It is off by default. A later Proposal applied with `--note` writes its own note, and the earlier note remains.

## What it prints

The JSON response has `ok`, `applied`, `summary` and, when changes were applied, a `receipt` that carries the Readiness decision. Reload after `applied: true`. When the response carries `apply.reconciliation-needed`, a write may have happened or an earlier one was never confirmed. Reload, open Motif to check the project, and do not retry automatically. A no-op does not need a reload, and an uncertain change stays pending for review.

## Related commands

- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) reads stored evidence after you reload the project.

entries.title: Apply one Proposal
entries.description: Applies one Proposal to the FieldWorks project as one unit of work, using the result of its latest Trial. MCP never applies; the CLI applies in person or in Autonomous mode. It has no Readiness override of its own.
entries.helpPage:
# Apply one Proposal

`motif apply --proposal <id>` applies one Proposal to the FieldWorks project in one unit of work, then records a Receipt. A Proposal that is still a Draft is finalized first. It takes the same path as `apply --all-pending`: every change is checked once against the project, and a refused Apply reopens the Draft under the same id. FieldWorks is checked first: while it holds the project, Apply is refused before anything else is done.

## When to use it

Use it after reviewing a Proposal and trying it. The Proposal's latest Trial must be current: neither the Proposal nor the project may have changed since. Close the project in FieldWorks first, and reload it afterwards.

## Example

```text
motif apply --proposal <id> --project <project> [--autonomous] [--message <text>] [--note] --json
```

## Mode, message and note

Every Receipt records how the Proposal was applied, `person` or `autonomous`, and a message. With no marker the mode is `person`, and the message defaults to the Proposal's label; `--message <text>` replaces it (one line, at most 128 characters). An agent declares Autonomous mode with `--autonomous` or by setting `MOTIF_AUTONOMOUS=1` in its environment, and an autonomous Apply is refused with `apply.message-required` unless it gives a `--message`; combining Autonomous mode with `--force` is refused with `apply.autonomous-force`. The window always records `person`.

`--note` also writes one Notebook record of the "Motif change" type in the same unit of work as the changes: its title is the Proposal's label, and its text is the Rationale, the Receipt reference and the message. It is off by default. A later Proposal applied with `--note` writes its own note, and the earlier note remains.

## What it prints

The JSON response has `ok`, `applied`, and a one-line `summary`, as `apply --all-pending` does. A Proposal that has not been tried is refused with `apply.trial-missing`; one that changed since its Trial is refused with `apply.trial-stale`. If the response contains `apply.reconciliation-needed`, reload and inspect the project because a write may have happened.

## Readiness

Apply can be refused with `apply.not-ready` when the current Trial has no Correctness Assessment for this revision. A timing-only Trial supplies no Correctness Assessment. A Correctness result with zero approved expectations supplies no comparison of approved readings. In a project with no stems, inspect the recorded parse results and comparisons. `--force` does not skip Readiness here; only [`motif apply <proposalId> --force`](cmd:apply) does, and Autonomous mode refuses `--force` everywhere, so collect the required evidence before applying. Apply and the Review window read the newest Correctness Assessment of the revision that leaves the Proposal ready, checking the newest ten at most and stopping at the first ready one; an older Assessment past those ten is not read. A Trial names any grammar the parser dropped with only a warning, such as an environment it could not read. When that dropped grammar is in what the Proposal adds or edits, the Trial is not clean, and Apply is refused with `apply.dropped-grammar` until it is fixed, in the Proposal or in FieldWorks, and the Proposal is tried again. When the parser could not check for dropped grammar, or the Trial was made before the check existed, the Trial says so and is not clean; Apply is then refused with `apply.not-ready` until the Proposal is tried again.

## Related commands

See [Review a Proposal's changes](cmd:proposal%20review) and [Apply pending changes](cmd:apply%20--all-pending).

entries.title: Measure a Selection
entries.description: Runs PanGloss over chosen Texts or word forms and stores the resulting Assessments. After FieldWorks saves project changes, capture a new Baseline before measuring them.
entries.helpPage:
# Measure a Selection

`assess` sends a Selection of words through PanGloss and stores the resulting Assessments. It uses the project's stored Baseline when one exists and captures one only when the project has none.

## When to use it

Use this to measure how a grammar parses the project's usual words, named Texts, every wordform, or a supplied word list. After FieldWorks saves grammar changes, capture a new Baseline before measuring them.

To parse some words again and update their main results, pass `--replaces <assessment-id>` with the id of the complete ParseTime Assessment they belong to. The replacement must use that same Baseline and contain only words in that Assessment. Each replaced word keeps the new run's id and measurement time; untouched words keep theirs. A run without `--replaces` records a separate measurement without replacing words in an existing run.

To select words whose recorded parser work exceeds a threshold, use `--retry-work-over <parser-work> --retry-source-assessment <id>`. Words without a recorded work count cannot match this selector.

## Example

```powershell
motif assess "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --all-wordforms --json
```

For an explicit reparse, save the chosen words in a file and name their original run:

```powershell
motif assess "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --words words.txt --replaces <assessment-id> --json
```

## What it prints

Human output reports the Selection and stored Assessment ids, followed by each word's comparison headline and any qualification on a second line. For example, when a completed search builds a Disapproved analysis but misses the word's undecided analysis, it prints “Rebuilt an analysis you Disapproved” and “Your undecided analysis wasn't built”.

Both human output and JSON begin with `counts`: how many words were measured, how many came out `analysed`, `noAnalysis`, `capped` (stopped at the work limit), `timedOut` (stopped at the time safety net) or `skipped`, and among the analysed words how many are `accepted` (some reading identifies every morph in the lexicon) and how many are `guessOnly` (every reading contains a morph the parser had to guess because it could not identify it, such as `a+?baga`). An analysed word is not necessarily an accepted one.

JSON returns the Baseline, Selection, and Assessment results. Each word's `comparison` carries its standing, outcome, stable `meaningCode`, headline, detail, completion flag and tone, plus matched analysis identities and their individual opinions, missing Approved analyses, rebuilt Disapproved analyses and extra readings. This is the same comparison used by the window; display wording is not a grouping identity.

The comparison's `availability` distinguishes `Available` (analysis identities were compared), `RecordedGradesOnly` (recorded reading grades are known, but matched analysis identities are unknown), and `Unavailable` (no morphology comparison was recorded or reconstructed). Unavailable evidence is not a known empty set. An incomplete search makes no claim that an Approved or undecided analysis was not built. No grammar verdict is inferred from the measurements.

## Limits

Assess and Trial use the Default Selection's per-word parser work limit and time policy, including for a supplied word list. A Trial's automatic before Assessment uses the exact limits frozen for the Trial. A stop at the work limit is the same on every computer. A stop at the time safety net varies with machine load, so compare `capped` and `timedOut` separately, and inspect the recorded limits before comparing independent runs. In JSON each stopped word's `stoppedBy` is `work-limit`, `time-safety-net`, or `both` when the work limit and the time safety net both fired inside that word's search; it is read from the word's outcome and the parser's evidence together, so a word that returned readings before a limit fired still names it. A word that was not stopped has no `stoppedBy`. A stopped word is not evidence that no analysis exists.

When object statistics are available, Motif keeps whole-run timing totals and per-object detail for the 2,000 words with the most parser work by default. If parser work are unavailable, it uses time on this computer. A named scope can set `timing-detail-words` in `<project>.motif.toml` to a number from 0 to 10,000. Results identify when word-level detail is incomplete. To keep detail for every word in an explicitly supplied Selection of at most 2,000 words, pass `--full-object-timing` with the Selection. A retry records object timings from the initial pass; it does not supply object timings for the retried result.

Each Assessment has a whole-run time limit, including retries; it is a time on this computer, not a measure of parser work. The project Parsing setting defaults to 3,600 seconds; `--max-seconds <seconds>` overrides it for this run, with a minimum of 60 seconds. If the limit is reached, Motif stops the parser, reports the number of words done and not done, records a `stopped-by-budget` job, and saves no Assessment. The command exits with code 5.

## A large list

`--words <file>` reads a UTF-8 file with one word per line, so a list of thousands of words needs no other preparation. The full JSON result grows with the list. Add `--summary` to print only the counts and one page of words, each with its outcome, whether its reading was accepted or guess-only, its `parserWork` when the parser counted them (a skipped word has none) and its `stoppedBy` when a limit stopped it; `--offset <n>` and `--limit <n>` choose the page (default 25 words from the start), and the output says which words it shows, such as “showing 1-25 of 7206”. The Assessment is stored whole either way.

An agent reads the same summary through the `motif_assess` tool. It returns the counts, one page of words and the stored Assessment id, and pages through that Assessment with `assessment`, `offset` and `limit` rather than measuring again. `wordsFile` names the word file as `--words` does, and giving both `words` and `wordsFile` is refused with `assess.words-ambiguous`. A file that is missing or unreadable is refused with `assess.words-file-unreadable`, and one with no words with `assess.words-file-empty`.

Word files must be at most 8 MiB of valid UTF-8 text without NUL bytes; an initial UTF-8 signature is accepted. A larger file is refused with `assess.words-file-too-large`; invalid UTF-8 or NUL bytes with `assess.words-file-not-text`. Split a large list into smaller files, or save a non-text file as UTF-8 with one word per line, then repeat the call.

## Related commands

- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) reads the usual word list.
- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) displays evidence already stored.

entries.title: Capture a Baseline
entries.description: Reads the saved .fwdata project to create or reuse a file-backed Baseline. Use it when the latest FieldWorks save should be the point of comparison for later work.
entries.helpPage:
# Capture a Baseline

`baseline capture --project` reads a saved `.fwdata` file and creates or reuses a file-backed Baseline. You can name a Known project by its name or pass its `.fwdata` path. The capture represents the project as of FieldWorks' last save.

## When to use it

Use this when a later Dry Run or Assessment should be measured against the latest saved project state. FieldWorks may remain open, but unsaved in-memory edits are not part of the capture.

## Example

```powershell
motif baseline capture --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

The response identifies the project, Baseline digest, capture time, source save time, and whether the published bytes were reused. JSON returns the Baseline token and capture facts.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) ensures a Baseline exists before recording parser evidence.
- [Queue a Baseline Refresh](cmd:baseline-refresh) requests a durable queued capture.

entries.title: Queue a Baseline Refresh
entries.description: Queues a job to capture the project's saved state as a Baseline. Use it when you want to monitor the capture through the job queue.
entries.helpPage:
# Queue a Baseline Refresh

`baseline-refresh` queues durable work to capture the project's saved state as a new Baseline. The job continues after this command exits.

## When to use it

Use this when you want the Baseline capture to run through the job queue and inspect its status later. For an immediate capture, use `baseline capture` instead.

## Example

```powershell
motif baseline-refresh --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

## What it prints

The command prints the job id when work is queued. Use that id to check whether the Baseline capture completed.

## Related commands

- [Inspect a job](cmd:jobs%20show) reads its current state.
- [Capture a Baseline](cmd:baseline%20capture) performs the synchronous capture.

entries.title: Compare two Assessments
entries.description: Joins two stored Assessments on their shared words and stores the Difference as a new Assessment. It lets you inspect changes without treating the result as a verdict.
entries.helpPage:
# Compare two Assessments

`compare` joins the words shared by two stored Assessments and stores the measured Difference as a new Assessment. It describes measured differences without deciding which run is better.

## When to use it

Use this after two runs when you want to inspect changed results on words present in both Assessments. Choose Assessments from the same Assessor and kind so the measured values have the same meaning; only shared words are compared.

## Example

```powershell
motif compare --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --from <assessmentId> --to <assessmentId> --json
```

## What it prints

Human output shows the new Difference Assessment id and its summary. JSON includes that id, both source Assessment ids, word counts, the Assessor, any tokeniser warning, and the rendered summary text. The command reads stored evidence rather than rerunning either Assessment.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records another Assessment.
- [Read an Assessment report](cmd:report) asks a focused question of one Assessment.

entries.title: Compose steps in a Draft
entries.description: Stages one or more composing steps in a Draft in one call, each a composing command's name and closed intent, and can first remove earlier operations. A later step sees the earlier ones, and if any step or removal is refused, nothing changes. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Compose steps in a Draft

Stages one or more composing steps in a Draft in one call, through the same checks as each composing command alone, and can first remove earlier operations from it. If any step is refused, or a removal is, nothing is added or removed. Only a person can Apply.

Composing operations does not set the Draft's review text. Before Finalize, add both a short label with `motif label` and a comment with `motif comment`.

Each step names a composing command and carries the same closed intent that command's `--intent` takes. A step may add a `cite` object, which Motif records as operation provenance without changing the intent or its digest.

One step:

```sh
motif compose --project grammar.fwdata --proposal plurals \
  --steps '[{"verb": "compose-author-phoneme", "intent": {"name": "i", "representations": ["i"]}}]'
```

Many steps in order:

```sh
motif compose --project grammar.fwdata --proposal sounds --steps '[
  {"verb": "compose-author-phoneme", "intent": {"name": "i", "representations": ["i"]},
   "cite": {"source": "Grammar 2026", "locator": "§ 3"}},
  {"verb": "compose-author-phoneme", "intent": {"name": "u", "representations": ["u"]}}
]'
```

Steps run in order and each one sees the changes of the steps before it. A step may add an `as` label, and a later step may write `@label` as a whole value in its intent in place of an ID the labelled step created (a rule may use it in `placement.after` or `placement.before`). A rule step resolves `@label` only there. `@label:kind` chooses among several created objects of different kinds, and a reference that matches none or more than one is refused with the objects the step did create; `compose-batch` describes the forms. Labels match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,20}` and are unique within the call.

`--remove` takes operation ids, separated by commas, to take out of the Draft before the steps run, which is how a step replaces something it staged earlier:

```sh
motif compose --project grammar.fwdata --proposal sounds --remove <operation id>,<operation id> \
  --steps '[{"verb": "compose-author-phoneme", "intent": {"name": "e", "representations": ["e"]}}]'
```

A removal that would leave another operation depending on it is refused; remove those operations too, or use `remove-operations` with `--force`. A refusal names the failing step's position and command.

The result lists each step's operations and the Draft's operation count afterwards. Add `--json` for the structured result.

The MCP tool is `motif_compose`, with `proposal`, `steps` and `remove` arguments; it requires Advanced AI mode and a profile that selects it. `compose` names its Draft with `--proposal`, because that argument names a Draft or a Proposal; `compose-batch` takes the same steps from a file and does not remove.

entries.title: Add an example to a sense
entries.description: Adds one new example sentence to a sense, with its text in one or more writing systems and optional translations; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply. It refuses an unknown sense, a writing system the project does not have, empty or repeated text, and a neighbour that is not an example of the sense.
entries.helpPage:
# Add an example to a sense

Add one new example sentence to a sense, with its text in one or more writing systems and optional translations. To bring an example over from another sense, use `compose-move-example`.

```sh
motif compose-add-example --project language.fwdata --draft ceb-d005 --intent '{
  "sense":"<sense-id>",
  "text":[{"ws":"<vernacular-tag>","text":"..."}],
  "translations":[{"type":"free","text":[{"ws":"<analysis-tag>","text":"..."}]}]
}'
```

`sense` and `text` are required and the intent is closed. `text` and each translation's `text` are lists of `{ws, text}` objects with one entry per writing system and no empty text. Every `ws` must be a vernacular or analysis writing system of the project. `reference` is an optional reference string. A translation's `type` is `free` (the default), `literal` or `back`. `after` or `before`, never both, name an example of the sense to place the new one next to; without either it goes last.

The new example and each translation get fresh identities when the Draft is composed.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when:

- the sense does not exist or the id names another kind of object;
- a writing system is not one of the project's, or one is given twice in the same text, or a text is empty;
- `after` or `before` is not an example of the sense.

The sense may be created by an earlier step of the same Draft. The Dry Run lists the sense's examples before and after, and shows the whole new example in every writing system with its translations, and the sense with its entry and gloss.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Add exception features to many entries
entries.description: Adds the same exception features to many entries in one Draft, keeping what each already has and removing nothing. Use it to restrict an affix to a list of entries. A derivational affix takes From Exception Features, or To Exception Features with side to. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Add exception features to many entries

Use this command to tag many stems with the same exception features, or to add the features an inflectional or derivational affix requires, in one call. It adds to what each entry already has and removes nothing; `compose-edit-exception-features` replaces a whole set for one entry instead.

```sh
motif compose-add-exception-features --project language.fwdata --draft tag-stems \
  --intent '{"msas":["<stem-grammatical-info-id>","<another-stem-grammatical-info-id>"],"exceptionFeatures":["<feature-id>"]}'
```

`msas` lists the ids of the grammatical info of existing entries: a stem or clitic carries the features, and an inflectional affix requires them of its stem, as for `compose-edit-exception-features`. `exceptionFeatures` lists features that are already in the project's Exception Features list; add one with `compose-author-exception-feature`. Both lists are required, must not be empty, and must not repeat an id. A feature an entry already has is left alone, so the command can be repeated. An unclassified affix has no exception features.

A derivational affix takes its From Exception Features, which a stem must carry for the affix to attach, by default. Add `"side":"to"` to add To Exception Features instead, which the derived stem receives; `side` is refused for a stem or an inflectional affix. The same ids work for an affix process (reduplication, for instance) because the features sit on its grammatical info, not on the form. `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` replaces the exact sets.

To restrict an affix to a list of stems, tag the stems with this command and make the affix require the feature (`compose-edit-exception-features` for an inflectional affix, `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` for a derivational one). One call replaces one intent per stem. Use a feature for a lexical class with a reason; a feature per stem is only a stem list.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite the operations. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on stems that should and should not take the affix, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Add a grammatical analysis
entries.description: Stages one more grammatical info on an entry that already has one, as FieldWorks holds it: an entry owns any number of analyses, each sense points at one, and the parser loads every analysis of the entry as its own rule or stem. One suffix entry can then serve two categories. A derivational analysis can name its one From inflection class, so an entry with one analysis per class attaches to several classes. The new analysis can take existing senses of the entry, a new sense with a gloss, or neither. It refuses a stem analysis on an affix, an affix analysis on a stem, and a sense that belongs to another entry. Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Add a grammatical analysis

Use this command when one existing form should work in two grammatical roles, such as a Verb suffix that must also attach to Copula stems. FieldWorks holds this as one entry with two grammatical infos (morphosyntactic analyses), and each sense points at one of them. The parser loads every analysis of an entry as its own rule, so the same form parses on both categories, and the glosses of the two senses tell the analyses apart.

```sh
motif compose-add-morphosyntax-analysis --project language.fwdata --draft copula-suffix \
  --intent '{"entry":"<suffix-entry-id>","msa":{"kind":"inflectional","category":"<copula-id>","slots":["<copula-slot-id>"]},"gloss":"not (copula)","analysisWs":"en"}'
```

`entry` is an existing entry, or one an earlier command added to the same Draft. `msa` has the same shape as in `compose-author-lexical-entry`: its `kind` must suit the entry's form (`stem` for a stem, `inflectional`, `derivational` or `unclassified` for an affix), `category` is the part of speech, a derivational analysis also needs `toCategory`, an inflectional one can name `slots`, and a stem can name an `inflectionClass` and `exceptionFeatures`, a list of existing exception features the analysis carries.

The new analysis is used by the senses you name. `senses` lists senses of this entry that should now point at it, and `gloss` with `analysisWs` (and an optional `definition`) adds a new sense that points at it. Give at least one of them: an analysis no sense uses is removed by FieldWorks the next time the project is checked or opened, so a call that gives neither is refused. Moving the last sense off an analysis drops that analysis, and the Dry Run says so, naming any slots the old analysis fills (they lose that membership); if an ad hoc prohibition or a morph bundle still refers to that analysis the command refuses instead, naming what refers to it. Then either leave one sense on the old analysis, or remove that prohibition first. An analysis identical to one the entry already has (same category, classes, slots, feature requirements and exception features) is refused.

A derivational affix is restricted to one inflection class per analysis. Give it as `fromInflectionClass`, a class of its From category or an ancestor, at the top level of the intent beside `entry` and `gloss`, not inside `msa` (inside `msa` the command refuses it with "unknown property 'fromInflectionClass'"). It applies only to a derivational analysis. This adds a class 2 analysis to an affix entry that already has a derivational analysis for class 1:

```sh
motif compose-add-morphosyntax-analysis --project language.fwdata --draft class-two \
  --intent '{"entry":"<affix-entry-id>","msa":{"kind":"derivational","category":"<verb-id>","toCategory":"<noun-id>"},"gloss":"agentive (class 2)","analysisWs":"en","fromInflectionClass":"<class-2-id>"}'
```

The Dry Run shows a `grammar/moDerivAffMsa/setFromInflectionClass` operation for the new analysis. Checked with the real parser: with the first analysis restricted to class 1 and this one to class 2, the affix parses stems of both classes and no stem of a third class. To let it attach to several classes, give the entry one derivational analysis per class: the parser loads each analysis as its own rule, so the classes add up, and a stem of any other class is not accepted. A class whose subclasses should all qualify can instead be the From class itself, because the parser includes a class's subclasses. Restrict the first analysis with `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction`.

The inflection classes already set on the entry's affix form apply to every inflectional analysis of the entry, whatever its category; if the new category has its own classes, check the form with `compose-edit-affix-inflection-classes`.

Dry Run and Trial the Draft on words in both roles and on words that should not gain an analysis, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

A derivational affix's composed summary lists a `Derivation: From -> To` line naming both categories, so a swapped pair shows at once, and its Dry Run warns when the project has no stem, subcategory stem or derivation that makes the From category, or when nothing takes the To category (or a subcategory) as input, which usually means the categories are the wrong way round.

## When not to use this

- To turn the one analysis an affix has into another affix kind, use `compose-change-affix-kind`.
- For an entry that does not exist yet, use `compose-author-lexical-entry`.
- For two separate entries with different forms, one per category, use two entries in their slots (the [suffix and prefix slots guide](guide:encoding/suffix-prefix-slots)).

An entry may hold two analyses with the same category, classes and slots when they differ by feature requirements or, on a stem, by exception features. The command refuses a new analysis only when an existing one is identical, feature requirements and exception features included. To give one morpheme two analyses that differ only by features (a relative marker that requires one group in one analysis and another in the second), first give the existing analysis its requirement with [Author a feature structure](cmd:compose-author-feature-structure) and a feature value, then add the second analysis and give it its own.

## A stem that two obligatory rules both want

When two phonological rules each require their own exception feature and one bleeds the other (syncope removes the vowel that the second rule's environment needs), a stem tagged for both takes only the outcome of the earlier rule. To let a stem surface both ways, give it two analyses, one tagged for each rule. Tag the existing analysis with `compose-edit-exception-features`, then add the second analysis with its own tag in the same Draft:

```sh
motif compose-add-morphosyntax-analysis --project language.fwdata --draft split-stem \
  --intent '{"entry":"<stem-entry-id>","msa":{"kind":"stem","category":"<verb-id>","exceptionFeatures":["<rhotacism-feature-id>"]},"gloss":"<gloss of the second reading>","analysisWs":"en"}'
```

The original sense stays on the original analysis and `gloss` adds a second sense for the new one, so an entry with one sense ends with two. Give the second sense a real gloss, because it lands in FieldWorks. Do not move the only sense to the new analysis with `senses`: the old analysis then loses its last sense and is dropped, and the split becomes a retag.

Each analysis is its own stem to the parser, so neither rule fires on the other's outcome. Checked with the real parser on a stem with a syncope rule before a d-to-r rule: with both tags on one analysis only the syncope form parsed, and after the split both forms parsed. See the [workflow guide](guide:encoding/workflow).

entries.title: Add a phonological feature value
entries.description: Stages one more value for an existing closed phonological feature. The feature must belong to the phonological feature system, and the value name and abbreviation must be new to it. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Add a phonological feature value

Stages one more value for a closed phonological feature that exists, such as `velar` for `place`. Use the closed input `{ "feature": "<canonical ID>", "name": "velar", "abbreviation": "vel" }`; `abbreviation` is optional. The feature must belong to the phonological feature system, not the morphosyntactic one. A value name or abbreviation the feature already has is refused. Only a person can Apply.

To create the feature in the first place use [Author a phonological feature](cmd:compose-author-phonological-feature). Phonemes and natural classes take the new value through [Set a phoneme's features](cmd:compose-edit-phoneme-features) and [Edit a natural class's features](cmd:compose-edit-natural-class-features).

The feature may have been created earlier in this Draft. In one [batch](cmd:compose-batch), use `"feature": "@identity"`; a later feature specification can use this add-value entry's own `as` label for its one created value. Across calls, use `"feature": "lookup:phonological-feature:identity"`, and bind the new value with `lookup:phonological-feature-value:identity|slash`. A name or abbreviation that matches several objects is refused.

entries.title: Add a Source
entries.description: Stages a new Source in the project's Motif Sources list, which the first one creates. Nothing is written until a person applies the pending changes.
entries.helpPage:
# Add a Source

Stage a new Source in the project's Motif Sources list. The first one creates the list. The intent gives the id, name, versification, Context and kind; nothing is written until a person applies the pending changes.

```sh
motif compose-add-source --project language.fwdata --draft pending --intent '{"id":"WEB","name":"World English Bible","versification":"English","context":"MAT-JHN","kind":"Paratext"}'
```

The command refuses an id that is empty, has spaces, is in use or was removed (a removed Source is restored, never re-added), a versification Motif does not know, and a Context that does not read in it. To stage a Source and apply it in one step use `motif source add --apply`.

entries.title: Create an ad hoc prohibition
entries.description: Creates a morpheme or allomorph co-occurrence prohibition, FieldWorks' ad hoc rule, naming a first morpheme or allomorph and the ones it cannot occur with. The Dry Run says plainly what is prohibited next to what; duplicates and unknown morphemes or allomorphs are refused, and only a person can Apply the Draft.
entries.helpPage:
# Create an ad hoc prohibition

Create a morpheme or allomorph co-occurrence prohibition, which FieldWorks calls an ad hoc rule. A morpheme prohibition names a first morpheme and the morphemes it cannot occur with; an allomorph prohibition does the same for forms. The parser then drops any analysis that contains the prohibited combination.

```sh
motif compose-author-adhoc-prohibition --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"kind":"morpheme","first":"<msa-id>","rest":["<msa-id>"],"adjacency":"anywhere"}'
```

A morpheme is a grammatical analysis (MSA) of an entry; an allomorph is a lexeme form or alternate form. Both may be created earlier in the same Draft. `adjacency` defaults to `anywhere`, as in FieldWorks; the other values are `somewhere-to-right`, `somewhere-to-left`, `adjacent-to-right` and `adjacent-to-left`. The prohibition is created enabled.

## One prohibition over a set of alternatives

FieldWorks holds the rest as a sequence that must all be present, so a single prohibition cannot ban "any of these". To ban the first from every member of a set, give `restAnyOf` instead of `rest`:

```sh
motif compose-author-adhoc-prohibition --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"kind":"morpheme","first":"<msa-id>","restAnyOf":["<msa-id>","<msa-id>"]}'
```

The command stages one prohibition per member, all in the same Proposal, and the Dry Run states each in full. A member that duplicates an existing prohibition, or equals the first, is refused and nothing is staged. Give `rest` or `restAnyOf`, not both.

## Which side is the first on

The adjacency says where the **first** sits relative to the **rest**, read as the sentence "the first cannot occur ___ the rest". `somewhere-to-right` and `adjacent-to-right` mean the first is on the right of the rest, that is, later in the word; `somewhere-to-left` and `adjacent-to-left` mean the first is on the left, earlier in the word. It is easy to read this the other way round for a prefix.

- A prefix as the first, a stem as the rest: the stem is to the prefix's right, so the first is on the left of the rest. Use `anywhere`, `somewhere-to-left` or `adjacent-to-left`. With `somewhere-to-right` or `adjacent-to-right` the rule can never match.
- A suffix as the first, a stem as the rest: the stem is to the suffix's left, so the first is on the right of the rest. Use `anywhere`, `somewhere-to-right` or `adjacent-to-right`. With a left adjacency the rule can never match.
- With several in the rest, they are read left to right.

The Dry Run states the rule as a full sentence, for example "morpheme 'pa-' cannot occur in the same word as bago", or "allomorph 'pa-' cannot occur immediately to the left of bago (the first comes before the rest in the word)", so a reversed direction shows at review. When the first is a prefix and the adjacency points to its right (or a suffix and a left adjacency) and every one of the rest is a stem or the opposite kind of affix, the Dry Run adds a `warning` that the rule can never match and names the adjacency to use; the rule is still staged. The command refuses an unknown morpheme or allomorph, an empty rest, and a prohibition that already exists in the project or earlier in the Draft. It also refuses a first morpheme or allomorph that appears in the rest, because the parser would ban it from every word or ignore the rule. Review the Dry Run and compare Trials before a person Applies the Proposal; the CLI verb always stages a Draft, MCP offers `motif_author_adhoc_prohibition` in the default tool list, and MCP cannot Apply it.

## Two entries with the same spelling

A morpheme prohibition names one entry's grammatical analysis, not a spelling, so it can stop one of two homograph stems taking an affix while the other still does. Give the affix's analysis as `first` and the unwanted stem's analysis as `rest`, with `adjacent-to-left` for a prefix or `adjacent-to-right` for a suffix; use `restAnyOf` for several such stems. Read the analysis ids from the lexicon, because two stems with the same form have different ones. A category cannot tell them apart when both are in the same category. An exception feature on the affix (`compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction`) admits only the stems that carry it and cannot exclude one stem, so use it when the few stems that take the affix are the ones to mark, and this prohibition when the few to refuse are.

## Stems that share a class with the hosts

The same prohibition keeps a derivational prefix, already restricted to a host inflection class with `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction`, off one stem of that class (the real parser stopped it on the named stem and kept it on the other); the From side of a derivational affix cannot exclude a stem, so this is the route.

The real parser has been tested with this prohibition for a plain prefix and for a reduplicating prefix process (copy the first consonant and vowel in front of the stem, as Cebuano `magR` and `umR` do): with two homograph stems, the rule removed the reading through the named stem and kept the other. A derivational suffix can be named too. When a word is both a stored stem and a stem plus a derivational suffix, the prohibition on the stored stem leaves the derived reading; add a second prohibition with the same `first` and `rest` = [the verb stem's analysis, the suffix's derivational analysis]. In the test in this repository (a prefix as `first`, `adjacent-to-left`) the second prohibition left no reading; a suffix as `first` was not tested this way. Other process shapes, such as infixes, have not been tested.

## When not to use this

- A slot, template, required feature or environment usually expresses the restriction better ([guide](guide:encoding/suffix-prefix-slots)).
- If the evidence does not say the combination is impossible, ask the linguist ([guide](guide:encoding/ask-the-linguist)).
- To turn an existing prohibition off or on, use `compose-edit-adhoc-prohibition`.

entries.title: Author an affix process
entries.description: Stages a new affix entry whose ordered input pattern matches phonemes, a natural class or the remaining stem, and whose output copies named parts, inserts phonemes, inserts a segment of a natural class, or copies a part with the features of a feature class laid over it: an infix, a partial or full reduplication, or a substitution that deletes matched input by omitting it from the output (Cebuano paN- before p/b gives m). It refuses an output that copies nothing or drops the remaining stem. Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Author an affix process

Use this command to stage one new affix whose form is described by a pattern and a realization. An input part names one phoneme, one natural class, or the remaining stem; output items copy named input parts, insert saved or previously staged phonemes, insert one segment of a natural class, or copy an input part with the features of a feature class laid over it.

This example copies a whole stem twice with an existing phoneme between the copies:

```sh
motif compose-author-affix-process --project language.fwdata --draft reduplication \
  --intent '{"morphType":"<prefix-or-suffix-id>","gloss":"repeated action","analysisWs":"en","msa":{"kind":"unclassified","category":"<verb-category-id>"},"input":[{"name":"stem","remaining":true}],"output":[{"copy":"stem"},{"insert":["<phoneme-id>"]},{"copy":"stem"}]}'
```

The intent has `morphType`, `gloss`, `analysisWs`, optional `definition`, optional `form` with its vernacular writing system `formWs` (the entry's headword, written without the hyphens FieldWorks shows on affixes, so the entry can be found in the lexicon; give both or neither), affix-only `msa`, `input` and `output`. The MSA kind is `inflectional`, `derivational` or `unclassified`; its category, optional target category and slots must match that kind and the morph type. References may name saved project objects or objects created earlier in the same Draft or batch; Motif resolves staged references while replaying the Draft.

Each input part has a distinct `name` and exactly one of `phoneme`, `naturalClass` or `remaining: true`. There may be at most one remaining-stem part, and it must be last unless it is the only part. An output may omit an input part, which deletes what it matched (for example the initial consonant in nasal substitution, where `p` becomes `m`: input `p` and `rest`, output insert `pa`, insert `m`, copy `rest`); omitting a part is how a process deletes. The remaining-stem part must still be copied, and at least one input must be copied, so a process cannot delete the whole stem. Each output item has exactly one of `copy`, `insert`, `insertClass`, or `modify` with `features`; inserted phoneme arrays are nonempty. `insertClass` names a natural class (by segments or by features, FieldWorks' insert natural class) and puts one segment of that class into the word; give it a class that picks out one sound unless you mean to leave the choice to the parser. A class of several segments does leave the choice of member to the parser: either member is read as the inserted segment, so a word that shows either one parses. `modify` names an input part (a phoneme, a natural class or the remaining stem), which is copied with the phonological feature values of `features` replacing its own (FieldWorks' modify from input, for example voicing the first consonant: input a voiceless class and `rest`, output `modify` it with a class holding the feature value voiced, then copy `rest`); `features` must be a natural class defined by features, not by segments. On the remaining stem, as in FieldWorks where every copy including the variable part can be a modify, every segment the stem captured takes the features (for example devoicing every voiced consonant), and a segment with no sound of the inventory that has the changed features does not parse. The part that results must be a sound in the phoneme inventory with those features, so give the inventory the voiced counterpart. A modification and an inserted class each count as changing the word, so a process that does only that is not identity-only. The realization must insert material, omit an input part, or copy one more than once, so an identity-only pattern is refused. A process with exactly one input part and one output item is held and allowed, but FieldWorks and PanGloss skip it when they load the grammar, so it will not parse; the Dry Run warns, and the fix is another part (for example a modified stem plus an inserted affix segment).

The limits are 1–16 input parts, 1–64 logical output items, 1–64 phonemes per insertion and 256 expanded output mappings. Nested contexts, truncation, replacing or deleting an existing process are not supported.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces. The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on affected words, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

A derivational affix's composed summary lists a `Derivation: From -> To` line naming both categories, so a swapped pair shows at once, and its Dry Run warns when the project has no stem, subcategory stem or derivation that makes the From category, or when nothing takes the To category (or a subcategory) as input, which usually means the categories are the wrong way round.

## When not to use this

- For nasal assimilation or substitution, use a phonological rule with `compose-author-phonological-rule`; an unconstrained affix process may require substantial parser work, while Verb-restricted processes merged on one entry stopped no words with compounding off.
- For a form that changes with its sound context, keep allomorphs under one entry with environments, using `compose-author-alternate-form`.
- For another pattern-based form of an affix that already uses a process, use `compose-author-affix-process-allomorph`.
- For a plain prefix or suffix, use `compose-author-lexical-entry` and a slot.

entries.title: Add an affix process allomorph
entries.description: Stages one more pattern-based form, an affix process with its own input pattern and output, on an existing affix entry whose forms may be plain allomorphs or processes. The lexeme form's morph type is copied and the form applies to all of the entry's grammatical info. It refuses a stem, a repeated pattern and a missing placement.
entries.helpPage:
# Add an affix process allomorph

Use this command to give an affix entry another pattern-based form, whether its lexeme form is a plain affix allomorph or an affix process, the way Lexicon Edit > Insert Allomorph > Affix Process does in FieldWorks. One call stages the new allomorph on an entry that exists, or that an earlier command added to the same Draft. Its `input` and `output` mean what they mean for `compose-author-affix-process`, including `insertClass` and `modify` with `features`.

This example adds a form of an existing nasal-substitution prefix that turns a stem-initial `t`, `d` or `s` into `n`:

```sh
motif compose-author-affix-process-allomorph --project language.fwdata --draft prefix-forms \
  --intent '{"entry":"<entry-id>","input":[{"name":"first","naturalClass":"<t-d-s-class-id>"},{"name":"rest","remaining":true}],"output":[{"insert":["<p-id>","<a-id>","<n-id>"]},{"copy":"rest"}],"placement":{"after":"<earlier-form-id>"}}'
```

The intent has `entry`, `input`, `output`, optional `inflectionClasses` and optional `placement`. There is no gloss, grammatical info, slot or morph type: the form copies the entry's morph type and applies to every grammatical info the entry has, so a change meant for one meaning of a multi-meaning affix needs a different entry. To give the form its own tense, gloss or slot, make it its own entry, because an allomorph cannot carry a label of its own ([what an allomorph can carry](guide:encoding/conditioned-allomorphs)). `input` and `output` follow the same rules and limits as an affix process: at most one remaining-stem part, last; at least one input copied; and a realization that inserts, omits or repeats something. There are no environments, because an affix process carries none.

The entry must be an affix. Its lexeme form may be a plain affix allomorph or an affix process (as `compose-author-affix-process` creates), and its other forms may be plain allomorphs or processes in any order, as FieldWorks allows. A stem, an entry with no lexeme form, an entry without affix grammatical info, a missing or non-adjacent placement, and a pattern and output the entry already has are refused, naming the entry. The new process takes the lexeme form's morph type. Order matters across the mix: an earlier form that matches blocks later ones, and the lexeme form is always last, so a plain elsewhere form belongs in the lexeme form with the processes ahead of it.

Alternate forms have declared precedence. When the entry already has alternate forms, `placement` is required and names the neighbours of the insertion gap, as `{"after":"<form-id>"}`, `{"before":"<form-id>"}` or both, and they must be adjacent now. The first alternate form takes no placement. `inflectionClasses` lists existing classes for an inflectional grammatical info the entry has, owned by that info's category or a category above it; the form then attaches only to stems of those classes for that inflectional analysis. FieldWorks ignores these form classes for a derivational analysis; use `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` to restrict that analysis instead. If the entry has no inflectional grammatical info, Motif refuses `inflectionClasses` and names that composer.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces. The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on affected words, including words just outside each pattern, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

## When not to use this

- For a spelling variant, or a form conditioned by an environment, use `compose-author-alternate-form`.
- For a new morpheme, create a new entry with `compose-author-affix-process` or `compose-author-lexical-entry`.
- For a regular sound change across many forms, use a phonological rule with `compose-author-phonological-rule`.

entries.title: Author an affix slot
entries.description: Stages a named inflectional affix slot owned by an existing category and can assign existing inflectional affixes to it in the same Draft. Inspect its Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Author an affix slot

Use this command when the existing inflectional slots do not express the intended grammar. It creates a named slot on an existing category and can assign existing inflectional affix MSAs to it in the same Draft.

```sh
motif compose-author-affix-slot --project language.fwdata --draft new-slot \
  --intent '{"category":"<category-id>","name":"person number","ws":"en","optional":false,"assignments":["<msa-id>"]}'
```

`category` names the existing category that owns the slot. `name` and `ws` identify its localized name, and `optional` says whether forms may omit the slot. `assignments` is an optional list of existing inflectional affix MSA ids. Each MSA's category must be the slot's category or a descendant of it.

The command stages a category-owned create, a name, an Optional value, and any requested MSA assignments. The create operation is declared as a dependency of those writes, so Draft order does not control execution. Finish the Proposal, inspect its Dry Run, then run a bounded Trial on affected words before a person Applies it.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Author an affix template
entries.description: Stages an active alternative template on an existing category, using ordered prefix and suffix slots that belong to the category or an ancestor. It preserves existing template order and records whether this template requires further derivation. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author an affix template

Use this command when two branches of a category need different required slots. It adds an active alternative template without changing the category's existing templates or their order.

```sh
motif compose-author-affix-template --project language.fwdata --draft plural-branch \
  --intent '{"category":"<category-id>","name":"plural branch","ws":"en","prefixSlots":["<prefix-slot-id>"],"suffixSlots":["<suffix-slot-id>"],"final":false}'
```

`category` names the existing category that owns the new template. `name` and `ws` give the localized name. `prefixSlots` and `suffixSlots` are ordered lists of existing slot ids from the project; each slot must belong to the template category or one of its ancestors. A slot may appear only once across both lists. The template is appended to the category's ordered template sequence.

`final` sets the template's Final value, which records whether the template requires further derivation. The template is active by default.

The Draft declares that the template create precedes its name, Final value and slot references. Finish the Proposal, inspect its Dry Run, and run a bounded Trial on affected words before a person Applies it.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Add Required Features
entries.description: Stages Required Features on an ordinary affix allomorph in a Draft. Populate the returned structure with feature values to select the form by the stem's grammatical features, including on derivational affixes. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Add Required Features

Stages an empty Required Features structure on one ordinary affix allomorph in a Draft. FieldWorks shows this as **Required Features**, on the lexeme form or an alternate form. The closed input is `{ "allomorph": "<form ID>" }`; the form may already exist or have been staged earlier in the Draft. Only a person can Apply.

Use the returned structure ID with [Author feature value](cmd:compose-author-feature-value), supplying `featStruc`, a morphosyntactic `feature` and its `value`. Required Features select this allomorph by the grammatical features of the stem it attaches to. They work on allomorphs of derivational affixes too: two prefix forms requiring transitive and intransitive respectively select matching stems and reject stems bearing the other value (`RealParserAllomorphGateTests`). A stem without a value is compatible with a requirement; use explicit stem values when testing the contrast.

This command preserves an occupied structure, even if it is empty, and refuses to replace it. It accepts ordinary affix allomorphs; a stem form or an affix process is a different LibLCM class. It imposes no restriction on the entry's grammatical info kind. Required Features are distinct from the whole affix's [grammatical features](cmd:compose-author-feature-structure) and from [inflection classes on an affix form](cmd:compose-edit-affix-inflection-classes).

Run a Trial with expected and excluded combinations before Finalize. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite the source on the staged operation.

entries.title: Author an alternate form
entries.description: Stages one more stem or affix form on an existing or earlier-staged entry, with its own environments and, when the entry has inflectional grammatical info, inflection classes. Use compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction for a derivational analysis. It adds no entry, sense or grammatical info and copies no condition from the lexeme form.
entries.helpPage:
# Author an alternate form

Use this command to give an entry another form, such as a prefix that changes before a vowel. One call stages the form on an entry that already exists, or that an earlier command added to the same Draft, and links the conditions you name. It adds no entry, sense or grammatical info and leaves the lexeme form and every other form as they are.

```sh
motif compose-author-alternate-form --project language.fwdata --draft new-words \
  --intent '{"entry":"<entry-id>","form":"mw","formWs":"sw","morphType":"<prefix-morph-type-id>","environments":["<before-vowel-id>"],"inflectionClasses":["<class-1-2-id>"]}'
```

`form` is written in the vernacular writing system `formWs`, exactly as typed: Motif stores the form as given and neither adds nor strips hyphens. `morphType` is the id of an existing morph type and must suit the entry: a stem or root type for a stem entry, an affix type for an affix entry. An affix entry whose lexeme form or other alternates are affix processes takes a plain affix form too; plain and process forms mix in one order.

Each form states its own conditions, and none are copied. `environments` lists existing phonological environments the form occurs in. `inflectionClasses` lists existing classes for an inflectional grammatical info the entry has, owned by that info's category or a category above it; the form then attaches only to stems of those classes for that inflectional analysis. FieldWorks ignores these form classes for a derivational analysis; use `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` to set its From Inflection Class and From Exception Features. If the entry has no inflectional grammatical info, Motif refuses `inflectionClasses` and names that composer. Leave either field out for no condition. Empty lists and repeated ids are refused, and so is an environment whose pattern names a natural class that does not exist: write the class's abbreviation, such as `[V]`, not its name.

Alternate forms have declared precedence: an eligible earlier form can block a later one. `placement` names the neighbours of the insertion gap, as `{"after":"<form-id>"}`, `{"before":"<form-id>"}` or both. Adjacent means the two are next to each other now. Leave it out and Motif chooses the gap: a form with environments goes just before the entry's first form without environments, and any other form goes after the last alternate form. A form with no environment always wins over every later form, so an explicit placement of a restricted form after an unrestricted one, or of an unrestricted form before a restricted one, is refused and the refusal names where to place it instead. In a `compose-batch` file a neighbour can be a label such as `@circ:suffix`. The lexeme form is always the last candidate.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

The command returns the new form's operations and created entity id. Dry Run and Trial the Draft on affected words, revise it, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

## Swapping the lexeme form with an alternate form

The lexeme form is always the last candidate and is never a placement neighbour, so no alternate form can be placed after it. To make an alternate the elsewhere form, or to swap the two, do it in two Drafts so each sees the other's result: first `compose-remove-alternate-form` on the alternate, and `compose-rewrite-lexeme-form` to give the lexeme form the alternate's text; then `compose-author-alternate-form` to add the old lexeme text as an alternate with its own `environments`, placed as the refusal text directs. An unrestricted alternate always sits ahead of the lexeme form, so it would hide a restricted lexeme form; that is why the composer refuses it and points here.

## When not to use this

- For a regular sound change across many forms, use `compose-author-phonological-rule` rather than listing a variant for each.
- Do not duplicate an unrestricted form for every stem; give each variant the narrowest environment that fits.

entries.title: Author a circumfix
entries.description: Stages a new circumfix entry as FieldWorks holds it: one entry whose prefix part and suffix part attach to a stem together, with one sense and one grammatical analysis. The parser pairs the two parts, so neither part alone attaches. Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal. In a compose-batch file its two parts are labelled @label:prefix and @label:suffix.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a circumfix

Use this command to stage one new circumfix: a single entry with a prefix part and a suffix part that attach to a stem together, as in Indonesian `ke-...-an`. FieldWorks holds it as one entry of the circumfix type whose lexeme form reads `ke- -an`, with a prefix form and a suffix form beside it. The parser pairs the two parts into one rule, so neither part alone attaches.

```sh
motif compose-author-circumfix --project language.fwdata --draft circumfix \
  --intent '{"prefix":"ke","suffix":"an","formWs":"id","gloss":"abstract noun","analysisWs":"en","msa":{"kind":"derivational","category":"<verb-category-id>","toCategory":"<noun-category-id>"}}'
```

The intent has `prefix` and `suffix`, written without hyphens, spaces or full stops (FieldWorks splits the lexeme form on a space or full stop), `formWs` for the writing system of both, `gloss`, `analysisWs`, optional `definition`, and `msa`. The MSA kind is `inflectional`, `derivational` or `unclassified`; a circumfix is an affix, so it is never a stem. `slots` belong to an inflectional circumfix, and `toCategory` to a derivational one. `prefixEnvironments` and `suffixEnvironments` each limit one part to existing environments; absent means any. `inflectionClasses` limits both parts to existing inflection classes of an inflectional or unclassified circumfix. References may name saved project objects or objects created earlier in the same Draft.

Each part of a circumfix keeps its own sound environment on PanGloss: the prefix part's environment is checked at the stem start and the suffix part's at the stem end (`RealParserCircumfixEnvironmentTests`). Separate circumfix entries with different suffix environments can choose a linker by the stem's last sound; see the [conditioned allomorphs guide](guide:encoding/conditioned-allomorphs). Run a Trial with the expected words, wrong linkers, missing halves and stems excluded by the prefix environment.

In a `compose-batch` file give the circumfix entry an `as` label. Its two parts have the distinct labels `@label:prefix` and `@label:suffix`, so a later `compose-author-alternate-form` can place a form `"placement":{"before":"@label:suffix"}` without copying an id from the output. `@label` alone is the entry, and `@label:msa` and `@label:senses` are as for any entry.

The command stages the entry, its lexeme form, the two parts, their conditions, the analysis and the sense in one Proposal. Dry Run and Trial it on words with and without the circumfix, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply. `compose-edit-morph-type` and `compose-edit-affix-inflection-classes` still refuse a circumfix, because a single form cannot be edited into or out of one.

A derivational affix's composed summary lists a `Derivation: From -> To` line naming both categories, so a swapped pair shows at once, and its Dry Run warns when the project has no stem, subcategory stem or derivation that makes the From category, or when nothing takes the To category (or a subcategory) as input, which usually means the categories are the wrong way round.

## When not to use this

- Two markers that can each occur without the other are two entries in two slots; use `compose-author-lexical-entry` and a template (the [suffix and prefix slots guide](guide:encoding/suffix-prefix-slots)).
- A one-sided affix is a plain prefix or suffix from `compose-author-lexical-entry`.
- For a marker that copies or changes the stem itself, use `compose-author-affix-process`.

entries.title: Author an environment
entries.description: Stages an environment with explicitly declared left and right contexts in a Draft. Contexts use project phonemes, natural classes or boundaries. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author an environment

Stages an environment with explicitly declared left and right contexts in a Draft. Contexts use project phonemes and natural classes, plus the word boundary `#` at the outer edge. An environment cannot hold a morpheme boundary or any other boundary marker, because the parser ignores such an environment and the form would be unconstrained. To condition a change on a morpheme boundary, use a phonological rule ([author a phonological rule](cmd:compose-author-phonological-rule)). Only a person can Apply.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Add an exception feature
entries.description: Stages a new exception feature in the project's Exception Features list, the tag that stems carry and affixes or rules can require. It refuses a name the list already has. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Add an exception feature

Use this command to add an exception feature to the project's Exception Features list. An exception feature is a tag with no meaning of its own: you tag the stems or clitics that belong to a lexical class, then tag the affixes that may attach only to that class. Black's FieldWorks parsing guide (section 2.1.6) uses it to stop an affix that is correct for some stems from also parsing every other stem, and to keep a handful of loan stems out of a sound change.
