```sh
motif compose-author-exception-feature --project language.fwdata --draft features \
  --intent '{"name":"Loan stem","ws":"en","abbreviation":"loan"}'
```

The intent has `name` and `ws`, and may have `abbreviation`. The name must be new in that writing system. Name the class by the fact it records, such as a stratum or a kin term, because the list is shared by every rule and affix.

The new feature does nothing until it is used. Tag stems with `compose-edit-exception-features`, require it on a derivational affix with `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction`, or require or exclude it in a rule with `compose-edit-phonological-rule-features`. Each of these can name the feature by the id this command returns, in the same Draft: the Draft composer declares the dependency from the reference, so one Proposal can create the feature and use it.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Author grammatical features
entries.description: Stages an empty feature structure on an existing or earlier-staged stem, inflectional affix or derivational affix MSA (side from or to) in a Draft, refusing an occupied slot even when its structure has no selections. Inflectional affix features are word requirements; use the returned exact structure identity to author selections. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author grammatical features

Stages an empty feature structure on a stem, inflectional affix or derivational affix MSA in a Draft. The MSA may already exist in the project or have been authored earlier in the same Draft. Only a person can Apply.

Use the closed input `{ "msa": "<canonical ID>" }` to name the exact MSA. A stem receives an MsFeatures structure; an inflectional affix receives an InflFeats structure for its word requirements. A derivational affix takes `"side"`, which is required for it and refused for any other MSA: `"from"` makes a FromMsFeatures structure, a requirement that is unified with the stem's features (a stem with a different value of that feature is refused; a stem with no value of it is accepted, and the required value is then imposed on the derived word), and `"to"` makes a ToMsFeatures structure, what the derived stem carries afterwards. A stem's MsFeatures is what a word reads out, and a derivational affix's ToMsFeatures changes it: put a noun's class there (for example nc7 on *kitabu*) so an affix that requires nc7 can match it and a mismatched one cannot. An inflectional affix's InflFeats only requires: it adds no feature to the word the way a stem's MsFeatures does, but the value it requires stays on the word, so two affixes agree when both require the same value of one feature (a subject marker and a relative marker, say), and a pair that disagrees has no analysis. To make two affixes agree, give both an InflFeats structure with one value of the same feature; an entry that serves two classes needs one grammatical info for each, because a feature holds one value. On the real parser, a subject and a relative slot are accepted with matching values and rejected with mismatched ones. For singular and plural nouns, put the gender pair (for example 7/8) on the stem and the number on each class prefix: every reading shows its prefix's number, but a number requirement never rejects a stem that has none. A value a derivational affix names in its ToMsFeatures replaces the stem's value of that feature, and a feature it does not name keeps the stem's value (tested with two features). So a stem tagged intransitive stays intransitive through a causative until the causative's ToMsFeatures says transitive, and then an affix that requires transitive applies to the causative and not to the bare stem. A derivational affix cannot remove a feature from the word, only give it another value. The real parser is tested on this (`RealParserDerivedStemFeatureTests`). Other MSA types and an occupied owning slot are refused. A present structure occupies the slot even when it has no selections.

Use the returned structure identity when [authoring a feature selection](cmd:compose-author-feature-value). An empty structure is valid, and a feature can be selected before choosing its value. Selections must fit the current domain of the named structure.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Author a feature value
entries.description: Stages a closed feature specification in an existing or earlier-staged structure, with value omitted when unchosen. Inflectional affix requirements use current morphosyntactic definitions, and any supplied value must belong to the exact feature. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a feature value

Stages a closed feature specification in an existing or earlier-staged feature structure, including a stem's MsFeatures or an inflectional affix's InflFeats. Inflectional affix selections are word requirements. Only a person can Apply.

Use the closed input `{ "featStruc": "<canonical ID>", "feature": "<canonical ID>" }`, adding `value` only when choosing a symbolic value. Each reference names an exact canonical identity; a supplied value must belong to that exact closed feature. Omit `value` to author a feature-only specification; null is refused. A second specification for the same feature is refused.

For InflFeats, the feature must currently belong to the project's morphosyntactic feature system and fit any declared structure type. The feature structure, feature and value may already exist or have been authored earlier in the same Draft. Use the structure identity returned by [authoring grammatical features](cmd:compose-author-feature-structure).

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Author inflection class
entries.description: Adds an inflection class or subclass, such as a noun class, to a Draft. Its owner is explicit and the category's default is unchanged; use the created id when authoring a stem.
entries.helpPage:
# Author an inflection class

Add a named inflection class, such as a noun class or conjugation, to a category. A class can be nested under an existing class in that same category.

```sh
motif compose-author-inflection-class --project language.fwdata --draft noun-classes \
  --intent '{"category":"<noun-id>","name":"Class Seven","ws":"en","abbreviation":"seven"}'
```

`category` is the existing part-of-speech id. Optional `parent` names an existing inflection class whose owning category must match it. `name` must be new within that category's class tree in `ws`; the writing system must be known. An optional `abbreviation` supplies a short label.

The command preserves the category's default inflection class. Use the create operation's `entityId` as `msa.inflectionClass` when authoring a stem. References may name something an earlier call added to the same Draft.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

Dry Run and Trial the Draft on affected words, revise it, then Finalize for a person to review and Apply.

## When not to use this

- Use a class only for arbitrary lexical grouping; a value that must agree with an affix is a feature ([guide](guide:encoding/feature-conditioned-slots)).
- For a sound-conditioned form, use an environment rather than a class.

entries.title: Author inflection feature
entries.description: Adds a closed morphosyntactic feature and its named values to a Draft. Use the created ids in feature-structure and stem-name authoring, then Dry Run and Trial the Draft before Finalize.
entries.helpPage:
# Author an inflection feature

Add a closed morphosyntactic feature and the values it can take, such as Number with Singular and Plural. One call stages the feature and all its named values in the project's morphosyntactic feature system.

```sh
motif compose-author-inflection-feature --project language.fwdata --draft number \
  --intent '{"name":"Number","ws":"en","abbreviation":"num","values":[{"name":"Singular","abbreviation":"sg"},{"name":"Plural","abbreviation":"pl"}]}'
```

`values` must contain at least one object with a `name` and an optional `abbreviation`. Value names must be distinct after Unicode normalization, and the feature name must be new in that writing system. The writing system must be known to the project.

The result names every created entity. The `createFeatures` operation supplies the feature id; each `createValues` operation supplies a value id. Existing feature-structure and feature-value composers attach these choices to a stem's grammatical info. This command makes no category or entry assignments.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

Dry Run and Trial the Draft on affected words, revise it, then Finalize for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Author a lexeme form
entries.description: Stages a lexeme form with explicitly authored spelling, writing system and morph type in a Draft. Dry Run and Trial the Draft before Finalize; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a lexeme form

Stages a lexeme form with explicitly authored spelling, writing system and morph type in a Draft. Dry Run and Trial the Draft before Finalize; only a person can Apply.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Author a lexical entry
entries.description: Stages one new dictionary entry with its lexeme form, one sense with gloss and optional definition, and grammatical info: a stem, or an inflectional, derivational or unclassified affix. An inflectional affix can name the inflection classes its form attaches to; use compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction for a derivational affix. Inspect its Dry Run and try words with it before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a dictionary entry

Use this command to add a stem or an affix the project does not have yet. One call stages a complete entry: its lexeme form, one sense with a gloss and an optional definition, and the grammatical info the parser needs to use it.

```sh
motif compose-author-lexical-entry --project language.fwdata --draft new-words \
  --intent '{"form":"kitabu","formWs":"sw","morphType":"<stem-morph-type-id>","gloss":"book","analysisWs":"en","definition":"a bound set of written pages","msa":{"kind":"stem","category":"<noun-id>","inflectionClass":"<class-7-8-id>"}}'
```

`form` is the lexeme form in the vernacular writing system `formWs`, without the hyphens FieldWorks shows on affixes. `morphType` is the id of an existing morph type such as stem, root, prefix or suffix. `gloss` and the optional `definition` are in the analysis writing system `analysisWs`.

`msa` is the grammatical info (in FieldWorks, the morphosyntactic analysis). Its `kind` must suit the morph type: `stem` for a stem or root, and `inflectional`, `derivational` or `unclassified` for an affix. `category` is the part of speech; a derivational affix also needs `toCategory`, the part of speech of the word it makes. An inflectional affix can name existing `slots` of its category or a category above it, and a stem can name an `inflectionClass`, such as a noun class, and `exceptionFeatures`, a list of existing exception features the analysis carries (the same rules as in `compose-add-morphosyntax-analysis`; a repeated id or an id that is not one of the project's exception features is refused, and only a stem takes them).

An inflectional affix can also be restricted. `inflectionClasses` lists existing inflection classes of the affix's category or a category above it, and its form then attaches only to stems of those classes; leave it out for no restriction. A derivational affix uses `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` to set its From Inflection Class and From Exception Features on the grammatical info; inflection classes on its form do not restrict its derivational analysis. `environments` lists existing phonological environments the form occurs in, for a stem or an affix. Empty lists, repeated ids and a stem's `inflectionClass` on an affix are refused.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

Every id can belong to something an earlier command added to the same Draft, such as a new part of speech. The command returns the new entry's operations and created entity ids for later calls. Dry Run and Trial the Draft on affected words, revise it, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

A derivational affix's composed summary lists a `Derivation: From -> To` line naming both categories, so a swapped pair shows at once, and its Dry Run warns when the project has no stem, subcategory stem or derivation that makes the From category, or when nothing takes the To category (or a subcategory) as input, which usually means the categories are the wrong way round.

## When not to use this

- For an affix, choose an inflectional or derivational MSA, not unclassified, which attaches without restriction; only an inflectional one fills an inflectional slot.
- Do not create an entry per stem that takes the same affix; one affix entry serves them all.
- For another form of an existing entry, use `compose-author-alternate-form`.

entries.title: Author a metathesis rule
entries.description: Stages one FieldWorks metathesis rule in a Draft: a left environment, a left and a right switch item that trade places, an optional middle and a right environment. Dry Run it and try words with it in a Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a metathesis rule

Use this command to stage one metathesis rule in a Draft: two neighbouring sounds that trade places, such as Cebuano *dahm-a* becoming *damh-a* (Wolff 5.14; Black §6.1.2.3). It writes the rule the way FieldWorks does, as a Metathesis Rule whose Rule Formula has a **Left environment**, the two **Switch these items** cells, an optional middle and a **Right environment**. FieldWorks shows the result of the switch below the formula; Motif computes it.

```sh
motif compose-author-metathesis-rule --project language.fwdata --draft h-c-metathesis --intent '{"name":"h and a consonant switch","direction":"simultaneous","left":[{"phoneme":"<a-id>"}],"leftSwitch":{"naturalClass":"<h-class-id>"},"rightSwitch":{"naturalClass":"<consonant-class-id>"},"right":[{"phoneme":"<a-id>"}],"placement":{"after":"<syncope-rule-id>"}}'
```

With the left switch an `h` class and the right switch a consonant class, the sequence h + consonant is rewritten as consonant + h, so a stem *dahma* is found for the word *damha* and *dahma* itself is rejected.

## The intent

- `name` and `direction` are the same as in [Author a sound rule](cmd:compose-author-phonological-rule).
- `leftSwitch` and `rightSwitch` each name one `phoneme` or one `naturalClass`. The left switch is the first item in the formula and moves to the right switch's place, and the right switch moves to the left one. Both are required.
- `middle` is an optional single `phoneme` or `naturalClass` between the switches that stays where it is. `middleWith` is `left` (the default) or `right` and says which switch's cell it belongs to, as in FieldWorks.
- `left` and `right` are the environments, each up to eight items in linguistic order, or left out when empty. An item names one phoneme, natural class, `word` or `morpheme` boundary, or `boundaryMarker`. Metathesis environment items cannot be optional, repeated or carry alpha variables.
- `placement` names the existing `after` or `before` rule that bounds the insertion gap. Rule order matters: put a metathesis rule after the rule whose output it reorders, such as a syncope rule.

## What Motif writes

Motif creates the rule, its name and direction, one structural item for each environment and switch in order, and the structural-change positions that FieldWorks stores (`grammar/phMetathesisRule/setStrucChange`). The positions name where each part sits in the rule's structure; the stored text is left to FieldWorks' own writer. A rule with an unset position is silently dropped by the parser, so Motif refuses to enable a metathesis rule without a left switch and a right switch.

The rule is staged enabled once its parts are complete. Finalize the Proposal, inspect its Dry Run, then use Trial to confirm the switched words parse and the unswitched ones do not before a person Applies it.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

## When not to use this

- For a sound that changes without moving, use [Author a sound rule](cmd:compose-author-phonological-rule).
- For one irregular word, use `compose-author-alternate-form`; a metathesis rule reorders every form that matches.
- Do not name a natural class wider than the evidence supports: the rule switches every matching pair.

entries.title: Author a natural class
entries.description: Stages a named segment natural class with explicitly declared phoneme members in a Draft. Members may name existing phonemes or phonemes created earlier through declared dependencies. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a natural class

Stages a named segment natural class with explicitly declared phoneme members in a Draft. Members may name existing phonemes or phonemes created earlier through declared dependencies. Only a person can Apply.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

## When not to use this

- Do not add a class that spans unrelated sounds; list only what the pattern needs.
- If a class with the same members already exists, reuse it rather than authoring a duplicate.

entries.title: Author a part of speech
entries.description: Stages a new part of speech, at the top of the category list or under an existing category, with its name and optional abbreviation. Later composer calls in the same Draft can use it as the category of entries, slots and affixes.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a part of speech

Use this command when the project has no category for a kind of word you are about to enter, such as a noun or a transitive verb. It creates the category in the project's parts-of-speech list, or under an existing category as a subcategory, and gives it a name and an optional abbreviation.

```sh
motif compose-author-part-of-speech --project language.fwdata --draft categories \
  --intent '{"name":"noun","ws":"en","abbreviation":"n"}'
```

`name` and `ws` give the category's name in one writing system; the name must not already belong to another category in that writing system. `abbreviation` is the short label FieldWorks shows in interlinear text. `parent` is the optional id of an existing category; the new one becomes its subcategory.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

The command stages the create, the name and the abbreviation in the Draft, and returns the new category's id. Later composer calls in the same Draft can name that id as the category of new entries, affix slots and affixes. Finish the Proposal and inspect its Dry Run before a person Applies it.

entries.title: Author a phoneme
entries.description: Stages a phoneme with literal representations, including symbols such as parentheses and slash, and optional explicit feature values. Put case spellings of the same sound on that phoneme; use its created identity in natural classes or phonological rules. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a phoneme

Stages a phoneme with explicitly authored name and representations in a Draft. Use its created identity in later natural classes or phonological rules. Only a person can Apply.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

`representations` are literal spellings, including `(`, `)`, `/`, square brackets and other symbols used by imported projects. Do not escape them as environment syntax: `"representations": ["/"]` stores a literal slash. Supply `features` as `{ "feature": "<feature ID>", "value": "<value ID>" }` pairs to give each distinct sound or literal symbol its explicit feature bundle. A shared bundle permits unification; use distinct bundles when the segments must stay distinct. Empty representations, dotted-circle-only representations, parser-reserved boundary/null spellings (`+`, `.`, `^0`, `*0`, `&0`, `∅`), duplicate spellings and spellings owned by another phoneme or boundary are refused. Spellings are canonically decomposed, and display dotted circles are removed as in FieldWorks' parser loader.

Put case spellings of the same sound on the same phoneme: `["c", "C"]` or `["ng", "Ng", "NG"]`. Accented vowels remain distinct when they express different sounds; do not fold accents away. Implicit capital letters carry no phonological features, so [Check a grammar](cmd:grammar%20check) warns when a featured lowercase phoneme lacks titlecase or uppercase representations.

A literal symbol in a phonological rule is a typed phoneme context, not textual syntax. In an allomorph environment, use a singleton [natural class](cmd:compose-author-natural-class) for a symbol that collides with environment syntax. For example, a class containing only the `(` phoneme can appear as `[LP]`; parentheses outside a class reference keep their environment meaning.

Create features, choose their particular values and author phonemes in one [batch](cmd:compose-batch) with references such as `@identity:values:slash`.

entries.title: Author a phonological feature
entries.description: Stages a closed phonological feature and its values in the project's phonological feature system, such as place with labial, coronal and velar. Phonemes carry the values and a natural class can be defined by them. Defining the first feature of a featureless project changes how rewrite rules that name segment classes are read, so Trial the rules after it. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a phonological feature

Stages a closed phonological feature and its values in the project's phonological feature system, such as `place` with `labial`, `coronal` and `velar`. Phonemes then carry the values (see [Set a phoneme's features](cmd:compose-edit-phoneme-features)) and a natural class can be defined by them ([Author a natural class](cmd:compose-author-natural-class), [Edit a natural class's features](cmd:compose-edit-natural-class-features)). Only a person can Apply.

```sh
motif compose-author-phonological-feature --project language.fwdata --draft features \
  --intent '{"name":"place","abbreviation":"plc","values":[{"name":"labial","abbreviation":"lab"},{"name":"coronal","abbreviation":"cor"}]}'
```

The intent has `name`, optional `abbreviation` and `values`, a nonempty list of `{ "name", "abbreviation" }` objects (the abbreviation is optional). Names are written in the project's first analysis writing system. A feature name or abbreviation that another phonological feature already has is refused, and so is a repeated value name or abbreviation inside the feature.

Use [Add a phonological feature value](cmd:compose-add-phonological-feature-value) to extend a feature that exists. A feature is not a part of speech, an inflection feature or an exception feature; those use other commands. The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project.

entries.title: Author a phonological rule
entries.description: Stages one regular phonological rule in a Draft, with one or more ordered right-hand sides, each with its own Output, contexts and rule features, and up to eight items in each Input and Output sequence. Output classes allow lexical alternatives; overlapping right-hand sides use the first applicable case, while feature changes preserve other features and alpha variables express agreement or disagreement. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a sound rule

Use this command to stage one regular phonological rule in a Draft. FieldWorks' Input and Output are the `input` and `output` arrays. Motif accepts up to eight items in each, in order. Each item names an existing `phoneme` or `naturalClass`, or an Output feature `change`. An empty `input` means insertion, and an empty `output` means deletion. A natural class in the input matches any member of that class. A rule whose Output is a multi-member segment class does not choose a member. It applies only the features the members share, so the input segment keeps its own value for every feature the members differ on. An *l* stays *l* under {l,w}, and a [-lat] *d* becomes *r* under {r,l}. Only an input with no value for those features matches every member (fieldworks-parser-conformance#38). Motif warns when an Output names a class of several segments. An aligned feature-class Output changes the specified features and preserves the others.

Before composing a rule, read the encoding guide for the phenomenon: `motif help guide:encoding/nasal-assimilation --full` for a nasal sound change, or `motif help` for the other guides.

```sh
motif compose-author-phonological-rule --project language.fwdata --draft nasal-rule --intent '{"name":"n becomes m before a labial","direction":"left-to-right","input":[{"phoneme":"<n-id>"}],"output":[{"phoneme":"<m-id>"}],"left":[{"boundary":"word"}],"right":[{"naturalClass":"<labial-class-id>"},{"boundary":"word"}],"placement":{"after":"<neighbor-rule-id>"}}'
```

For example, the Input sequence n t can become the Output sequence m d:

```sh
motif compose-author-phonological-rule --project language.fwdata --draft sequence-rule --intent '{"name":"nt becomes md","direction":"simultaneous","input":[{"phoneme":"<n-id>"},{"phoneme":"<t-id>"}],"output":[{"phoneme":"<m-id>"},{"phoneme":"<d-id>"}]}'
```

The two sides may have different lengths: n k to n shortens the matched sequence, and t to n k lengthens it. Use the single-outcome shorthand above or `rightHandSides`, one or more ordered cases with their own `output`, `left`, `right`, `requiredFeatures`, `excludedFeatures` and optional `inputCategories` (part-of-speech ids). Do not mix the two forms. Every outcome requires `output`; omitted contexts and applicability lists are empty. Input, name and direction belong to the whole rule.

`direction` is `left-to-right`, `right-to-left` or `simultaneous`. `left` and `right` each contain up to eight items in linguistic order, and either may be left out or empty: a rule with no left context applies wherever its right context and input match, a rule with no right context likewise, as FieldWorks allows. An item names one phoneme, natural class, `word` or `morpheme` boundary, or `boundaryMarker` id. An explicit `boundaryMarker` keeps its authored identity; use `boundary: "word"` or `boundary: "morpheme"` to name a standard boundary. In the first phoneme set, `#` and `+` must use FieldWorks' standard word and morpheme marker identities. If a code is stored only under another identity, or the rule names a marker with the wrong identity, the command refuses; repair the project in FieldWorks by re-pointing references to the standard marker, removing the stray marker, then saving and reloading. A spare duplicate "+" or "#" beside a standard marker that already holds the code does not block the rule, which always uses the standard marker. A word boundary must be at the outer edge. `placement` names the adjacent rule before the insertion gap (`after`), the adjacent rule after it (`before`), or both for an interior gap; the first rule needs no placement. The command refuses stale or nonadjacent anchors, classes that are empty or outside this project's phonological data, contradictory alpha references, metathesis, and allomorph environments.

For feature changes and alpha agreement or disagreement, read `motif help guide:encoding/feature-rules --full`. Output `change` contains feature/value pairs to set on the matched segment, and requires equal Input and Output lengths. `variables` on a feature-class item or Output change contains `{ "variable": "alpha", "feature": "<feature-id>", "polarity": "+" }` references; use `-` for disagreement. The whole rule can name up to 24 distinct alpha variables, matching FieldWorks' loader. A variable may have a single reference or only negative references, and may use any declared closed phonological feature with values, even before it is assigned to phonemes. The same variable cannot name two features or have contradictory polarity on one item. FieldWorks HCLoader cannot discover a variable confined to repeated items inside multi-item contexts; such a variable needs a reference on Input, Output, a non-repeated item, or a single-item context.

The response lists the operations created. Take the `entityId` from its `grammar/phPhonData/createPhonRules` operation and use that returned value in the next rule's `placement.after` or `placement.before`. Repeat the command against the same Draft to stage a whole sequence; Motif replays its earlier operations while composing each rule, so you do not need to Apply between calls. The first rule in an empty sequence has no placement; every rule added to a nonempty sequence needs an explicit adjacent anchor.

To stage several rules in one file, use the compose-batch command with batch-local `as` labels and `@label` placement anchors. Labels apply only to phonological-rule placements and must match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,20}` (1–21 ASCII characters).

The rule is staged disabled and is enabled only after every right-hand side has complete supported contexts. Finalize the Proposal, inspect its Dry Run, then use Trial to check the expected parse and generation behavior before a person Applies it.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

## When not to use this

- For one irregular word or stem, use `compose-author-alternate-form` or an allomorph; a rule changes every form that matches its context.
- For one affix with a few listed variants, keep them under one entry with environments.
- Do not widen the context or the classes beyond what the evidence supports.

## Several right-hand sides

```json
{
  "name": "nasal outcomes by context",
  "direction": "simultaneous",
  "input": [{ "phoneme": "<n-id>" }],
  "rightHandSides": [
    { "output": [{ "phoneme": "<m-id>" }], "right": [{ "phoneme": "<p-id>" }], "requiredFeatures": ["<lexical-tag-id>"] },
    { "output": [{ "phoneme": "<ng-id>" }], "right": [{ "phoneme": "<k-id>" }], "requiredFeatures": ["<lexical-tag-id>"], "excludedFeatures": ["<keep-id>"] }
  ]
}
```

The array declares case order. At a matching site, FieldWorks uses the first applicable right-hand side. Overlapping cases do not freely alternate. For Wolff's *bukid* → *kabukiran/kabukilan*, a rule cannot give both outcomes: an Output class containing r and l keeps the input's own value for every feature r and l differ on, so it does not offer both. Author the free variation as alternate forms of the stem, or use one rule per outcome with a feature-class or literal Output scoped by a lexical rule feature. Required and excluded features select the words a case affects, and alpha variables share identities across the entire rule. There is no authoring ceiling on the number of cases. Read `motif help guide:encoding/phonological-rules --full` for the distinction between optional alternatives and ordered cases.

entries.title: Author a stem name
entries.description: Adds a category-owned stem name with explicit feature regions to a Draft. Each region states where an allomorph bearing this stem name is eligible; attaching it to an allomorph is a separate operation.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a stem name

Add a named set of feature conditions describing where a stem allomorph is eligible. A stem name belongs to a category and contains one or more regions; each region is a nonempty set of closed feature/value choices.

```sh
motif compose-author-stem-name --project language.fwdata --draft plural-stem \
  --intent '{"category":"<noun-id>","name":"Plural stem","ws":"en","regions":[[{"feature":"<number-id>","value":"<plural-id>"}]]}'
```

`category` is the existing part-of-speech id. `name` must be new among that category's stem names in the known writing system `ws`. An optional `abbreviation` supplies a short label. Every region choice must use a closed feature in the morphosyntactic feature system and a value belonging to it; a region cannot name the same feature twice.

The command creates the stem name, its regions and their complete feature specifications. It does not attach the stem name to an allomorph: that is the separate semantic `grammar/moStemAllomorph/setStemName` operation. It authors no fallback stem or affix.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

Dry Run and Trial the Draft on positive and negative words, revise it, then Finalize for a person to review and Apply.

## When not to use this

- A stem name only names feature conditions; it attaches to no allomorph and authors no stem.
- For forms conditioned by sounds, use environments with `compose-author-environment`, not a stem name.

entries.title: Author a text
entries.description: Stages a Text with Free Translation, Literal Translation and Notes in a Draft. FieldWorks writing system rules determine its segments, words and punctuation; missing exact NFD wordforms are created. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a text

```sh
motif compose-author-text --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"title":"Story","ws":"ceb","analysisWs":"en","paragraphs":[{"segments":[{"text":"(nakapaluwas) ug?","freeTranslation":"Did someone rescue?","literalTranslation":"rescued and?","notes":["Check the question in context."]}]}]}'
```

The closed intent gives the Text's title, vernacular writing system `ws`, and paragraphs. Each paragraph lists baseline pieces in `segments`, joined by single spaces. A piece is an object with `text` and optional `freeTranslation`, `literalTranslation` and `notes` (an ordered array of strings). All text uses NFD. An unknown or repeated property is refused.

FieldWorks' own LibLCM paragraph parser determines sentence segments, words and punctuation using the writing system's word-forming characters and existing phrase wordforms. Punctuation outside a phrase stays in the paragraph and becomes Punctuation Forms. A punctuation-only paragraph is allowed. Motif adds no paragraph or word-count limit.

Free Translation, Literal Translation and Notes are stored on the Segment, in `analysisWs`; omit that tag to use the project's default analysis writing system. An annotated piece must be exactly one FieldWorks segment. End each sentence with its punctuation or put it in a separate paragraph. A piece spanning sentences or ending inside a segment is refused when it carries annotations, so annotations cannot silently move to a different sentence.

The earlier segment shape, an array such as `["(nakapaluwas)","ug,","?"]`, is also accepted. Its tokens are joined with spaces and parsed in the same way; array boundaries alone do not force a sentence boundary.

A word whose exact form already exists in that writing system reuses its wordform. A missing form creates one new wordform in the same Draft, with an explicit dependency from the Text. Different spelling or case remains a different wordform.

The result lists created wordforms and the Text by identity. Inspect the Draft's Dry Run, revise it, then Finalize for review. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Author a variant entry
entries.description: Creates a sense-less variant of one sense in one step, with its form, morph type, environments and variant type, so the parser reads it as that sense's stem; the Dry Run warns when the component has no stem analysis. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Author a variant entry

Create a sense-less variant of one sense in one step: the entry, its lexeme form with morph type and environments, and a variant reference to the main sense. The parser reads the variant as that sense's stem, with the sense's gloss and analysis, so a second shape of a stem needs no copied sense.

```sh
motif compose-author-variant-entry --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"component":"<main-sense-id>","variantType":"<variant-type-id>","form":"plit","formWs":"ceb","morphType":"<stem-morph-type-id>","environments":["<environment-id>"]}'
```

`component`, `variantType`, `form`, `formWs` and `morphType` are required; `environments` and `hideMinorEntry` (true hides the minor entry) are optional, and the intent is closed. The entry gets no sense and no analysis. The Dry Run warns when the component has no stem analysis, because the parser would then load nothing for the variant. Use `compose-strip-variant-senses` for variants that already exist with a copied sense. A sense-less variant is what LibLCM's CreateVariantEntryAndBackRef makes (ADR 0112).

entries.title: Compose many intents
entries.description: Stages every intent in a JSON file in one Draft with one project load, through the same checks as each composing command alone. If any intent is refused, nothing is added, and both a label and a Rationale are still required before Finalize. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Compose many intents

Stages every intent in a JSON file in one Draft with one project load, through the same checks as each composing command alone. If any intent is refused, nothing is added. Only a person can Apply.

Composing operations does not set the Draft's review text. Before Finalize, add a short label with `motif label` and a Rationale with [`proposal rationale`](cmd:proposal%20rationale).

The file names each intent's composing command and carries the same closed intent that command's `--intent` takes.
Add an optional `citation` beside `intent`; Motif records it as operation provenance without changing the intent or its digest.

```json
{"intents": [
  {"verb": "compose-author-phoneme", "intent": {"name": "i", "representations": ["i"]},
   "citation": {"source": "Grammar 2026", "locator": "§ 3"}},
  {"verb": "compose-author-natural-class", "intent": {"name": "front", "abbreviation": "F", "members": ["<phoneme id>"]}}
]}
```

Phonological-rule entries may add an `as` label and a later rule may use `@label` in `placement.after` or `placement.before`:

```json
{"intents": [
  {"verb": "compose-author-phonological-rule", "as": "r1",
   "intent": {"name": "first rule", "direction": "left-to-right", "input": [{"phoneme": "<phoneme id>"}],
     "output": [], "left": [{"boundary": "word"}], "right": [{"boundary": "morpheme"}]}},
  {"verb": "compose-author-phonological-rule", "as": "r2",
   "intent": {"name": "second rule", "direction": "left-to-right", "input": [{"phoneme": "<phoneme id>"}],
     "output": [], "left": [{"boundary": "word"}], "right": [{"boundary": "morpheme"}],
     "placement": {"after": "@r1"}}}
]}
```

Any entry may add an `as` label, and a later entry may write `@label` as a whole value anywhere in its intent in place of an ID that the labelled entry created. A phoneme entry labelled `ph`, for instance, lets a later natural class list `"members": ["@ph"]`. Without a kind `@label` means the one object the entry created that nothing else it created sits under (the new entry of an entry composer, the new phoneme); if the entry created several unrelated objects, or you want a dependent one, name the kind: `@label:msa` (or `@label:morphosyntaxanalyses`), `@label:senses`, `@label:codes`, the last word of the operation kind without `create`. A step that creates alternate forms also names each one by its morph type, `@label:prefix`, `@label:suffix`, `@label:infix`, `@label:proclitic`, `@label:enclitic` or `@label:stem`, which tells the two parts of a circumfix apart. A reference that matches nothing, more than one object (the refusal names them), a label declared later, or an entry that created nothing is refused, and the refusal names the objects the entry did create.

Select one of several values created with a phonological feature by its exact value name in the default analysis writing system: `@identity:values:slash`. Names are case-sensitive and canonically equivalent Unicode spellings match. Bare `@identity:values` refuses when there is more than one value. The selector searches only values created by that labelled entry; a value added by another entry uses that entry's own label. Rule input, output and feature contexts accept the same references as other intents.

```json
{"intents": [
  {"verb": "compose-author-phonological-feature", "as": "identity",
   "intent": {"name": "identity", "values": [{"name": "letter"}, {"name": "slash"}]}},
  {"verb": "compose-author-phoneme", "as": "slash",
   "intent": {"name": "literal slash", "representations": ["/"],
     "features": [{"feature": "@identity", "value": "@identity:values:slash"}]}},
  {"verb": "compose-author-phoneme",
   "intent": {"name": "letter c", "representations": ["c", "C"],
     "features": [{"feature": "@identity", "value": "@identity:values:letter"}]}}
]}
```

For subsequent calls in the same Draft, or for saved features, use `lookup:phonological-feature:identity` and `lookup:phonological-feature-value:identity|slash`. Each feature or value matches an exact name or abbreviation in the default analysis writing system. Zero or several matches refuse; use a canonical ID to disambiguate. Lookup runs after earlier staged edits, and both lookup forms work in feature specs and rules.

Labels must match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,20}` (1–21 ASCII characters). They are case-sensitive and unique within the file. Motif resolves them to canonical IDs before composing and declaring dependencies. They are not saved as intent data. Only a whole value that starts with `@` and names a declared label is replaced, so the plain text `ph` is never touched; the text `@home`, naming no declared label, is left as written; names, citations, and IDs in other fields keep their normal meaning.

Intents run in file order, and each one sees the changes of the intents before it, so the Draft ends as it would after the same commands run one at a time. A refusal names the failing intent's position and command.

There is no limit by intent or operation count.

## Changing many stems at once

The per-stem composers take one target each, and a batch is how a whole clean-up becomes one Proposal. Put one intent per stem in the file, for example `compose-set-stem-part-of-speech` to retype hundreds of stems (each with its own `expectedPartOfSpeech`) and, to stop stems parsing, retype or delete them (the do-not-parse flag changes no parse). Mix verbs freely; `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` takes `alsoMsas` and `compose-add-exception-features` takes `msas`, so those two need only one intent for a list. Give the Draft its own Rationale before Finalize.

entries.title: Change an affix’s kind
entries.description: Stages a change of one affix between inflectional, derivational and unclassified in place, keeping its category and the senses that use it. What the new kind cannot hold, such as a template slot or a To category, is reported as a warning, not refused. Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Change an affix's kind

Use this command when an affix was entered as one kind and the evidence says another: inflectional (it fills a slot of a template), derivational (it makes a word of a category from a word of another), or unclassified (not yet analysed). Choosing and changing later is the normal path, so the change is made in place and can be changed back with the same command.

```sh
motif compose-change-affix-kind --project language.fwdata --draft kind \
  --intent '{"msa":"<affix-msa-id>","kind":"derivational","toCategory":"<category-id>"}'
```

The intent has `msa`, the id of the affix's current grammatical info, and `kind`: `inflectional`, `derivational` or `unclassified`. `toCategory` belongs to `derivational` only and names the category of the word the affix makes; when it is absent the affix keeps its attaching category on both sides. `slots` belongs to `inflectional` only and names existing slots of the affix's category or an ancestor; an inflectional affix applies only in a template slot, so a change to inflectional without `slots` is allowed but reported. An affix already of the kind asked for stages nothing.

What the change does: it creates the grammatical info of the new kind with the attaching category, points every sense that used the old one at it, moves every ad hoc morpheme prohibition and every parser-analysis morph bundle that referred to the old one to the new one (in the same place in the prohibition's list), and deletes the old one. The new grammatical info has a new id, so use that id to change the kind back. Exception features of the attaching side carry between inflectional and derivational. The form is not touched, so a reduplication or other process stays as authored.

What the new kind cannot hold is listed in the Dry Run as related objects, never refused: the slots of an inflectional affix, a derivational affix's From and To inflection classes, To exception features, stem name, features and a To category different from the attaching one, an inflectional affix's features, and inflection classes on the form when the affix stops being inflectional. To restore it, give the same slots, classes or `toCategory` when changing back.

A moved prohibition or morph bundle is listed in the Dry Run too, because it now names an affix of another kind: the prohibition still bans the same affix, but it has no effect while an inflectional affix fills no slot, and approved analyses now state the affix as the new kind. The only refusals rest on an invalid model: the grammatical info is a stem's, not an affix's, or its entry has no affix form, or a slot belongs to another category, or an object of some other class that Motif cannot point at another grammatical info still refers to the old one and would be left pointing at nothing.

A change to derivational lists a `Derivation: From -> To` line naming both categories in the composed summary, and its Dry Run warns when the project has no stem, subcategory stem or derivation that makes the From category, or when nothing takes the To category (or a subcategory) as input, which usually means the categories are the wrong way round.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on words the affix should and should not parse, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Delete a prohibition
entries.description: Stages deletion of one flat ad hoc prohibition after checking its complete expected-current state. Referenced entries and forms are kept; the Dry Run lists any grammatical analyses and word-analysis references deleted by native FieldWorks cleanup.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a prohibition

`compose-delete-adhoc-prohibition` stages deletion of one flat allomorph or morpheme ad hoc prohibition. MCP offers `motif_delete_adhoc_prohibition`; only a person can Apply.

Supply `target` and the complete `expected` state: `kind`, nullable `first`, ordered `rest` and legacy `allomorphs` arrays, integer `adjacency`, and Boolean `disabled`, using the same shape as [Retarget a prohibition](cmd:compose-edit-adhoc-prohibition-references). The expected state must match, including disabled or legacy occurrences. Unknown targets, groups and stale state refuse.

The Dry Run names the deleted prohibition and every grammatical analysis and stored word-analysis reference that native FieldWorks cleanup deletes. Referenced entries and forms are kept; Apply refuses as stale if the cleanup effects differ from the reviewed Dry Run. Stage the deletion before [deleting a process graph](cmd:compose-delete-affix-process) or `compose-delete-lexical-entry` that it currently refers to. A remaining native or custom incoming reference to the prohibition blocks deletion and is named.

entries.title: Delete an affix process
entries.description: Stages deletion of an affix process and its whole owned graph after every incoming reference has been explicitly moved or removed. An optional plain allomorph of the same entry replaces it, becoming the lexeme form when needed.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete an affix process

`compose-delete-affix-process` stages deletion of one affix process with every input, output and other object it owns. Supply `entry` and `form`, with optional `replacement`: an existing plain affix allomorph of the same entry and morph type. A plain replacement can be authored earlier in this Draft with [Add an alternate form](cmd:compose-author-alternate-form). MCP offers `motif_delete_affix_process`; Apply stays with a person.

If the process is the lexeme form, its plain replacement moves from the alternate list to the lexeme slot. If the process is an alternate, the plain replacement stays where it is. Without `replacement`, the process is deleted without selecting a survivor. Other forms, senses and grammatical analyses are kept.

Every incoming reference into the whole process graph must be moved or removed first in the same Draft. [Retarget prohibition references](cmd:compose-edit-adhoc-prohibition-references) or [delete each prohibition](cmd:compose-delete-adhoc-prohibition). Disabled and legacy references count too. A reference from a stored analysis or custom field also blocks deletion; the refusal names every remaining source, field and occurrence and explains how to clear it. No reference is silently cleared by deletion.

The Draft binds the complete process graph and declares dependencies on the changes clearing its references. Changes to the graph require recomposition; new references after a Dry Run require renewed review. The Dry Run lists the deleted graph identities, the plain replacement and the entry content kept. Run a Trial with unaffected and affected words before a person Applies.

entries.title: Delete an empty sense
entries.description: Deletes an empty sense and its unused analysis. An analysis containing only a part of speech is allowed when the entry has a linked variant reference; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete an empty sense

Delete one wholly empty sense of an entry, together with the stem analysis that only that sense uses. A variant entry that keeps one empty sense blocks its main entry's path; this removes the sense so the variant takes it.

```sh
motif compose-delete-empty-sense --project language.fwdata --draft ceb-d001 \
  --intent '{"target":"<sense-id>","entry":"<owning-entry-id>"}'
```

Both fields are required and the intent is closed. The command refuses, and changes nothing, when:

- the sense has any content, such as a gloss, definition, example, note or sub-sense; there is no flag that overrides this, because deleting a sense with content loses a person's work;
- `entry` is not the entry that owns the sense;
- anything else refers to the sense.

An analysis containing only a part of speech is allowed only when the entry has a variant reference with a component target. The Dry Run records the removed part of speech. The sense's analysis is deleted with it only when no other sense of the entry uses it and nothing else, such as a parser analysis, refers to it. If another sense uses it, the analysis stays. If something else refers to it, the command refuses.

Run many at once with `compose-batch`, one entry per sense, so a whole clean-up becomes one Proposal. Each operation carries a rationale; the Draft still needs its own Rationale (`proposal rationale`) before Finalize.

Use this editor through the CLI or MCP. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Delete a phonological environment
entries.description: Deletes a phonological environment that no allomorph, rule or other object uses. It refuses an environment still in use and names each user. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a phonological environment

Deletes a phonological environment that no allomorph, rule or other object uses. It refuses an environment still in use and names each user.

```sh
motif compose-delete-environment --project language.fwdata --draft cleanup \
  --intent '{"environment": "<environment-id>", "expectedText": "/ _ [C]"}'
```

`environment` and `expectedText` are required and the intent is closed. `expectedText` must match the current value, so a wrong or stale target is refused and nothing is staged. The command refuses, changing nothing, while any allomorph, rule or other object refers to the environment, and names each with its class, id and entry.

In FieldWorks: Grammar, Phonology, Environments, select the environment, Delete.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite the operation. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Delete an exception feature
entries.description: Deletes an item of the Exception Features list that nothing refers to any more. It refuses while anything still uses it and names each user. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete an exception feature

Deletes an item of the Exception Features list that nothing refers to any more.

```sh
motif compose-delete-exception-feature --project language.fwdata --draft cleanup \
  --intent '{"feature": "<feature-id>", "expectedName": "<current feature name>"}'
```

`feature` and `expectedName` are required and the intent is closed. `expectedName` must match the current value, so a wrong or stale target is refused and nothing is staged. The command refuses, changing nothing, while any other object refers to the feature, an item that has sub-items, or an item that is not in the Exception Features list. The message names each referrer with its class, id and entry. Take the feature off those with `compose-edit-exception-features` (or `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` for affix from and to features) first, in the same Draft or an earlier one.

In FieldWorks: Grammar, Exception Features, select the item, Delete. `compose-edit-exception-features` takes the feature off the stems and affixes that carry it first.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite the operation. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Delete an entry
entries.description: Deletes one whole dictionary entry, with its forms, senses and grammatical info, because the entry is redundant; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply. It refuses an entry that a variant, relation, parser analysis or prohibition still refers to.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete an entry

Delete one whole dictionary entry together with its lexeme form, alternate forms, senses, examples, grammatical info and entry references. Use it when the entry is redundant, for example a duplicate whose forms now live on another entry, or an old entry a new one replaces.

```sh
motif compose-delete-lexical-entry --project language.fwdata --draft redundant-entries \
  --intent '{"entry":"<entry-id>"}'
```

`entry` is required and the intent is closed.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when any object outside the entry refers to the entry or to anything it owns: a variant or complex-form reference in another entry, a lexical relation, a morph bundle of a parser analysis, an ad hoc prohibition, or a reversal entry. The message names the referrers; remove or retarget each reference first, for example with `compose-link-variant` or `compose-remove-alternate-form`. References between the entry's own parts, such as a sense that uses one of its analyses, are not referrers.

The Dry Run lists the entry's headword, its lexeme form and alternate forms with their classes, text in every writing system and morph type, its senses with gloss and definition, its analyses, and the number of entry references, so a reviewer sees exactly what goes. A Draft may delete several entries, and may delete an entry and author its replacement in the same Draft.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Delete a natural class
entries.description: Deletes a natural class that nothing uses: no rule or other class refers to it, and no environment string writes its name or abbreviation in square brackets. It refuses otherwise and names each user. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a natural class

Deletes a natural class that nothing uses: no rule or other class refers to it, and no environment string writes its name or abbreviation in square brackets. It refuses otherwise and names each user.

```sh
motif compose-delete-natural-class --project language.fwdata --draft cleanup \
  --intent '{"naturalClass": "<natural-class-id>", "expectedName": "<current class name>"}'
```

`naturalClass` and `expectedName` are required and the intent is closed. `expectedName` must match the current value, so a wrong or stale target is refused and nothing is staged. The command refuses, changing nothing, while a rule, another natural class or an object refers to the class, or an environment string contains `[Name]` or `[Abbreviation]` for it, and names each.

In FieldWorks: Grammar, Phonology, Natural Classes, select the class, Delete. Use `compose-relink-natural-class` to point the users at another class first.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite the operation. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Delete a sound rule
entries.description: Removes one phonological rule and the contexts only it uses, after checking its name. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a sound rule

Use this command to remove a phonological rule and the contexts only it uses.

```sh
motif compose-delete-phonological-rule --project language.fwdata --draft drop-rule \
  --intent '{"target":"<rule-id>","expectedName":"<current rule name>"}'
```

`expectedName` must match the rule's name, so a wrong or stale target is refused and nothing is staged. To keep a rule but stop it applying, disable it instead (`compose-set-phonological-rule-disabled`).

entries.title: Delete a sense
entries.description: Deletes one top-level or nested meaning that carries content, with what it owns, because the meaning is kept elsewhere; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply. It refuses an entry's only meaning and any meaning that a relation, cross-reference or parser analysis refers to.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a sense

Delete one sense, top-level or sub-sense, together with its sub-senses and examples. Use it when the meaning is kept somewhere else, for example a derived word that was folded into its root as a sense and now has an entry of its own. For a sense with nothing in it, `compose-delete-empty-sense` is the stricter command.

```sh
motif compose-delete-sense --project language.fwdata --draft ceb-d003 \
  --intent '{"target":"<sense-id>","owner":"<entry-id>"}'
```

`target` and `owner` are required and the intent is closed. `owner` is the entry that owns a top-level sense, or the parent sense of a sub-sense, so a wrong id is refused instead of deleted.

What goes: the sense, every sub-sense and example under it, and the entry's grammatical analysis that only these senses used. An analysis is removed only when no remaining sense uses it and nothing else, such as a parser analysis, refers to it. FieldWorks leaves such an analysis in the entry; here it goes so the entry keeps no unused analysis. The Dry Run lists the deleted sense and its owner's remaining senses, and for the sense and each deleted sub-sense its gloss and definition in every writing system, its notes, source, scientific name, semantic domains, status, examples with their translations, and pictures (file and caption), plus each deleted analysis, so a reviewer sees exactly what goes. Semantic domains and status are shown by name. A writing system the project cannot resolve is shown by its numeric handle.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when:

- the sense is the only sense of its entry, unless the entry stays a variant (a variant reference with a variant type) of an entry or sense that has a stem analysis; a sense-less variant is a shape LibLCM makes, and the parser reads it as that stem, but an entry that is not a variant, or varies a non-stem, would load nothing;
- anything refers to the sense or to one of its sub-senses or examples: a lexical relation or cross-reference, a component or primary lexeme of a variant or complex-form reference, a reversal entry that lists the sense, or a morph bundle of a parser analysis; the message names the referrer, and the reference must be removed or retargeted first;
- `owner` is not the sense's owner.

A Draft may delete several senses; each is composed against the Draft's earlier steps, so a second deletion from the same entry sees the first one's result.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Delete a text segment Note
entries.description: Deletes one Note of a Text Segment, the objects compose-edit-text-notes sets. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a text segment Note

Deletes one Note of a Text Segment, the objects compose-edit-text-notes sets.

```sh
motif compose-delete-text-segment-note --project language.fwdata --draft cleanup \
  --intent '{"note": "<note-id>", "expectedText": "<current note text>"}'
```

`note` and `expectedText` are required and the intent is closed. `expectedText` must match the current value, so a wrong or stale target is refused and nothing is staged. The command refuses, changing nothing, when the text differs from the Note's current text, or the id is not a Note of a Text Segment. Use `compose-edit-text-notes` to replace a Note instead of deleting it.

In FieldWorks: Texts & Words, Interlinear Text, clear the Note line of the segment.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite the operation. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Edit an ad hoc prohibition
entries.description: Stages one explicit Disabled value for a flat allomorph or morpheme prohibition in a Draft. The expected value guards against stale evidence; Motif never Applies this change automatically. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit an ad hoc prohibition

```sh
motif compose-edit-adhoc-prohibition --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<portableId>","expectedDisabled":false,"disabled":true}'
```

The closed intent names one existing allomorph or morpheme prohibition. `expectedDisabled` must match the value Motif reads while preparing the Draft; a stale value is refused. Set `disabled` to `true` to turn off a confirmed duplicate or `false` to enable a rule again. Grouped prohibitions are not supported.

The command stages one write in the Draft. It does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and compare bounded before and after Trials with the same words. Review the after Report; only a person can Apply a Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

## When not to use this

- It cannot add a prohibition, only turn an existing one off or on; to create one use `compose-author-adhoc-prohibition`, and not for a combination you could model.
- If a slot, template, required feature or environment can express the restriction, author that instead ([guide](guide:encoding/suffix-prefix-slots)).
- If the evidence does not say whether to switch one off, ask the linguist ([guide](guide:encoding/ask-the-linguist)).

entries.title: Retarget a prohibition
entries.description: Stages new allomorph or morpheme references for one ad hoc prohibition with an expected-current guard. Each occurrence stays within its original entry; first means Key Allomorph / Key Morpheme, rest means Other Allomorph(s) / Other Morpheme(s), and disabled is the inverse of Active.
entries.helpPage:
# Retarget a prohibition

`compose-edit-adhoc-prohibition-references` stages new references for one flat allomorph or morpheme ad hoc prohibition. MCP offers `motif_edit_adhoc_prohibition_references`; it stages a Draft and leaves Apply to a person.

Supply `target`, `expected` and `references`. Both state objects require `kind` (`allomorph` or `morpheme`), `first` (a canonical id, or null), ordered `rest` ids, ordered legacy `allomorphs` ids (empty for morpheme prohibitions), integer `adjacency`, and Boolean `disabled`. Adjacency uses FieldWorks' stored values: 0 anywhere, 1 somewhere to right, 2 somewhere to left, 3 adjacent to right, 4 adjacent to left. Every expected value must match the project as the Draft's earlier changes leave it.

In FieldWorks, `first` is **Key Allomorph** or **Key Morpheme**, and `rest` is **Other Allomorph(s)** or **Other Morpheme(s)**. `disabled` is the inverse of **Active**: `disabled: true` means Active is off, and `disabled: false` means Active is on.

The replacement keeps kind, adjacency, Disabled and the number and order of occurrences. Each new allomorph belongs to the same entry as the allomorph it replaces; each new morpheme is a grammatical analysis of the same entry as its predecessor. Unknown objects, wrong classes and cross-entry destinations refuse. Enabled prohibitions can be retargeted; a Trial measures the changed restriction.

Removing a morpheme reference can make LibLCM delete an unused grammatical analysis and clear its stored word-analysis references, as FieldWorks does. The Dry Run lists every such deletion for review before Apply; changed cleanup effects make Apply refuse as stale.

A process allomorph can point to a plain alternate authored earlier in the same Draft. Stage these edits before [deleting the process](cmd:compose-delete-affix-process). To remove the restriction instead, [delete the prohibition](cmd:compose-delete-adhoc-prohibition).

entries.title: Edit affix class restrictions
entries.description: Replaces an inflectional affix form's exact class restriction set, an ordinary prefix, suffix or interfix or an affix process such as reduplication, after checking the expected current ids. An empty set removes the restriction; for derivational affixes, use compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction instead. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit affix class restrictions

Replace the exact inflection class restriction set on an existing inflectional affix form, an ordinary affix or an affix process such as an inflectional reduplication.

```sh
motif compose-edit-affix-inflection-classes --project language.fwdata --draft numerals \
  --intent '{"target":"<affix-form-id>","expectedInflectionClasses":[],"inflectionClasses":["<class-id>"]}'
```

All three intent fields are required. Both class lists are unordered sets of canonical ids; `expectedInflectionClasses` must match the form's current memberships. An empty `inflectionClasses` list removes every restriction, leaving the form unrestricted rather than prohibiting attachment.

The target must be a usable ordinary inflectional prefix, suffix or interfix form with a vernacular spelling, or an affix process of any affix morph type, which the parser also restricts by these classes. A spelling that writes a bracket pattern is not refused. Circumfix entries are refused. The entry must have at least one inflectional grammatical-info record, and each record must have a usable category. Class ids returned by earlier composition calls in the same Draft can be used directly, and their dependencies are declared from the references.

This editor applies to inflectional affixes. The parser ignores a derivational affix's form classes; use `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` to set its From Inflection Class and From Exception Features.

Use this editor through the CLI; it is not exposed as an MCP tool.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects and run a Trial on affected words before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Edit an affix slot
entries.description: Changes whether an existing inflectional affix slot is optional, renames it, or both. The response lists every affix and template using the shared slot; Motif stages a Draft and never Applies it automatically. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit an affix slot

```sh
motif compose-edit-affix-slot --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<portableId>","expectedOptional":false,"optional":true}'
```

To rename the slot instead, or as well, add `writingSystem`, `expectedName` (the name it has now, empty if none) and `name`:

```sh
motif compose-edit-affix-slot --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<portableId>","writingSystem":"en","expectedName":"NUM","name":"Number"}'
```

Give `expectedOptional` with `optional`, the three rename fields, or both sets. A rename changes only the label: the slot keeps its identity, so every affix and template that uses it still does and the parse does not change.

The closed intent names one existing inflectional affix slot. `expectedOptional` must match the value in the project when the Draft is composed. The response lists every inflectional affix MSA and affix template that uses the shared slot, so the effect of changing its optionality is visible.

This command stages one Optional-field write in the Draft and does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and run a bounded Trial on the words affected by the slot. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Edit an affix template
entries.description: Adds, removes or reorders the existing prefix or suffix slots of a known affix template. Motif stages a Draft without Applying it automatically. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit an affix template

```sh
motif compose-edit-affix-template --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<portableId>","expectedPrefixSlots":["<id>","<id>"],"prefixSlots":["<id>","<id>"],"expectedSuffixSlots":[],"suffixSlots":[]}'
```

The closed intent names one existing affix template and gives its current and requested prefix and suffix orders. Each expected list must match the project. The requested lists may add existing slots, drop slots, or reorder them; each slot appears at most once, and the command stages one add, remove or move per difference through identity-relative placement.

The command stages the required move operations in the Draft. It cannot create or delete a template or slot, and it does not change the FieldWorks project. Inspect the Dry Run and run a bounded Trial on relevant words. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Edit an allomorph condition
entries.description: Changes the environment references on one existing stem or affix allomorph after checking its current list. Shared environments remain unchanged for every other allomorph that uses them. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit an allomorph condition

```sh
motif compose-edit-allomorph-condition --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<portableId>","field":"phoneEnv","expectedEnvironments":["<id>"],"environments":["<id>"]}'
```

The closed intent names one existing stem or affix allomorph, its LibLCM field, the current environment identities and the requested identities. `phoneEnv` is an unordered OR-list on stems and affixes. `position` is the affix allomorph's ordered list of position environments; only that list's order matters. A stale current list, unsupported target and environment outside the project's phonological data are refused.

The command changes references on this allomorph only. If an environment is shared, every other user keeps its reference and the environment itself is not edited. Create a new typed environment with `compose-author-environment` when the restriction needs a new context. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and run a bounded Trial on positive and negative examples. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Edit an allomorph form
entries.description: Changes one writing-system alternative of a selected ordinary stem or affix alternate after checking its owner and current form. Keeps the form identity, conditions and references; stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit an allomorph form

```sh
motif compose-edit-allomorph-form --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"entry":"<entry-id>","target":"<alternate-id>","writingSystem":"qaa","expectedForm":"pata","newForm":"pātaʔ"}'
```

Selects one existing ordinary stem or affix alternate by `target` and expected owning `entry`. Its current text in `writingSystem` must match `expectedForm` by canonical Unicode equivalence. A moved or deleted target, a different owner, a lexeme form, an affix process, a writing system outside this project's vernacular systems, or stale text refuses the edit before anything is staged. Set `newForm` to an empty string to clear that alternative; a nonempty replacement must contain non-whitespace text. A canonically equivalent replacement, including clearing an already absent alternative, produces no write.

The Form write preserves the allomorph ID, alternate order, morph type, abstract flag, sound environments, stem name, inflection classes, required features, references and other writing-system alternatives. Underlying does not mean abstract: FieldWorks skips ordinary abstract forms. Every underlying phoneme needs a nonempty representation; ordered rules realize distinctions omitted by running spelling.

For lexeme forms use [Rewrite lexeme forms](cmd:compose-rewrite-lexeme-form) with `foldStressMarks=false` and explicit `newForm`. Preserve a selected marked headword with [Edit a citation form](cmd:compose-edit-citation-form).

The CLI and MCP tool stage operations in a Draft. Inspect the Dry Run and Trial results before a person Applies the Proposal. No project is changed by composing. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the selected evidence.

entries.title: Decide an analysis
entries.description: Stages one human decision about an existing analysis or wordform in a Draft: approve, disapprove, return to unknown, mark the spelling incorrect, or store a parser reading as an unknown analysis. It names the exact canonical identity. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Decide an analysis

```sh
motif compose-edit-analysis-decision --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"decision":"approve","analysis":"<analysisId>"}'
```

The closed intent records one human decision. For `approve`, `disapprove` or `unknown`, name the stored analysis by its exact canonical identity in `analysis`; `unknown` removes an earlier approval or disapproval and is refused when the analysis has none. For `misspelled`, name the wordform in `wordform` instead: `{"decision":"misspelled","wordform":"<wordformId>"}`.

To store a parser reading as a new analysis in the unknown state, name the wordform and the reading's ordered morphs by exact identity: `{"decision":"add-reading","wordform":"<wordformId>","morphs":[{"form":"<allomorphId>","msa":"<msaId>","inflType":"<inflTypeId>"}]}`. Each morph names at least one of `form`, `msa`, `inflType` or `guessedString`. A reading that already has a stored analysis is refused. The result lists the new analysis in `createdObjects`; use that identity to approve or disapprove it in the same Draft.

There is no option yet to clear or correct a `misspelled` mark.

The command uses the same operations a collected word change does. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and review it. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Edit a citation form
entries.description: Writes a selected source headword in one Citation Form alternative after checking its current text. Leaves parser forms and other writing-system alternatives intact; stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a citation form

```sh
motif compose-edit-citation-form --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<entry-id>","writingSystem":"qaa","expectedForm":"","newForm":"páta"}'
```

Writes a selected source headword on an existing lexical entry. `expectedForm` is required, including an empty string when no Citation Form is held in that writing system. Comparison uses canonical Unicode equivalence. Set `newForm` to an empty string to clear that alternative; a nonempty replacement must contain non-whitespace text. A canonically equivalent replacement, including clearing an already absent alternative, produces no write. A missing or non-entry target, stale text or a writing system outside this project's vernacular systems refuses before staging.

Only the selected Citation Form alternative changes. Lexeme and alternate forms, their identities and references, and other writing-system alternatives stay intact. Citation Form is not parsed: retain a marked dictionary spelling here while the parser forms carry source-supported underlying distinctions. Use [Rewrite lexeme forms](cmd:compose-rewrite-lexeme-form) with `foldStressMarks=false` or [Edit an allomorph form](cmd:compose-edit-allomorph-form) for parser forms. The rewrite command's `setEmptyCitationForm` only copies the old lexeme spelling; it cannot supply a different selected source headword.
