The CLI and MCP tool stage operations in a Draft. Inspect the Dry Run and Trial results before a person Applies the Proposal. No project is changed by composing. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the selected evidence.

entries.title: Edit a clitic’s Attaches to Categories
entries.description: Set the Attaches to Categories of a clitic stem analysis to an exact set of parts of speech. Review the before and after category names in the Dry Run.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a clitic's Attaches to Categories

Set the "Attaches to Categories" of a clitic's stem analysis to an exact set of parts of speech. The analysis must belong to an entry whose form is a proclitic, enclitic or clitic. An empty set removes the restriction.

```sh
motif compose-edit-clitic-attachment --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"target":"<stem-analysis-id>","expectedCategories":["<current-category-id>"],"categories":["<category-id>","<category-id>"]}'
```

`expectedCategories` must match the current set exactly, so a change made since you read the analysis is refused. To make a form a clitic and restrict it in one Proposal, compose `compose-edit-morph-type` first in the same Draft; this edit sees the new morph type.

A proclitic or enclitic form also parses as a word on its own: FieldWorks and HermitCrab load each as a lexical entry in the Clitics stratum and as an attaching rule (Black, Parsing Conceptual Introduction, section 2.3: the parser handles a clitic "whether it is written attached or as a separate word"), and no property says it must attach. To keep a bound clitic from parsing alone, give its form the allomorph condition [author an environment](cmd:compose-author-environment) whose left context is a natural class, one environment per class that can precede it (for example a vowel class and a consonant class), then set both with `compose-edit-allomorph-condition`; a form with no left context then cannot start a word.

Attaches to Categories limits a clitic's hosts by their grammatical category. An exception feature on the clitic's own stem analysis does not choose the host: HermitCrab and PanGloss read it as a feature the clitic carries, never as a requirement on the host (`RealParserCliticHostTests`). For hosts that differ by category, give them a sub-category and list it here; for hosts that differ by their last sound, use allomorph environments as above.

The Dry Run shows the before and after category names. Review the Trial before a person Applies the Proposal. The CLI and MCP stage the Draft; MCP cannot Apply it.

entries.title: Turn a compound rule off or on
entries.description: Stages one explicit Disabled value for an endocentric or exocentric compound rule in a Draft. FieldWorks compound rules join any two stems, so a rule that builds non-words can be switched off; the expected value guards against stale evidence, and only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Turn a compound rule off or on

```sh
motif compose-edit-compound-rule --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<portableId>","expectedDisabled":false,"disabled":true}'
```

The closed intent names one existing endocentric or exocentric compound rule. `expectedDisabled` must match the value Motif reads while preparing the Draft; a stale value is refused. Set `disabled` to `true` to turn the rule off or `false` to turn it on again.

FieldWorks compound rules can accept any two stems, so a rule that builds non-words can be switched off here. Turning it off removes every word it builds, real compounds included, so test known compounds before and after.

The command stages one write in the Draft. It does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and compare bounded before and after Trials with the same words. Review the after Report; only a person can Apply a Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

## When not to use this

- It turns an existing compound rule off or on and builds nothing; it cannot repair a rule that builds the wrong words.
- Turning a rule off removes real compounds too, so Trial known compounds first and ask the linguist before switching one off.

entries.title: Edit Definition
entries.description: Stages the full meaning of a sense in Definition, checking the current text separately in each writing system. Empty replacement text clears that alternative; review the Draft before a person Applies it.
entries.helpPage:
Stages Definition, the full meaning of an existing sense, in a Draft.

```
motif compose-edit-definition --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<senseId>","alternatives":[{"writingSystem":"en","expectedText":"<current meaning>","text":"<full meaning>"}]}'
```

Use the sense's canonical identity, not its entry's identity. Each alternative checks the current plain text in that writing system against `expectedText` before staging anything. Give `"expectedText":""` when it has no text. Canonically equivalent Unicode spellings compare equal. Every alternative must match; a stale value refuses the entire edit.

Give `"text":""` to clear an alternative. Other writing systems stay as they are. Text is preserved, including whitespace; Motif sets no word-count limit. Gloss is the short translation equivalent, while Definition holds the full meaning; use [Edit Gloss](cmd:compose-edit-gloss) to revise the short equivalent separately.

Dry Run and Trial the Draft, then Finalize for review. Staging changes no saved FieldWorks data. Only a person can Apply.

entries.title: Restrict a derivational affix
entries.description: Sets, replaces or explicitly clears the From Inflection Class and the To Inflection Class, and can set the exact From Exception Features and To Exception Features on an existing affix entry's derivational grammatical info; alsoMsas applies the same change to many affixes. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Restrict a derivational affix

Set which stems a derivational affix can attach to through the affix's derivational grammatical info. Inflection classes on the form do not restrict a derivational analysis.

```sh
motif compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction --project language.fwdata --draft derivation \
  --intent '{"msa":"<derivational-msa-id>","fromInflectionClass":"<class-id>","fromExceptionFeatures":["<feature-id>"]}'
```

`msa` is the id of the derivational grammatical info on an existing affix entry. `fromInflectionClass`, when present, sets the From Inflection Class; the class must belong to the MSA's From category or one of its ancestors. `toExceptionFeatures` replaces the whole To set, as `fromExceptionFeatures` does the From set; to add to a set instead, use `compose-add-exception-features`. `fromExceptionFeatures`, when present, replaces the exact set of valid From Exception Features; pass an empty list to remove them all. `toExceptionFeatures`, when present, replaces the exact set of To Exception Features, the features the derived stem receives; an empty list removes them all. Omit a field to leave its current value unchanged. Give at least one of the fields.

`alsoMsas` lists further derivational grammatical info ids that receive the identical change, so one intent restricts hundreds of affixes; `msa` and `alsoMsas` must not repeat an id. The change is the same for each, so an affix that needs a different set takes its own intent in a `compose-batch` file. An affix process (a reduplication, say) takes the same fields, since the restriction sits on its grammatical info.

To remove the current From Inflection Class, pass `"clearFromInflectionClass":true` instead of `fromInflectionClass`. Do not supply both fields. You can combine the clear field with `fromExceptionFeatures`; omitting both class fields leaves the current class unchanged.

`toInflectionClass` sets the To Inflection Class, the class the derived stem receives, so it can then take that class's inflection (for example a passive or causative of a loan verb whose own class takes none). The class must belong to the MSA's To category or one of its ancestors. `"clearToInflectionClass":true` removes it; do not supply both. Omitting both leaves it unchanged.

## Keeping out a few stems of a host class

The From side can only require: the parser reads the From Inflection Class and the From Exception Features as features a stem must carry, and FieldWorks holds no way to exclude one. To let an affix attach to a class but not to some stems of it, such as a lexical agent noun that shares a class with real hosts, create a morpheme prohibition with `compose-author-adhoc-prohibition`: give the affix's derivational analysis as `first`, the unwanted stem's analysis as `rest` (or `restAnyOf` for several stems), and `adjacent-to-left` for a prefix or `adjacent-to-right` for a suffix. The real parser has been tested with a derivational prefix restricted to a class here: it stopped on the named stem and kept attaching to another stem of the same class. When the unwanted word is both a stored stem and a verb stem plus a derivational suffix (a noun `ombaji` that is also `omb` plus `-aji`), the stem prohibition removes only the stored-stem reading and the derived reading stays. Add a second prohibition with the same `first` and `rest` set to the verb stem's analysis followed by the suffix's derivational analysis (read left to right), with the same adjacency. The test in this repository used a prefix as `first` with `adjacent-to-left`: the word had two readings, the stem prohibition left the derived one, and the second prohibition left none. A suffix as `first` with `adjacent-to-right` was not tested this way; compare Trials before a person Applies.

An inflectional affix uses Inflection Classes on its form instead: set them while authoring the form with `compose-author-lexical-entry` or `compose-author-alternate-form`, or edit them with `compose-edit-affix-inflection-classes`. Motif stages the operations in a Draft; Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on stems that should and should not take the affix, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Set exception features
entries.description: Sets the exact exception features a stem or clitic carries, or the ones an inflectional affix requires of its stem. An empty list clears the set. Derivational affixes use their own command. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set exception features

Use this command to set the exception features on a stem or clitic, or the ones an inflectional affix requires of its stem. It replaces the whole set; an empty list clears it, and anything left out is removed. To add features without resetting the others, use `compose-add-exception-features`.

```sh
motif compose-edit-exception-features --project language.fwdata --draft features \
  --intent '{"msa":"<grammatical-info-id>","exceptionFeatures":["<feature-id>"]}'
```

`msa` is the id of the grammatical info of an existing entry:

- A stem or clitic (a stem analysis) carries the features. They are what an affix, or a rule that requires them, looks for.
- An inflectional affix requires the features, as its From Exception Features. A stem must carry all of them for the affix to attach. An affix with none attaches to any stem, whatever the stem carries (Black 2025, section 2.1.6).
- A derivational affix keeps its own command, `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction`. An unclassified affix has no exception features in FieldWorks, so it is refused.

Every feature must already be in the project's Exception Features list; add one with `compose-author-exception-feature`. A clitic can carry features for what attaches to it, but FieldWorks has no way to make a clitic require a feature of its host: a clitic attaches by the host's category only.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on stems that should and should not take the affix, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Edit Gloss
entries.description: Stages the short translation equivalent of a sense in Gloss, checking the current text separately in each writing system. Use Definition for the full meaning; empty replacement text clears an alternative.
entries.helpPage:
Stages Gloss, the short translation equivalent of an existing sense, in a Draft.

```
motif compose-edit-gloss --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<senseId>","alternatives":[{"writingSystem":"en","expectedText":"<current gloss>","text":"<short equivalent>"}]}'
```

Each alternative checks the current plain text against `expectedText` in that writing system before staging anything. Use an empty expected string for an empty alternative, and `"text":""` for a guarded clear. Canonically equivalent Unicode spellings compare equal. A stale alternative refuses the whole edit. Unmentioned writing systems stay as they are.

A gloss is usually a few words for interlinear text. Put the full meaning in [Definition](cmd:compose-edit-definition). Motif allows the text FieldWorks accepts and imposes no word-count limit. The advanced `add-set-gloss` command stages an unguarded semantic operation; this composer checks the authored expectation first.

Dry Run and Trial the Draft, then Finalize for review. Staging changes no saved FieldWorks data. Only a person can Apply.

entries.title: Edit an inflectional affix
entries.description: Changes which existing category slots an inflectional affix MSA uses. Other MSA kinds and slots outside the category hierarchy are refused; Motif stages a Draft and never Applies it automatically. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit an inflectional affix

```sh
motif compose-edit-inflectional-affix --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<portableId>","expectedSlots":["<id>"],"slots":["<id>"]}'
```

The closed intent names one existing inflectional affix MSA and its current and requested slot memberships. `expectedSlots` must match the project. Every requested slot must belong to the MSA's category, an ancestor category, or a subcategory of it, because the parser matches a template's category against the affix's category and a category covers its subcategories. A slot of an unrelated category is refused, since the parser would never use it there; give the affix grammatical info in that category instead. Other MSA subtypes are refused.

The command stages the necessary slot membership operations in the Draft and does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and run a bounded Trial on relevant words. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Edit lexical notes
entries.description: Stages an entry Note or a named sense note, checking the current text separately in each writing system. Record example words for an affix and its allomorphs in the entry Note; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
Stages an entry Note or one of the named sense notes shown in FieldWorks Lexicon Edit.

```
motif compose-edit-lexical-note --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<entryId>","field":"note","alternatives":[{"writingSystem":"en","expectedText":"","text":"<example word and explanation>"}]}'
```

`field` chooses a FieldWorks field:

| Value | FieldWorks name | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `note` | Note | Entry |
| `anthropology-note` | Anthropology Note | Sense |
| `discourse-note` | Discourse Note | Sense |
| `general-note` | General Note | Sense |
| `grammar-note` | Grammar Note | Sense |
| `phonology-note` | Phonology Note | Sense |
| `semantics-note` | Semantics Note | Sense |
| `sociolinguistics-note` | Sociolinguistics Note | Sense |

Each writing-system alternative must give `writingSystem`, `expectedText` and `text`. The current plain text must match the expectation; canonically equivalent Unicode spellings compare equal. An empty expectation means no current text. Empty replacement text clears that alternative. A stale alternative refuses the entire edit, and unmentioned writing systems stay as they are.

Record example words for affix entries in Note. FieldWorks has no built-in Note on stem allomorphs, affix allomorphs or affix processes: record an allomorph's spelling and example in its owning entry's Note. No artificial allomorph field is created. Project custom fields and the separate Extended Notes collection are different fields.

Dry Run and Trial the Draft, then Finalize for review. Staging changes no saved FieldWorks data. Only a person can Apply.

entries.title: Edit a form’s morph type
entries.description: Change an existing form’s morph type within its family: stem types among themselves, or affix types such as prefix, suffix and infix among themselves. Review the form and its before and after types in the Dry Run.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a form's morph type

Change the morph type of an existing form without replacing the form or its analysis. A stem form changes among FieldWorks' stem family: roots, stems, clitics, particles and phrases. An affix form, ordinary or a process such as reduplication, changes among the affix types: prefix, suffix, infix, simulfix, suprafix and the interfixes, so a prefix entered by mistake can become a suffix in place. Changes between the stem and affix families require a different authoring path because their analyses differ, and a circumfix is two parts in one entry, so no single form is edited into or out of one.

```sh
motif compose-edit-morph-type --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"target":"<form-id>","morphType":"<morph-type-id>"}'
```

The Dry Run identifies the form and its before and after types. Review the Trial before a person Applies the Proposal. The CLI and MCP stage the Draft; MCP cannot Apply it.

entries.title: Edit a natural class
entries.description: Adds or removes phonemes from one existing segment natural class after checking its exact current members. The response lists rules, environments and insertions that still use the class. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a natural class

Use this command when a segment class contains a sound it should not contain, or needs one additional member. It stages identity-based member edits in a Draft.

```sh
motif compose-edit-natural-class --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<classId>","expectedMembers":["<phonemeId>","<phonemeId>"],"members":["<phonemeId>"]}'
```

The closed intent names an existing segment natural class, its exact current phoneme identities and the requested distinct phoneme identities. Both lists must be nonempty, the current list must still match, and every requested phoneme must belong to this project's first phoneme set. The class keeps its identity, abbreviation and subtype; a feature class cannot be converted in place.

The response lists rewrite rules, environments and natural-class insertions that still use the class. Those references keep using the edited class. If only some users should follow a new definition, create a separate class and use `compose-relink-natural-class` for the intended users. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and run a bounded Trial on the corrected form and a productive held-out form. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Edit a natural class's features
entries.description: Stages a change to the feature values that define a feature-based natural class: set a constraint (a feature the class already constrains takes the new value in place) and clear constraints. The class must keep at least one constraint, and a segment class is refused. The response lists the environments, rules and insertions that use the class. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a natural class's features

Stages a change to the feature values that define one natural class, so the class matches the phonemes that carry them. Use the closed input `{ "target": "<natural class ID>", "set": [ { "feature": "<ID>", "value": "<ID>" } ], "clear": [ "<feature ID>" ] }` with at least one of `set` and `clear`. A constraint on a feature the class already has takes the new value in place. The class must keep at least one constraint, because a feature class with none cannot condition an environment; define a new class instead of emptying one. A segment class has no feature constraints and is refused: change its members with [Edit a natural class](cmd:compose-edit-natural-class). Only a person can Apply.

```sh
motif compose-edit-natural-class-features --project language.fwdata --draft classes \
  --intent '{"target":"<class-id>","set":[{"feature":"<place-id>","value":"<labial-id>"}]}'
```

The response lists the environments, rules and insertions that use the class (`RelatedObjects`); the change reaches each of them. Create a class by features with [Author a natural class](cmd:compose-author-natural-class) (`features`).

entries.title: Set a category class default
entries.description: Sets or clears a part of speech's explicit default inflection class after checking the expected current reference. Clearing can reveal an inherited default; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a category class default

Change the explicit default inflection class of an existing part of speech. The expected value is the stored explicit reference, not the effective default inherited from an ancestor.

```sh
motif compose-edit-part-of-speech-inflection-class-default --project language.fwdata --draft numerals \
  --intent '{"target":"<part-of-speech-id>","expectedInflectionClass":null,"inflectionClass":"<class-id>"}'
```

All three intent fields are required. `expectedInflectionClass` and `inflectionClass` are each either a canonical id or `null`. The desired class must belong to the target category or one of its ancestors. Setting the desired value to `null` clears the explicit reference; an inherited default may then apply.

Use this editor through the CLI; it is not exposed as an MCP tool.

Use a class id returned by an earlier composition in the same Draft directly in `inflectionClass`. The Draft composer declares the dependency from that reference. This edit creates no class.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects and run a Trial on affected words before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Edit a phoneme's representations
entries.description: Stages new written representations for an existing phoneme, or respells one it has, so a multigraph such as ng, ts or dy is another way the same segment is written and never a second phoneme. It refuses a spelling another phoneme or boundary already has, and a respelling that an environment writes. Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a phoneme's representations

Use this command to change how an existing phoneme is written. A multigraph such as `ng`, `ts` or `dy` is one representation of one phoneme, so add it to the phoneme it spells; do not author a second phoneme for it. Check the inventory first, and use `compose-author-phoneme` only for a sound the inventory lacks.

```sh
motif compose-edit-phoneme --project language.fwdata --draft sounds \
  --intent '{"target":"<phoneme-id>","add":[{"representation":"ng"}]}'
```

The intent has `target` and at least one of `add` and `respell`. Each `add` item is `{"representation":"..."}` and is appended after the phoneme's current codes. Each `respell` item is `{"from":"...","to":"..."}` and rewrites that code in place, keeping its identity.

Refusal messages begin with a stable name:

- `phoneme-edit-empty`: nothing to add or respell.
- `phoneme-not-in-inventory`: the target is not a phoneme of the first phoneme set.
- `phoneme-representation-invalid`: a representation is empty after removing display dotted circles, or is reserved by the parser for a boundary or null segment.
- `phoneme-representation-duplicate`: a representation already belongs to a phoneme or boundary, or is named twice, so no duplicate segment is created.
- `phoneme-representation-not-found`: a `from` is not a representation of the phoneme.
- `phoneme-representation-referenced`: an environment writes the `from` spelling; change that environment first.

To fold one phoneme into another use `compose-merge-phoneme`, and to move a spelling out again use `compose-split-phoneme`. To set the phonological features of a phoneme use [Set a phoneme's features](cmd:compose-edit-phoneme-features). The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

Representations are literal, so `(`, `)` and `/` can be added or respelled without environment escaping. [Author a phoneme](cmd:compose-author-phoneme) describes literal storage and the singleton-class route for textual environments. Keep case aliases such as `c`/`C` and `ng`/`Ng`/`NG` on the same phoneme so they share its features. Set a distinct feature bundle with [Set a phoneme's features](cmd:compose-edit-phoneme-features) when a literal must not unify with other sounds.

entries.title: Set a phoneme's features
entries.description: Stages feature values on an existing phoneme: set a value (a feature the phoneme already has takes the new value in place, one it lacks gains it) and clear features. A phoneme with no feature structure gets one. It refuses a value that does not belong to its feature, a feature both set and cleared, a clear of an absent feature and a change that alters nothing. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a phoneme's features

Stages feature values on one phoneme that exists. Use the closed input `{ "target": "<phoneme ID>", "set": [ { "feature": "<ID>", "value": "<ID>" } ], "clear": [ "<feature ID>" ] }` with at least one of `set` and `clear`. A feature the phoneme already has takes the new value in place, a feature it lacks gains a specification, and a phoneme with no feature structure gets one. A value that does not belong to its feature, a feature named in both lists, a `clear` of a feature the phoneme does not have, and a change that alters nothing are refused. Only a person can Apply.

```sh
motif compose-edit-phoneme-features --project language.fwdata --draft features \
  --intent '{"target":"<phoneme-id>","set":[{"feature":"<place-id>","value":"<labial-id>"}]}'
```

The features come from [Author a phonological feature](cmd:compose-author-phonological-feature). To give a new phoneme its features at the start, put `features` in [Author a phoneme](cmd:compose-author-phoneme) instead. A phoneme that carries no features is matched by a natural class defined by segments, never by a class defined by features. An archiphoneme is a phoneme like any other, so it can take features too (guide archiphonemes).

Features and values created earlier in the same Draft are available. In a [batch](cmd:compose-batch), a particular value from a multi-value feature can be named as `@identity:values:slash`; across calls use `lookup:phonological-feature:identity` and `lookup:phonological-feature-value:identity|slash`. No positional value selection is inferred.

entries.title: Edit a sound rule
entries.description: Changes one existing regular phonological rule in place, keeping its identity and position. Replace its ordered rightHandSides under an expected-current guard to add, remove or reorder outcomes with their own Output, contexts and rule features; feature changes and rule-wide alpha variables are preserved. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a sound rule

Use this command to change a regular rewrite rule that exists, in place. The rule keeps its identity and its place in the order. Edits of individual parts keep applicability sets; replacing the right-hand sides supplies those sets explicitly. Name only the parts to change; a part you leave out stays as it is.

```sh
motif compose-edit-phonological-rule --project language.fwdata --draft widen-rule \
  --intent '{"rule":"<rule-id>","right":[{"phoneme":"<u-id>","optional":true},{"phoneme":"<p-id>"}],"expected":{"right":[{"phoneme":"<p-id>"}]}}'
```

- `name`, `direction`, `input`, `output`, `left` and `right` are the same as in [Author a sound rule](cmd:compose-author-phonological-rule). Motif accepts up to eight phoneme or natural-class items in each Input and Output, in order; the two sides may have different lengths. A multi-member segment-list Output class does not choose a member: it applies only the features the members share, so the input keeps its own value for the rest, and Motif warns; an aligned feature-class Output changes only its specified features. Output also accepts `change` feature bundles and alpha `variables` as described in the feature-rules encoding guide. An empty list clears `left` or `right`, turns the rule into an insertion (empty `input`) or into a deletion (empty `output`).
- `expected` is a guard. Give the current value of any part you change; if the rule no longer matches, nothing is staged and the message names the part.
- A context item may be `optional` (zero or one time), or carry `minimum` and `maximum` (`-1` for no limit). Boundaries cannot repeat.

The command replaces the rule's contexts and keeps everything else. Use `rightHandSides` for a rule with multiple outcomes; the `output`, `left` and `right` shorthand is ambiguous there and is refused. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on words the rule should and should not change, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply. The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project.

For an agent, read `motif_grammar(kind="phonological_rules", detail="detailed")` first. Each rule has an `id` and an `intent` containing `name`, `direction`, `input`, `output`, `left` and `right`. Use the `id` as `rule` and copy the whole `intent` into `expected` when staging the edit through `motif_compose_batch` (verb `compose-edit-phonological-rule`), or `motif_edit_phonological_rule` in a profile that exposes it; the order of every item is checked. For example, change an Output of m d to n k while guarding the two current items:

```sh
motif compose-edit-phonological-rule --project language.fwdata --draft sequence-rule --intent '{"rule":"<rule-id>","output":[{"phoneme":"<n-id>"},{"phoneme":"<k-id>"}],"expected":{"output":[{"phoneme":"<m-id>"},{"phoneme":"<d-id>"}]}}'
```

A detailed read also returns `rightHandSideCount`. An `intent` of null means a context or applicability reference cannot be represented by this composer. Multiple right-hand sides return all outcomes in order, including each case's required and excluded features and input categories.

Feature and alpha rules read back faithfully. The returned variable names are stored constraint identities: reuse those names in replacement parts to preserve sharing with Input or contexts you leave in place. A variable may occur once or have only negative references; replacing Input when it holds every reference can recreate its stored identity while preserving sharing. Read `motif help guide:encoding/feature-rules --full` for feature change, polarity and parser limitations.

## Add, remove or reorder outcomes

Read the complete intent first. Replace `rightHandSides` with the complete desired sequence and give `expected.rightHandSides` exactly as read. For example, to keep only the second outcome, copy that complete outcome object into a one-item replacement list and retain the original list in `expected`. To reorder, permute the replacement list. The rule identity, position and disabled flag stay; the right-hand-side objects are recreated atomically, including their contexts and feature references.

An unrestricted single-outcome read retains the older `output`, `left`, `right` form. Guard all three together when converting it to `rightHandSides`, or express those three parts as one outcome under `expected.rightHandSides`. Omitted contexts and applicability sets within each replacement outcome become empty. `inputCategories` contains part-of-speech ids; a nonempty set admits those categories and their subcategories. Required and excluded feature sets contain exception feature or inflection class ids. Copy these fields when retaining a case's restrictions. A stale context, Output, case order, category or feature set refuses before staging any operations.

Input, direction and name can be edited on their own even when the rule has several right-hand sides. A complete replacement has one or more outcomes, and cannot be mixed with the single-outcome Output/context shorthand. The first applicable outcome wins; use an Output natural class for free lexical alternatives rather than overlapping cases. Dry Run and Trial both alternatives and untagged controls.

entries.title: Set rule features
entries.description: Sets the exact exception features or inflection classes a phonological rewrite rule requires of a stem, and the ones it excludes. An empty list clears a set. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set rule features

Use this command to limit a regular rewrite rule by exception features or inflection classes. It sets the exact set the word must carry for the rule to apply, and the exact set it must not carry. An empty list clears a set; a set you leave out stays as it is.

```sh
motif compose-edit-phonological-rule-features --project language.fwdata --draft rule-features \
  --intent '{"rule":"<rule-id>","excludedFeatures":["<feature-id>"]}'
```

- `requiredFeatures`: the word must carry all of them. A rule that requires none applies to every word.
- `excludedFeatures`: the word must carry none of them.
- Each id is an exception feature from the project's Exception Features list or an inflection class. A feature cannot be both required and excluded.

Tag the stems first with `compose-edit-exception-features`. FieldWorks keeps a rule feature item for each feature a rule uses; the command creates it when it is missing. This is the principled way to make a sound change skip a few stems before you write a separate rule or a duplicate stem (Black 2025, section 6.1.2.2.2).

This shorthand addresses a regular rewrite rule with one right-hand side. For multiple outcomes, use [Edit a sound rule](cmd:compose-edit-phonological-rule) with a guarded complete `rightHandSides` sequence; set `requiredFeatures` and `excludedFeatures` separately within each outcome. The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on words the rule should and should not change, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Set a stem allomorph's name
entries.description: Sets or clears the stem name of one stem allomorph after checking the expected current stem name. The name must belong to a stem category of the entry or an ancestor; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a stem allomorph's name

Change the stem name of an existing stem allomorph, so that the allomorph is used only for the inflectional features its stem name selects. The expected value is the stored stem name, or `null` when the allomorph has none.

```sh
motif compose-edit-stem-allomorph-stem-name --project language.fwdata --draft plural-stems \
  --intent '{"target":"<stem-allomorph-id>","expectedStemName":null,"stemName":"<stem-name-id>"}'
```

All three intent fields are required. `expectedStemName` and `stemName` are each either a canonical id or `null`. The target must be a stem allomorph, either the lexeme form or an alternate form of its entry. The desired stem name must belong to the part of speech of one of the entry's stem analyses, or to an ancestor of it; an entry with no stem analysis that has a part of speech is refused. Setting `stemName` to `null` clears the stem name. When the expected and desired values are the same, the command adds no operations.

Use this editor through the CLI; it is not exposed as an MCP tool.

Use a stem name id returned by an earlier composition in the same Draft directly in `stemName`. The Draft composer declares the dependency from that reference. This edit creates no stem name.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects and run a Trial on affected words before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Set a stem's class
entries.description: Sets or clears the inflection class of one stem analysis after checking the expected current class. The class must belong to the stem's part of speech or an ancestor; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a stem's class

Change the inflection class of an existing stem analysis. The expected value is the stored class, or `null` when the analysis has none.

```sh
motif compose-edit-stem-inflection-class --project language.fwdata --draft numerals \
  --intent '{"target":"<stem-analysis-id>","expectedInflectionClass":null,"inflectionClass":"<class-id>"}'
```

All three intent fields are required. `expectedInflectionClass` and `inflectionClass` are each either a canonical id or `null`. The target must be a stem analysis with a part of speech. The desired class must belong to that part of speech or one of its ancestors. Setting `inflectionClass` to `null` clears the class. When the expected and desired values are the same, the command adds no operations.

Use this editor through the CLI; it is not exposed as an MCP tool.

Use a class id returned by an earlier composition in the same Draft directly in `inflectionClass`. The Draft composer declares the dependency from that reference. This edit creates no class.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects and run a Trial on affected words before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Edit the Notes of existing text segments
entries.description: Stages, in bulk, the replacement of the Notes of segments in existing Texts: each edit names a Text, a segment or a word in it, and the one Note the segment is to hold. Apply refuses a segment whose Notes, in any writing system, changed since the edit was composed. Other Notes of the segment are removed. Give one intent with many edits, or --notes-tsv, never one intent per edit. A Trial reparses nothing of the grammar. Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit the Notes of existing text segments

Sets or replaces the Notes of segments in Texts that already exist, in bulk, without creating a new Text. Each edit names a Text (its name, or its id when two Texts share a name), a segment or a word, and the Note. The segment then holds exactly that one Note: the first existing Note keeps its identity and its text in the analysis writing system is replaced, and any other Notes of the segment are removed, with whatever text they hold in other writing systems. Free and Literal Translations, words and the baseline are untouched.

```sh
motif compose-edit-text-notes --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"edits":[{"text":"Tracking","word":"balay","note":"loan: Spanish"},{"text":"Tracking","segment":12,"note":"proper name"}]}'
```

`segment` is the 1-based number of the segment counted across all paragraphs of the Text. `word` is a form in NFD; it must occur in exactly one segment of that Text, otherwise the edit is refused and names the segment numbers to choose from. Two edits for one segment are refused. Notes are written in `analysisWs` when given, otherwise in the project's default analysis writing system.

For thousands of edits, use one intent with many edits, not one intent per edit; either put the intent in a file and give a tab-separated file, or use a single `compose-batch` entry whose intent holds all the edits. Thousands of separate intents are slow, because each one is composed on its own.

Give a tab-separated file of `Text<TAB>segment-number-or-word<TAB>Note` lines instead of `--intent` (the two cannot be combined):

```sh
motif compose-edit-text-notes --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft --notes-tsv notes.tsv [--analysis-ws en]
```

The file may start with the exact header line `Text<TAB>Locator<TAB>Note` (any capitalization), which is skipped; a first line that differs from it is data. A locator of digits that is a whole number is a segment, anything else a word, so a numeric word is addressed by its segment. There is no quoting: a cell holds no tab or line break, and quote marks stay in the Note. Blank lines are skipped.

All unresolved or ambiguous edits are reported together, each named by its edit number (or TSV line), so one run lists everything to fix.

Each staged operation remembers every Note's text in every writing system. If a segment's Notes change in any of them before Apply, that Apply is refused (`text-notes.stale-source`) and you compose the edit again. The Dry Run lists every segment changed; a Notes-only Proposal changes no grammar and no parse, so its Trial measures only the words of the edited segments and matches the baseline. Only a person can Apply the Proposal. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record a source on every operation.
usage: Usage: motif compose-edit-text-notes --draft <name> --project <fwdata> --intent '<closed intent JSON>', or --notes-tsv <file> [--analysis-ws <tag>] in place of --intent [--cite-source <text> [--cite-locator <text>]]

entries.title: Link a variant
entries.description: Links a variant reference to its main entry or sense and sets its variant type. Self-links and cycles are refused; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Link a variant

Link an existing variant reference to its main entry or sense and set its variant type. The command replaces the reference's current component targets and types with the ones named; any extra components and types are dropped.

```sh
motif compose-link-variant --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"target":"<variant-reference-id>","component":"<main-entry-or-sense-id>","variantType":"<variant-type-id>"}'
```

All three fields are required. The type must be in the project's variant types list. The command refuses self-links and cycles, and checks again when the Proposal runs. If the reference changes after composing, compose it again. Review the Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal. The CLI and MCP both stage a Draft; MCP cannot Apply it.

This command only edits a reference that already exists. To link two entries that have no variant reference between them yet, use [Make an entry a variant](cmd:compose-make-variant-of), which works on two existing entries and creates the reference.

entries.title: Make an entry a variant
entries.description: Makes an existing entry, or one created earlier in the Draft, a variant of another entry or sense by creating its variant reference with a variant type, as Add Variant does in FieldWorks. Self-links, cycles and a second link to the same component are refused; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Make an entry a variant

Make an existing entry, or one created earlier in the same Draft, a variant of another entry or sense. The command creates the entry's variant reference with the variant type and the main entry or sense as its component, as Add Variant does in FieldWorks. The reference has no primary lexemes and the minor entry stays shown unless `hideMinorEntry` is true.

```sh
motif compose-make-variant-of --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"entry":"<variant-entry-id>","component":"<main-entry-or-sense-id>","variantType":"<variant-type-id>"}'
```

`entry`, `component` and `variantType` are required; `hideMinorEntry` (true or false, default false) hides the variant's minor entry. The type must be in the project's variant types list. The command refuses an entry that is its own main entry, a link that would form a cycle, and a second variant reference from the entry to the same component; to change the type of an existing reference, use `compose-link-variant`. It checks again when the Proposal runs. Review the Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal. The CLI and MCP both stage a Draft; MCP cannot Apply it.

entries.title: Make many entries variants
entries.description: Makes many existing entries variants of their main entries or senses in one step, all with one variant type, such as cross-reference stubs that should be variants. Every link is checked against the project and the links before it, and a refusal names the link and the blocking object; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Make many entries variants

Make many existing entries variants of their main entries or senses in one step, all with one variant type. It is the bulk form of [`compose-make-variant-of`](cmd:compose-make-variant-of), for a project that holds many cross-reference stubs that should be variants.

```sh
motif compose-make-variants-of --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"variantType":"<variant-type-id>","onlyStubs":true,"links":[{"entry":"<stub-id>","component":"<main-entry-or-sense-id>"}]}'
```

`variantType` and `links` are required; each link needs `entry` and `component`. Every link is checked as `compose-make-variant-of` checks one, and also against the links before it in the same list, so two links that together form a cycle are refused. A refusal names the link's position and the objects that block it, and nothing is added. With `onlyStubs` true, an entry that has a sense with content is refused and the sense and field are named.

The command links only. To remove a stub's empty senses afterwards, use `compose-delete-empty-sense`. Review the Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal. The CLI and MCP both stage a Draft; MCP cannot Apply it.

entries.title: Merge a boundary marker
entries.description: Points every rule or environment that uses a stray duplicate of the word or morpheme boundary marker at the standard marker, then removes the duplicate, so a rule with a boundary can be authored again. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Merge a duplicate boundary marker

Use this command when a project holds a second copy of the word boundary (`#`) or morpheme boundary (`+`) marker that rules or environments already use. It points every such use at the standard marker and removes the copy, which clears the refusal that blocks rules with a boundary.

```sh
motif compose-merge-boundary-markers --project language.fwdata --draft boundary-merge \
  --intent '{"marker":"<stray-marker-id>"}'
```

`marker` is required. If nothing uses the copy, `compose-retire-boundary-marker` does the same without re-pointing. The command refuses the standard marker, a marker that is not a duplicate of `#` or `+`, and a marker used by anything other than a boundary context. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Merge entries
entries.description: Merges one entry into another so the two become one entry, as Merge Entry does in FieldWorks: the merged entry's senses, grammatical info and alternate forms move to the entry that stays, its lexeme form joins the other's or becomes an alternate form, and every reference to it points at the entry that stays; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply. It refuses an entry merged into itself or an id that is not an entry.
entries.helpPage:
# Merge entries

Merge one entry into another so the two become one entry. Use it when two entries are the same word, for example a duplicate left by an import or a spelling variant that is better kept as an alternate form. It is the Merge Entry of FieldWorks, run by LibLCM's own entry merge.

```sh
motif compose-merge-lexical-entries --project language.fwdata --draft duplicates \
  --intent '{"entry":"<entry-to-merge-id>","into":"<entry-that-stays-id>"}'
```

`entry` and `into` are required and the intent is closed. The entry named by `entry` ceases to exist; the entry named by `into` stays.

What the merge does, as FieldWorks does it with no text lost:

- The senses, grammatical info (analyses) and alternate forms of the merged entry are added to the entry that stays.
- When the two lexeme forms differ in text, the merged entry's lexeme form becomes an alternate form of the entry that stays; when they are equal, they become one form.
- Every reference to the merged entry, such as a variant, complex form, lexical relation or parser analysis, points at the entry that stays. References between the two entries themselves are dropped, because an entry cannot refer to itself.
- Equal alternate forms and equal analyses become one.
- Text fields that differ are joined; a field that only the merged entry has is copied.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when `entry` and `into` are the same entry or when either id is not an entry. Different lexeme-form classes and morph types are allowed, as in FieldWorks. When their text differs, even a stem merged into an affix keeps its form as an alternate form of the surviving entry.

The Dry Run lists the merged entry's headword, forms, senses, analyses and entry references and the entry they join. Entry text in every writing system, including custom fields, is bound to the Dry Run; editing it afterward requires a fresh Dry Run. The preview shows the merged entry leaving the lexicon.

Use this editor through the CLI or the matching MCP tool, which only stages. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Merge a phoneme into another
entries.description: Stages a merge of one phoneme into another: each spelling of the first becomes another way to write the second, and the first phoneme is removed from the inventory and from its natural classes. It refuses a spelling another phoneme has, a natural class the first phoneme alone fills, and a rule or environment that uses the first phoneme. Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Merge a phoneme into another

Use this command when two phonemes are really one sound that the language writes two ways, such as a vowel written `u` and `o`. The first phoneme (the source) is merged into the second (the target): every spelling of the source is added to the target after the target's own, and the source is removed. Use `compose-edit-phoneme` instead to add a spelling no phoneme has yet.

```sh
motif compose-merge-phoneme --project language.fwdata --draft sounds \
  --intent '{"source":"<phoneme-id-to-remove>","target":"<phoneme-id-to-keep>"}'
```

The intent has exactly `source` and `target`. The Dry Run lists the natural classes the source leaves, and the Proposal shows the removal of the source and each spelling added to the target.

What changes and what does not:

- The target keeps its identity, its features and its natural classes. They now describe the merged sound.
- The source leaves every natural class it is in. It is not added to the target's classes, so no class gains a member the language did not give it.
- The source's features are discarded with it. Check them before you merge.
- Each moved spelling is a new representation on the target; its identity is not the source's.
- Words and environments keep their text. A word spelled with a moved spelling reads as the target.

Refusal messages begin with a stable name:

- `phoneme-merge-same`: the source and the target are one phoneme.
- `phoneme-not-in-inventory`: a phoneme is not in the first phoneme set.
- `phoneme-merge-nothing-to-move`: the source has no spelling to move.
- `phoneme-merge-code-conflict`: a spelling of the source also belongs to another phoneme or boundary, the target included. Fix the spelling with `compose-edit-phoneme` first.
- `phoneme-merge-class-would-empty`: the source is the only member of a natural class. Edit or remove that class first.
- `phoneme-merge-referenced`: an environment writes a spelling of the source, or a rule or another object uses the source. Merging would widen what it matches, so change it first.

To take a merge back, apply `compose-split-phoneme`. The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Move an example to another sense
entries.description: Moves one example sentence, with its translations, from its sense to another sense, which may belong to another entry, keeping its identity; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply. It refuses an example that any other object refers to, a move to the sense that already owns it, an unknown example or sense, and a neighbour that is not an example of the target sense.
entries.helpPage:
# Move an example to another sense

Move one example sentence, with its translations, from its sense to another sense. The target sense may belong to a different entry. Use it when a duplicate meaning is about to be deleted with `compose-delete-sense` but holds examples the surviving meaning lacks.

```sh
motif compose-move-example --project language.fwdata --draft ceb-d004 \
  --intent '{"example":"<example-id>","toSense":"<sense-id>"}'
```

`example` and `toSense` are required and the intent is closed. `after` or `before`, never both, name an example of the target sense to place the moved one next to; without either it goes last.

The example keeps its identity, text in every writing system, reference and translations; only its owning sense changes, as LibLCM allows. FieldWorks itself offers no such move, so nothing here copies the example: the old sense no longer has it.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when:

- the example or the sense does not exist, or the ids name other kinds of object;
- the target sense is the sense that already owns the example;
- anything outside the example refers to it, such as an annotation or a relation; what such a reference means can depend on the sense that owns the example, so the message names the referrer and it must be removed or retargeted first;
- `after` or `before` is not an example of the target sense.

The target sense may be created by an earlier step of the same Draft. The Dry Run lists, for the old and the new sense, their examples before and after, and shows the full example in every writing system with its translations, the old sense with its entry and gloss, and the target sense with its entry and gloss.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Move a sense to a new entry
entries.description: Moves one sense, with its sub-senses and examples, out of its entry into a new entry of its own, so a derived word folded into its root as a sense gets its own lexeme form and analysis; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Move a sense to a new entry

Move one sense of an entry, with its glosses, definitions, examples and sub-senses, into a new entry of its own. Use it when an import folded a derived word into its root as a sense, such as `kaayu` inside `ayu`: the word gets its own lexeme form and analysis, and the root keeps its other senses.

```sh
motif compose-move-sense-to-entry --project language.fwdata --draft ceb-d002 \
  --intent '{"sense":"<sense-id>","form":"kaayu","formWs":"ceb","morphType":"<stem-morph-type-id>"}'
```

`sense`, `form`, `formWs` and `morphType` are required, and the intent is closed. `msa` is optional and takes the same shape as `compose-author-lexical-entry`: a `kind` (`stem`, `inflectional`, `derivational` or `unclassified`) with its `category`, and `toCategory`, `slots` or `inflectionClass` where the kind has them. Without `msa` the new entry gets a copy of the sense's own analysis, which is what FieldWorks' "move sense to a copy of its entry" does. A copy is refused when the analysis has no category, or carries anything a copy would drop, such as features; give `msa` then.

The sense keeps its identity. It becomes the only sense of the new entry, and it and its sub-senses point at the new entry's analysis. The old entry's analysis is removed only when no remaining sense uses it and nothing else refers to it, so the root stays valid.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when:

- the sense is the only sense of its entry, unless the entry stays a variant of an entry or sense that has a stem analysis (see `compose-delete-sense`);
- the sense is a sub-sense; only a top-level sense moves;
- a sub-sense has an analysis different from the sense's own;
- a parser analysis (morph bundle) still refers to the sense, because its morph and analysis would no longer match; retarget it first;
- the morph type and the analysis disagree, for example a stem analysis on a suffix.

A Draft may move several senses out of one root. Each move is composed against the Draft's earlier steps, so the second move sees the first one's result. The Dry Run lists the old entry's senses, the new entry's senses and the sense's analysis; each operation carries a rationale, and the Draft still needs its own (`proposal rationale`) before Finalize.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Reorder sound rules
entries.description: Moves phonological rules to a new order, with the fewest moves, so a later rule sees the output of the earlier ones. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Reorder sound rules

Use this command to change the order in which phonological rules apply. A later rule sees the output of the earlier ones, so order decides whether a chain such as a class-to-nasal rule and a nasal deletion works at all.

```sh
motif compose-order-phonological-rules --project language.fwdata --draft rule-order \
  --intent '{"rule":"<rule-id>","before":"<other-rule-id>"}'
```

Give either one move (`rule` with `before` or `after`) or the whole new order (`order`, every rule once). The command plans the fewest moves and refuses an unknown rule, an incomplete order, or an order that changes nothing. Rules keep their contexts, features and disabled state.

Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on a word that needs the chain, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Stage a Parsimony disposition
entries.description: Stages a keep, fix, ask, or defer decision for one exact Parsimony finding in a Draft Proposal. A pending keep does not suppress current findings, and only a person can Apply it.
entries.helpPage:
# Stage a Parsimony disposition

Use this command to stage a decision about one finding in a Draft Proposal. The intent names an existing Notebook record type, the finding's exact subject and evidence digest, and one disposition: `keep`, `fix`, `ask`, or `defer`. A reason is optional; `ask` requires a question.

```sh
motif compose-record-parsimony-disposition --project language.fwdata --draft review-one --intent '{"recordTypeId":"...","measureId":"P-allo-duplicate-form","subject":{},"disposition":"keep","evidenceDigest":"...","evidenceContract":"...","subjectCaption":"...","measureCaption":"...","reason":"..."}'
```

The command appends bounded Notebook and reserved-field operations to the Draft. Review the Proposal with Dry Run before a human Applies it. A pending keep does not change the live findings; it becomes project data only after Apply and a later Refresh.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Stage a source-validated decision
entries.description: Stages, in a Draft, a decision a named program made from cited sources: an approval or disapproval of one existing analysis under a non-human agent, or the evidence for a wordform or analysis alone. It is never a person's decision and never sets spelling status; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Stage a source-validated decision

`compose-record-source-validated-decision` stages a decision that a named program, not a person, made from cited sources. It has two forms.

To approve or disapprove an analysis, give the existing analysis as `target`, an `agent` (a `name` and the `version` of the source release it stands for) and a `member` of `approves` or `disapproves`. FieldWorks will show the decision under that non-human agent. A person's approvals and disapprovals are never touched, and a new release of the sources is a new agent. Agents are told apart by name and version, so if release 1 approved an analysis and release 2 disapproves it, `difference produce --reference source-validated` marks the word `conflicting-decisions` and counts neither; stage the later release only after you have decided what to do with the earlier one.

To record why a word form is wrong or right without deciding anything in FieldWorks, give the wordform or analysis as `target` and leave `agent` and `member` out. This never changes spelling status, which stays a person's.

Either way, `evidence` says why: a `tier` (for example `source-approved`, `misspelled-typo` or `ill-formed`), the cited `sources` (a dictionary, a grammar, a corpus or an example, each with an optional locator) and the facts the tier requires: a typo needs `intendedForm` and `editType`, an ill-formed word needs `violatedRule`, a nonstandard variant needs `standardForm`, and a source-approved analysis needs a dictionary, a grammar and a corpus source. Read the records back with `evidence show`.

Motif stages the change in a Draft for a person to review. Only a person can Apply.

entries.title: Relink natural-class users
entries.description: Moves explicitly named environments and rewrite-rule contexts to a replacement class created earlier in the Draft. Other users remain on the source class. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Relink natural-class users

Use this command when a class should keep its current meaning for most of the grammar, but selected users need a new class. It changes only the environment and rewrite-rule contexts you name.

```sh
motif compose-relink-natural-class --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"source":"<sourceClassId>","replacement":"<newClassId>","replacementCreationOperation":"<createOperationId>","environments":[{"target":"<environmentId>","expectedLeft":[{"naturalClass":"<sourceClassId>"}],"expectedRight":[]}],"ruleContexts":["<ruleContextId>"]}'
```

Create the replacement class earlier in the same Draft and use both its entity id and the operation id returned by that create. Each environment entry supplies its exact current typed left and right contexts; Motif compares their rendering with the saved environment string before replacing the source-class references. Each listed rule context must currently point to the source class. Unlisted users stay on the source class; the composer response lists the current users so you can review the declared scope, and the Dry Run records the actual references that change.

Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run to confirm the intended scope, and run a bounded Trial across corrected, held-out and contrastive forms. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Remove an alternate form
entries.description: Removes one alternate form (allomorph) of an entry that nothing refers to; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply. It refuses the lexeme form and a form that a parser analysis or any other object refers to.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove an alternate form

Remove one alternate form (allomorph) of an entry. Use it when an alternate form stands in for something that now has its own entry, or is redundant.

```sh
motif compose-remove-alternate-form --project language.fwdata --draft ceb-d004 \
  --intent '{"entry":"<entry-id>","form":"<form-id>"}'
```

`entry` and `form` are required and the intent is closed. The form must be an alternate form owned by the entry; the lexeme form cannot be removed this way.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when anything refers to the form: a morph bundle of a parser analysis, an ad hoc prohibition, or any other object. The message names the referrer; retarget or remove that reference first. The Dry Run shows the entry's alternate forms before and after and a preview of the removed form, with its class, its text in every writing system, its morph type, its position and its number of environments. A writing system the project cannot resolve is shown by its numeric handle.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Remove exception feature
entries.description: Takes one exception feature off every stem that carries it and out of every phonological rule branch that requires or excludes it, then deletes the feature, in one Proposal, and reports the counts first. Affix restrictions are counted, not edited. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove exception feature

Use this command to take one exception feature out of the grammar's uses in one step: every stem that carries it, and every phonological rule branch that requires or excludes it. It reports the counts first.

```sh
motif compose-remove-exception-feature --project language.fwdata --draft drop-retains \
  --intent '{"feature":"<feature-id>","expectedName":"Retains initial cluster"}'
```

`expectedName` must match the feature's current name in some writing system, so a stale id is refused. `keepFeature: true` removes the references but leaves the feature in the Exception Features list.

The command finds the references in one pass over the analyses and the rules, so its cost grows with their number and it starts no parser. It then deletes the feature and its Phonological Rule Features wrapper in the same Proposal, as FieldWorks does when you delete an exception feature, unless you keep it or an affix still names it.

Read the output before you finalize:

- **Affixes.** It does not edit affix From or To Exception Features. An affix that requires the removed feature matches no stem afterwards and its readings disappear. The output counts these analyses and keeps the feature; edit them with `compose-edit-exception-features` or `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction`.
- **Widening.** A rule branch that required only this feature applies to every stem afterwards; the output warns you.

Run a Trial after Dry Run. The Trial prints the reading-identity proof (ADR 0115) for the words it parsed: how many words kept the same readings, and each reading lost or newly allowed.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Finalize the Proposal for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Remove a feature value
entries.description: Stages the removal of one feature's specification from a stem's MsFeatures, an inflectional affix's InflFeats, or a derivational affix's FromMsFeatures or ToMsFeatures, so the stem stops carrying the feature or the affix stops requiring or giving it. The feature structure stays. Refuses a feature the structure does not specify. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove a feature value

Use this command to take one feature's specification off a feature structure: a stem's MsFeatures, so the stem no longer carries the feature, or an inflectional affix's InflFeats, so the affix no longer requires it. It undoes [authoring a feature value](cmd:compose-author-feature-value).

```sh
motif compose-remove-feature-value --project language.fwdata --draft agreement \
  --intent '{"featStruc":"<feature-structure-id>","feature":"<feature-id>"}'
```

The intent has exactly `featStruc` and `feature`. The structure stays even when it ends up empty; an empty structure requires nothing. To change a value, remove the specification and author the new one in a later Draft step, because a second specification for the same feature is refused while the first exists.

Refusal messages contain a stable name:

- `feature-value-not-found`: the structure has no specification for that feature.
- `feature-structure-not-grammatical-info`: the structure belongs to none of a stem, an inflectional affix or a derivational affix.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Retire an affix slot
entries.description: Deletes an inflectional affix slot that no affix analysis and no template uses any more. It refuses a slot still in use and names what uses it; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Retire an affix slot

Delete an inflectional affix slot that nothing uses any more.

```sh
motif compose-retire-affix-slot --project language.fwdata --draft slot-cleanup \
  --intent '{"slot":"<slot-id>"}'
```

`slot` is required and the intent is closed. The command refuses, changing nothing, while any inflectional affix analysis still names the slot or any affix template still lists it, and the message says how many of each. Move the affixes to another slot with `compose-edit-inflectional-affix` and take the slot out of its templates with `compose-edit-affix-template` first, in the same Draft or an earlier one; nothing is reassigned or cascaded for you.

A template that loses its last slot is allowed, and the grammar check then warns that the template has no slots. Use `compose-edit-affix-slot` to rename a slot or change whether it is optional instead of retiring it.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite the operation. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Retire a boundary marker
entries.description: Removes a stray duplicate of the word or morpheme boundary marker from the first phoneme set, so a phonological rule with a boundary can be authored again. It refuses the standard marker and any marker a rule, environment or other object still uses; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Retire a duplicate boundary marker

Remove a stray second copy of the word boundary (`#`) or morpheme boundary (`+`) marker from the first phoneme set. Motif refuses to author a rule with a boundary while the set holds two markers for the same boundary, because it cannot tell which one the rule should name; retiring the unused copy clears that refusal.

```sh
motif compose-retire-boundary-marker --project language.fwdata --draft boundary-fix \
  --intent '{"marker":"<marker-id>"}'
```

`marker` is required and the intent is closed. The refusal that sends you here names the stray marker and the standard marker the rule must use. The command retires only a marker whose every spelling is `#` or `+` and whose standard marker, with the same spelling, is still in the set. It refuses the standard marker itself, and refuses, changing nothing, when any rule, environment or other object still refers to the marker; the message names the referrer. Retarget that use to the standard marker in FieldWorks first. Nothing is retargeted or cascaded for you.

The Dry Run shows the phoneme set's boundary markers before and after. Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to cite the operation. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Rewrite lexeme forms
entries.description: Rewrites existing lexeme forms with expected-current guards while preserving their identities and references. Give explicit new forms to retain underlying distinctions until ordered grammar rules realize running spelling; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Rewrite lexeme forms

```sh
motif compose-rewrite-lexeme-form --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"foldStressMarks":false,"entries":[{"entryGuid":"<id>","writingSystem":"qaa","expectedForm":"pata","newForm":"pātaʔ"}]}'
```

Rewrites the lexeme forms of existing entries, many in one Draft, preserving each form's identity, references, conditions and other writing-system alternatives. Each entry names its writing system and the `expectedForm` it holds now; a different current form refuses the whole batch and stages nothing. Give an explicit `newForm` with `foldStressMarks=false` to restore an underlying distinction from selected evidence.

A parser form may carry represented segments, vowel quantity or lexical stress that running spelling omits. Keep the form nonabstract and each phoneme's representation nonempty. Morphology and sound rules use those distinctions before final ordered rules realize the unmarked written word. Marked dictionary spellings may stay in Citation Form. Restoring information requires source evidence; the command cannot infer missing stops or quantity from plain spelling.

The initial proof targets unmarked running text using simultaneous regular rules ordered on Morphology, with empty Clitics and Surface strata, `NotOnClitics=true`, empty `HC/Strata` and `HC/DelReapps=0` (the FieldWorks default). A value of 0 still permits inverse deletion. Attached clitics and multiple cycles require separately proved domains. PanGloss 0.15.2 completes the generic `patʔa` → `pat-a` proof; the reference hc.dll hangs beyond 600 seconds on `pat-a` with the full simultaneous chain, so parity for that case is unproved.

The legacy `foldStressMarks` option computes the new form from `expectedForm` and requires `newForm` to be omitted: decompose to NFD, remove only U+0300 (grave), U+0301 (acute), U+0302 (circumflex), U+0304 (macron) and U+030C (caron), recompose to NFC. Every other mark, such as the tilde of n-tilde, is kept. This is a destructive spelling fold, not a phonological realization. In Wolff's Cebuano notation acute marks length, grave marks a following glottal stop, and caron marks exceptional stress. Do not fold a distinction needed by the grammar; retaining it only in Citation Form cannot condition parsing.

`setEmptyCitationForm` copies the old lexeme spelling into an empty Citation Form in that writing system. It leaves an existing Citation Form alone and skips an entry whose lexeme form would not change. To preserve a different selected source headword, use [Edit a citation form](cmd:compose-edit-citation-form). To edit an existing ordinary alternate, use [Edit an allomorph form](cmd:compose-edit-allomorph-form).

The command stages writes in the Draft. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run and Trial the actual written words; only a person can Apply a Proposal. A spelling-only result cannot prove quantity or stress erased before output.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on the operations this command produces.

entries.title: Set a character's class
entries.description: Stages one change that makes named characters of a project writing system part of a word or punctuation, such as making the curly quotes punctuation so they stop being part of a word. The Trial re-reads the Texts with the changed writing system; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a character's class

```sh
motif compose-set-character-class --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"ws":"ceb","class":"punctuation","characters":"\u2018\u2019"}'
```

Moves the named characters of one project writing system between word-forming (part of a word) and punctuation (not part of a word). `class` is `wordForming` or `punctuation`; `characters` lists the characters together, one visible character each. Motif refuses punctuation for a letter, mark or modifier, because no writing-system setting can make one so.

The command stages one write in the Draft. It does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and Trial the affected Texts: the Trial re-reads them with the changed writing system, so a word such as `‘baba’` becomes `baba`. Review the after Report; only a person can Apply a Proposal. Apply writes the project's writing-system file and re-reads the Texts that contain the changed characters.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on the operation this command produces.

entries.title: Set entry parsing flag
entries.description: Stages the FieldWorks do-not-parse flag on a lexical entry. The flag does not stop the entry parsing: PanGloss, FieldWorks HermitCrab and XAmple all parse a flagged entry, whole entry and not just compounds; to stop a stem parsing, retype it with compose-set-stem-part-of-speech or delete it.
entries.helpPage:
# Set entry parsing flag

```sh
motif compose-set-entry-do-not-parse --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<entry-id>","expectedDoNotParse":false,"doNotParse":true}'
```

This stages the FieldWorks `DoNotUseForParsing` flag on one lexical entry. Its intended scope is the entire entry, including its morphs and analyses: it is not a restriction on compounds alone. Set `doNotParse` to `false` to clear it. The composer refuses a missing or wrong-type target and an `expectedDoNotParse` value that does not match the saved project.

Neither FieldWorks' HermitCrab nor its XAmple transform reads this flag, and PanGloss parses a flagged entry too, so the flag changes no parse, in a Trial or in FieldWorks. It is only a note kept in the project and is not a way to retire an entry. To stop a stem parsing, retype it to the category it belongs to with `compose-set-stem-part-of-speech` (a particle, determiner or interjection takes no inflection or derivation), or delete the entry; otherwise disable the rule or template that lets it parse. Setting the flag deletes nothing, and a Proposal that sets `doNotParse` back to `false` (with `expectedDoNotParse` `true`) clears it.

To flag many entries in one Proposal, put one `compose-set-entry-do-not-parse` intent per entry in a [`compose-batch`](cmd:compose-batch) file; but to change how words parse, retype the stems the same way instead.

The command stages a change in the Draft; it does not change the project. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record a source on the operation. Only a person can Apply a Proposal.

entries.title: Set default compounding
entries.description: Stages one explicit change to the parser's built-in default compounding in a Draft.
