Use `--wait-timeout-ms` to set the wait bound. Omit `--wait` to receive the queued job id.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) queues the same review without waiting.
- [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) opens a stored result.
- [List Parsimony measures](cmd:parsimony%20measures) shows registered checks and views.

entries.title: Stage a finding disposition
entries.description: Stages a keep, fix, ask, or defer decision from one finding in a stored Parsimony Report. It derives the exact subject and evidence from that finding and appends the existing Notebook operations to a Draft Proposal. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Stage a finding disposition

```sh
motif parsimony dispose --project language.fwdata --report <reportId> --finding <findingId> \
  --disposition keep|fix|ask|defer --record-type <portableId> --draft <name> \
  [--reason <text>] [--question <text>] [--json]
```

This command reads one finding from a stored Parsimony Report and derives its exact subject, evidence digest, evidence contract, and readable captions. The Report must belong to the project's current Baseline; a Report measured just before an Apply can still answer that its decision is already recorded, but it cannot stage a new one. `--record-type` must be a portable ID from `parsimony record-types`. Supply `--question` only with `--disposition ask`.

The command appends the existing Notebook judgment operations to a Draft Proposal. Review them with Dry Run, then a person uses `apply` to write the judgment to FieldWorks. When the bound Dry Run shows only these Notebook effects, Readiness does not require a Correctness Assessment because the judgment cannot change parsing. A mixed Proposal keeps the normal Assessment requirement. A pending keep does not suppress a current finding.

The same decision is never staged twice. Two dispositions are the same decision when they agree on the finding's subject, measure and evidence, the disposition, the reason and the question; the record type, and the Report and the Draft they came from, do not count.

- If the saved project already holds this decision as its current judgment, the command succeeds and stages nothing. It prints `This decision is already recorded; nothing was staged in draft '<name>'.`, and with `--json` the response's `outcome` is `already-recorded` and its operation list is empty.
- If the Draft already stages this decision, the command is refused with `parsimony.decision-already-staged`: `This decision is already staged in Draft '<name>'.`
- If the finding ID names more than one finding in the Report, the command is refused with `parsimony.finding-ambiguous` and stages nothing, because no single finding can be disposed.

entries.title: Read Parsimony expectations
entries.description: Reads human-confirmed negatives and native Approved and Disapproved readings from the saved FieldWorks project. The versioned projection keeps surface negatives, exact reading negatives, and native Opinions separate for later Parsimony measures and paired verification.
entries.helpPage:
# Read Parsimony expectations

```sh
motif parsimony expectations --project language.fwdata [--json]
```

Reads the saved project's `parsimony-expectations/v1` projection. It lists human-confirmed [reviewed negatives](term:reviewed-negative) by case and revision, then reports FieldWorks' default-human Approved and Disapproved readings in separate sections. Native Disapproved Opinions reject one exact reading and do not become whole-word negatives.

Conflicts and unavailable identities are included in `issues`; callers must not count them as qualified evidence. This command reads the FieldWorks project and does not run PanGloss or change it.

entries.title: Find the newest Report
entries.description: Names the newest stored Parsimony Report and the bundle it was measured from. It reads the project's store only and does not run PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Find the newest Report

`parsimony latest` names the newest stored Parsimony Report for a project and the bundle it was measured from. It reads the project's store only and does not invoke PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony latest --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

The response returns `reportId` and `bundleId`. Pass the Report id to [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) to read its findings.

When the project has no Parsimony Report yet, the command is refused with `parsimony.no-report`. A stored Report that cannot be read is refused with `parsimony.report-damaged`.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) creates a Parsimony Report.
- [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) reads one by id.

# List Parsimony measures

`parsimony measures` lists the fixed Parsimony checks registered in this build, their axes, evidence tiers, required capabilities, citations, and recipe links. It reads the catalog and does not invoke PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony measures --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) queues a selected measure.
- [Read a Parsimony view](cmd:parsimony%20view) inspects captured evidence.

entries.title: Confirm a reviewed negative
entries.description: Confirms a forbidden surface form or exact reading as a human and stages its Notebook record in a Draft Proposal. A negative may have no grammar owner; only Apply writes it to the FieldWorks project.
entries.helpPage:
# Confirm a reviewed negative

```sh
motif parsimony negative confirm --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '<closed intent JSON>' \
  --confirm "I confirm this form or reading is forbidden in the stated context." [--json]
```

This HumanOnly command stages a human-confirmed surface or exact reading negative as Notebook operations in a Draft Proposal. Supply the Notebook `recordTypeId`, stable `caseId`, vernacular `writingSystem`, `form`, `context`, and a `target` with discriminator `"type":"surface"` or `"type":"reading"`. A reading target carries an ordered `morphs` array; each `identity` names the exact `form`, `msa`, and optional `inflType` portable IDs. `wordformId` and `analysisId` are optional, so the negative can exist without a wordform or grammar owner. `reason`, human actor fields, timestamp, and source `reportId` are optional.

Example surface target:

```json
{
  "recordTypeId": "record-type/<22-character-base64url-id>",
  "caseId": "case_0000000000000000000002",
  "writingSystem": "qaa",
  "form": "example",
  "context": "the stated environment",
  "target": { "kind": "surface" }
}
```

The command appends the existing Notebook create, description, and reserved-field operations to the Draft. Review the Draft with `dry-run`, then a person uses `apply` to save the judgment in FieldWorks. Until Apply succeeds, the negative is not part of the saved project. Run `parsimony expectations` to read it back.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony negative confirm --project <fwdata> --draft <name> --intent '<closed intent JSON>' --confirm "I confirm this form or reading is forbidden in the stated context." [--json]

entries.title: Retract a reviewed negative
entries.description: Withdraws a reviewed negative by naming its exact current revision heads and stages a retraction in a Draft Proposal. The Notebook history remains in the FieldWorks project, and only Apply records the withdrawal.
entries.helpPage:
# Retract a reviewed negative

```sh
motif parsimony negative retract --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '<closed retraction JSON>' \
  --confirm "I confirm this reviewed negative should be withdrawn." [--json]
```

This HumanOnly command stages a retraction revision for a saved reviewed negative. The closed intent names the Notebook `recordTypeId`, `judgmentId`, and every current `expectedHeads` entry as a revision ID and content digest; the composer refuses stale heads. An optional `reason`, human actor, and explicit UTC timestamp can record why the judgment was withdrawn.

The command appends the retraction's Notebook operations to a Draft Proposal and preserves the earlier revisions. Review the Draft with `dry-run`, then a person uses `apply` to save the retraction in FieldWorks. Run `parsimony expectations` to confirm the negative is no longer effective.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony negative retract --project <fwdata> --draft <name> --intent '<closed retraction JSON>' --confirm "I confirm this reviewed negative should be withdrawn." [--json]

entries.title: List Notebook record types
entries.description: Lists the saved Notebook record types with their portable IDs and readable names. Use the ID when you stage a Parsimony disposition.
entries.helpPage:
# List Notebook record types

```sh
motif parsimony record-types --project language.fwdata [--json]
```

Lists the saved record types in the project's Notebook with each type's portable ID and readable name. Choose a type by its ID; Motif never picks one by English name.

entries.title: Read a retirement review
entries.description: Reads the review state for one staged rule-based allomorph retirement Draft. It returns its latest matching Dry Run and names evidence that is not available yet; it never invents a finding or parser result.

entries.title: Retract a disposition
entries.description: Stages a withdrawal of a saved Parsimony disposition using its exact current Notebook heads and digests. The history stays in FieldWorks, and the finding returns to Active after a person Applies the current retraction.
entries.helpPage:
# Retract a disposition

```sh
motif parsimony retract <recordId> --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --expected-heads '[{"revisionId":"<portableId>","contentDigest":"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>"}]' [--json]
```

Use the `recordId` of a current disposition record. `--expected-heads` must name every current head and its exact digest; include both heads to resolve a conflict. Motif refuses a stale digest, a superseded record, or a record from another project.

Retraction appends a new Notebook record and retains the earlier judgment history. It stages an agent-attributed Draft Proposal; a person must Apply it. After the retraction is applied and current, refresh the project evidence to see the finding return to Active.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony retract <recordId> --project <fwdata> --draft <name> --expected-heads '<revisionId and contentDigest JSON array>' [--json]

entries.title: Revise a disposition
entries.description: Stages a revision to a saved Parsimony disposition using its exact current Notebook heads and digests. The revision keeps the same finding subject and evidence, and only a person can Apply it.
entries.helpPage:
# Revise a disposition

```sh
motif parsimony revise <recordId> --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --expected-heads '[{"revisionId":"<portableId>","contentDigest":"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>"}]' \
  --disposition keep|fix|ask|defer [--reason <text> | --clear-reason] [--question <text>] [--json]
```

Use the `recordId` of a current disposition record. `--expected-heads` must name every current head and its exact digest; include both heads to resolve a conflict. Motif refuses a stale digest, a superseded record, or a record from another project.

The revision appends a Notebook record and preserves the finding's subject and evidence binding. Supply a reason to replace it, use `--clear-reason` to remove it, or omit both to preserve it. `ask` requires `--question`; other choices must omit it. This command stages an agent-attributed Draft Proposal. Review it with Dry Run and Preflight; only a person can Apply it.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony revise <recordId> --project <fwdata> --draft <name> --expected-heads '<revisionId and contentDigest JSON array>' --disposition keep|fix|ask|defer [--reason <text> | --clear-reason] [--question <text>] [--json]

entries.title: Read a Parsimony Report
entries.description: Reads a stored Parsimony Report by id. It uses the saved Report and does not run PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Parsimony Report

`parsimony show` reads a previously stored Parsimony Report by id. It reads the saved Report and does not invoke PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <reportId> --json
```

The response returns the Report id, its frozen Baseline and artifact identities, its Assessment references, findings, and rendered text.
A check that could not look appears as a note: an information line in the rendered text and in `notes`, never a finding. A Report also lists authored grammar settings the parser ignores, as information only.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) creates a Parsimony Report.

entries.title: Read a Proposal's Parsimony status
entries.description: Says whether Parsimony has measured a Proposal's candidate after its Trial: not set up, not yet run, queued, running, ready, stale or failed, with a Grammar group and a Text group. It reads stored jobs and Reports only and never starts a run. Parsimony is advisory and never changes the Trial, Readiness or Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Proposal's Parsimony status

`parsimony status` says whether Parsimony has compared a Proposal's candidate grammar with the Baseline. A committed Trial queues that comparison on its own, behind all other work, so the answer is usually "queued", "running" or "ready" without anyone asking for it.

The overall state is one of `not-set-up` (PanGloss is missing), `not-yet-run`, `queued`, `running`, `ready`, `stale` (an input changed since the run, with the reasons listed) or `failed` (with a plain category such as `timed-out` for a very large grammar). The Grammar group runs every time. The Text group needs a saved Parsimony Selection and reports `not-set-up` until there is one.

Parsimony is advisory. A failed, timed-out or cancelled run never changes the Trial, Readiness or Apply, and there is no single score: each measure reports its own new, resolved, unchanged and changed-evidence findings. This command reads stored jobs and Reports and never starts a parse.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony status --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --proposal proposal/AbCd --json
```

## Timeouts and freshness

When PanGloss ran past its time limit on a grammar, Motif does not queue another automatic run for the same Baseline and PanGloss; the status reads `failed` with category `timed-out`. Run `motif parsimony` by hand to try again. A new Baseline or a new PanGloss clears this by itself.

A `ready` status was checked against the Baseline, the Proposal, its prerequisites, PanGloss and the measures. A changed human judgment or Parsimony Selection is not checked.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) runs a measure or group by hand.
- [Show a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) reads a stored Report.

entries.title: Read a Parsimony view
entries.description: Reads a bounded page from a fixed view over one frozen bundle. Parser views use a Report id to bind the exact Assessment references; filters and cursors are bound to the bundle. Only the declared view filters are accepted.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Parsimony view

`parsimony view` reads one page from a fixed, documented evidence view in a published bundle. The cursor is bound to the bundle, view, and filters; the command accepts no SQL and does not build missing artifacts. Supply the Report id when reading parser cases so Motif can restore the exact Assessment references.

Use `--report <reportId>` with `parsimony-active-findings`, `parsimony-suppressed` or `parsimony-suppression-history` to compare saved judgments with that exact Report and show evidence freshness. Active and suppressed finding rows include the current head IDs and `contentDigest` values; include every head for the same `judgmentId` when revising or retracting a conflict. Suppression-history rows include each revision's `contentDigest` as well, and every row names its judgment by `visibleId` (for example `MJ-7K3Q-9XDF`) and `recordTitle`, which match the Notebook record. `unresolved-judgment` rows list records that need a look: a `check` of `hash-failed` means "hash failed on this record entry" and the judgment does not suppress its finding, and a `state` of `warning` means an edited ID or sentence that still applies. Narrow those views with `--measure-id`, `--disposition`, `--state`, `--search` or `--subject-key`.

The `environment-excess` and `natural-class-excess` views cap each name list at 30 names when read whole, and list every name when you pass `--object-id`; each row's `totals` give the full count of every list.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony view allomorph-context --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --bundle <bundle-id> --object-id <allomorph-guid> --json
```

Read parser outcomes from the Report that named their Assessment:

```powershell
motif parsimony view parser-cases --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --bundle <bundle-id> --report <report-id> --json
```

Use `parsimony measures` to list view codes and their required inputs. A view with missing facts or Assessment material reports that capability as unavailable rather than returning an empty result.

## Related commands

- [List Parsimony measures](cmd:parsimony%20measures) lists registered checks and views.
- [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) opens stored findings.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony view <view-code> --project <fwdata> --bundle <id> [--object-id <guid> | --category-id <guid> | --statement-kind environment|natural-class] [--scope project-approved|default-selection] [--case-key <key>] [--report <id>] [--measure-id <id>] [--disposition keep|defer|fix|ask] [--state <state>] [--search <text>] [--subject-key <key>] [--cursor <cursor>] [--limit <n>] [--json]

entries.title: Check phonology examples
entries.description: Queues an advisory check of one saved Example Set revision against the current Baseline's grammar and records the result as an Assessment. It never changes the FieldWorks project, Readiness or Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Check phonology examples

`phonology-examples check` queues an advisory check of one saved Example Set revision against the grammar in the project's current [Baseline](term:baseline). For each example it asks PanGloss to generate surface forms from the underlying form in the example's declared context and reports whether the expected form was observed. A check never changes the FieldWorks project, never changes Readiness, and Apply ignores it.

## When to use it

Use this after saving examples with a cited source, to see whether the grammar as captured produces the forms you expect, and which rules applied. A result is `agree` when an expected form was observed, `disagree` when the search completed without it, and `unavailable` when nothing usable was measured (for example no parser, an empty lexicon, or a context that names no entry). Unavailable is never a pass.

## Example

```powershell
motif phonology-examples check --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <revisionId> --wait --json
motif jobs assessments --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <jobId> --json
```

## What it prints

The id of the queued job. With `--wait` it waits for the job to finish and prints the job's status. The job records one Assessment of kind `PhonologyExamples`; `jobs assessments` gives its id, and [phonology-examples results](cmd:phonology-examples%20results) reads it. `--work-cap` and `--timeout-ms` bound the whole check. If no Baseline has been captured the command is refused; if the Baseline changes before the job runs, the job fails and the check must be requested again.

## Related commands

- [Save phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20save) records the revision this command checks.
- [Read phonology check results](cmd:phonology-examples%20results) reads the stored result.

entries.title: List phonology examples
entries.description: Lists the current revision of each saved advisory phonology Example Set in stable order. Use the returned cursor to read another page.
entries.helpPage:
# List phonology examples

`phonology-examples list` reads the current revision of each saved phonology Example Set from the project's Motif store. Example Sets are advisory evidence and do not affect Readiness or Apply.

## When to use it

Use this to find a set and its current revision before reading or revising it. The command reads stored headers and does not capture the FieldWorks project or run PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif phonology-examples list --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Each item gives the set name, current revision id, and example count. A response with a continuation cursor has another page; pass that cursor as JSON with `--continuation`.

## Related commands

- [Save phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20save) creates a new set or advances one at its exact current revision.
- [Show a saved phonology revision](cmd:phonology-examples%20show) reads the complete examples a page at a time.

entries.title: Read phonology check results
entries.description: Reads the stored result of one advisory phonology check as a page of per-example summaries or one complete example. It reads stored evidence without capturing a project or running PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Read phonology check results

`phonology-examples results` reads the stored result of one phonology check: a page of per-example summaries, or one complete example. A check is advisory evidence about a saved Example Set against a [Baseline](term:baseline); it never changes Readiness and Apply ignores it.

## When to use it

Use this after a check has finished to see, for each example, whether the expected surface form was `agree` (observed), `disagree` (a completed search without it) or `unavailable` (no usable measurement, such as a missing parser or lexical context). Unavailable is never a pass. The command reads stored rows only: it does not capture the project or run PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif phonology-examples results --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <assessmentId> --json
motif phonology-examples results --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <assessmentId> --example front-vowel --json
```

## What it prints

A page lists each example with its disposition, completion, observed form and how many rules applied, in authored order. A response with a continuation cursor has another page; pass that cursor as JSON with `--continuation`. A summary lists at most 32 applied rule ids and says how many it left out. `--example <id>` prints the complete retained example with every ordered, visited and applied rule, and `--out <path.json>` also writes that JSON to a file. `--example` cannot be combined with `--page-size` or `--continuation`.

## Related commands

- [Show a saved phonology revision](cmd:phonology-examples%20show) reads the examples a check measured.
- [List saved phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20list) finds each set's current revision.

entries.title: Save phonology examples
entries.description: Saves underlying forms, expected surface forms and their context, with optional citations, as an immutable advisory Example Set revision. Saving does not change the FieldWorks project.
entries.helpPage:
# Save phonology examples

`phonology-examples save` records underlying forms, expected surface forms and the grammar context for each example as an immutable revision, with an optional citation on each. A saved set is advisory evidence: it never changes Readiness and Apply ignores it. Saving does not change the FieldWorks project.

## When to use it

Use this to keep a set of underlying forms and expected surface forms, with their sources, next to the project. To revise a set, save it again with its exact current revision id as `expectedRevisionId`.

## Example

Create a UTF-8 JSON file with a `name` and an `examples` array. Each example has an `id`, `underlying`, one or more `expected` forms, and a `context` tagged with `kind`. An optional `citation` has a `source` and `locator`.

```json
{
  "name": "Vowel harmony",
  "examples": [
    {
      "id": "front-vowel",
      "underlying": "a-ku",
      "expected": ["e-ki"],
      "context": {"kind": "hcXmlEntry", "entryId": "entry-17"},
      "citation": {"source": "Field notes", "locator": "example 12"}
    }
  ]
}
```

Then save it:

```powershell
motif phonology-examples save --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --file examples.json --json
```

## What is checked

An example whose context is a FieldWorks entry (`entryGuid` and `msaGuid`) is checked against the project's current Baseline, by reading the Baseline's saved project file. The entry must exist, and the stem MSA must belong to that entry. If one does not, nothing is saved and the refusal `phonology-examples.entry-not-found` names the example ids and the GUIDs that were not found, up to ten, with a count of the rest.

An example whose context is an HC XML entry id (`hcXmlEntry`) is not checked against FieldWorks: those ids belong to a grammar export, not to the project.

If the project has no Baseline yet, the set is still saved, because authoring examples before capturing a Baseline is a normal order of work. The response then says `not-verified-no-baseline`, and the check command will report any entry it cannot find as unavailable. A Baseline file that is missing or unreadable gives `not-verified-baseline-file-missing` the same way.

## What it prints

The response names the saved set and revision, including its executable and cited revision digests, and an `entryVerification` value: `verified` when every FieldWorks entry was found in the Baseline, `not-applicable` when no example names a FieldWorks entry, or `not-verified-no-baseline` and `not-verified-baseline-file-missing` when the check could not run. A citation-only edit creates a new cited revision while leaving the executable digest unchanged.

## Related commands

- [List saved phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20list) shows each set's current revision.
- [Show a saved phonology revision](cmd:phonology-examples%20show) reads its examples and citations.

entries.title: Show phonology examples
entries.description: Reads a bounded page from one exact saved Example Set revision, including its citations. It reads stored evidence without capturing a project or running PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Show phonology examples

`phonology-examples show` reads one exact saved revision and returns its examples in authored order, including source context and any citations. Example Sets are advisory evidence and do not affect Readiness or Apply.

## When to use it

Use this to inspect a current or historical revision. The command reads Motif's stored rows and does not capture the project or run PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif phonology-examples show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <revisionId> --json
```

## What it prints

Each example includes its underlying form, expected forms, generation context, and optional citation. A continuation cursor marks another page; pass that cursor as JSON with `--continuation`.

## Related commands

- [List phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20list) finds the current revision of each set.
- [Save phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20save) records a new immutable revision.

entries.title: Prepare a project for Motif
entries.description: Creates Motif's reserved human judgment field in a FieldWorks project after explicit confirmation. It does not add a judgment or create a writing system.
entries.helpPage:
# Initialize a project

Prepare a FieldWorks project to hold human judgments about Parsimony recommendations. Motif creates two reserved Notebook fields, one for the judgment data and one for its visible ID, and saves them in the project after you confirm.

```text
motif project initialize --project <fwdata> --confirm "Initialize this project to work with Motif Proposals?" [--json]
```

This command is available in the CLI and is never exposed as an MCP tool. The confirmation text must match exactly. Initialization does not create a judgment, a Notebook record, a Proposal, or a writing system.

The project must have an analysis writing system. If Motif finds an incompatible or duplicate definition with a reserved name, resolve it deliberately in FieldWorks and run initialization again. Motif does not rename or repair an existing definition.

A project that still has the older single field named `MotifHumanJudgment` is refused: delete Motif's test/demo judgment records and that field in FieldWorks, then initialize again. Motif does not convert old records.

Motif keeps a byte-checked recovery copy of the original project before it saves. Motif cannot undo a save, so the project is recoverable from that copy. If Motif cannot establish whether the save completed, the refusal names the recovery copy and gives the restore step: Close FieldWorks, then copy the recovery copy over the project file. Motif never restores the project by itself. A successful run that keeps a copy names it but gives no restore step, because restoring would undo the initialization. Inspect the saved project before you restore or retry.
usage: Usage: motif project initialize --project <fwdata> --confirm "Initialize this project to work with Motif Proposals?" [--json]

entries.title: Read a project tag
entries.description: Reads the tag Motif stores for this project on this machine. When its vernacular language code is already used, Motif tries the exact folder name and refuses if that choice is invalid or taken.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a project tag

Read the tag Motif stores for this project on this machine. For a project without a tag, Motif uses its vernacular language code when that code is available. If the code is already used, Motif tries the exact folder name and refuses if that name is invalid or taken.

```text
motif project tag --project <fwdata>
```

Use `--json` to receive the tag as structured output. If Motif cannot choose a valid, unused tag, choose one with `project tag --set`.

entries.title: Set a project tag
entries.description: Chooses the tag Motif stores for this project on this machine. The tag must follow the lowercase rules and be unused by every other Known project.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a project tag

Choose the tag Motif stores for this project on this machine. A tag starts with a lowercase letter, uses lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, contains at most ten characters, and must be unused by every other Known project.

```text
motif project tag --set cebu --project <fwdata>
```

Use `--json` to receive the saved tag as structured output. The new tag remains in place when Motif records the project again.

entries.title: Add a Proposal Comment
entries.description: Adds a Comment to an open Proposal, in Markdown. A person or an assistant may add one; an assistant says what it calls itself, and the Comment shows as author for person.
entries.helpPage:
# Add a Comment to a Proposal

Adds a Comment to an open Proposal, in Markdown. A person or an assistant may add one; an assistant says what it calls itself with `--author`.

## Example

```text
motif proposal comment add <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --text "Please keep the second gloss"
motif proposal comment add <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --file comment.md --author "Claude (Opus 5.5)"
```

Give the full Proposal id. Without `--author` the Comment is the person's; `--person` names the person, and defaults to the computer's user name. An author label and a person name hold at most 100 characters, and a Comment shows as "author for person". The label is only a label: Motif does not check it, and nothing depends on it.

A Comment stays outside the Proposal's changes and remembers which content it was written for. It can be added until the Proposal is applied, declined, withdrawn or superseded; reopening the Proposal allows Comments again. When a person's Comment is newer than the [Rationale](cmd:proposal%20rationale), `show` reports `commentsChanged`, and an assistant is told to read it.

entries.title: Delete a Proposal Comment
entries.description: Deletes a Comment from an open Proposal. Only a person deletes a Comment.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a Comment on a Proposal

Deletes a Comment from an open Proposal. Only a person deletes a Comment; an assistant cannot.

## Example

```text
motif proposal comment delete <proposalId> <commentId> --project <fwdata>
```

Give the full Proposal id and the Comment number that `show` lists. A deleted Comment is gone. Comments cannot change once the Proposal is applied, declined, withdrawn or superseded.

entries.title: Edit a Proposal Comment
entries.description: Replaces the text of a Comment on an open Proposal. Only a person edits a Comment; it then shows that it was edited, and when.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a Comment on a Proposal

Replaces the text of a Comment on an open Proposal. Only a person edits a Comment; an assistant cannot.

## Example

```text
motif proposal comment edit <proposalId> <commentId> --project <fwdata> --text "Keep the second gloss, drop the third"
motif proposal comment edit <proposalId> <commentId> --project <fwdata> --file comment.md
```

Give the full Proposal id and the Comment number that `show` lists. The Comment then shows that it was edited, and when; the earlier text is not kept. A Comment cannot be empty: [delete it](cmd:proposal%20comment%20delete) instead. Comments cannot change once the Proposal is applied, declined, withdrawn or superseded.

entries.title: Write a Proposal's Rationale
entries.description: Writes or replaces what a Proposal changes and why, in Markdown. The Rationale stays outside the Proposal's content, so rewriting it never changes what the Proposal does, and it can be rewritten until the Proposal is applied or closed.
entries.helpPage:
# Write a Proposal's Rationale

Writes or replaces a Proposal's Rationale: what the Proposal changes and why, in Markdown. Whoever builds the Proposal, usually an assistant, writes it.

## Example

```text
motif proposal rationale <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --text "Plural -s was missing from the noun template"
motif proposal rationale <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --file rationale.md
motif proposal rationale <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --text "..." --author "Claude (Opus 5.5)"
```

Give the full Proposal id, the one `new` or `proposals` returned; a name or a prefix is refused. A Draft that has never been finalized has a Proposal id too, so write the Rationale before [`finalize`](cmd:finalize), which refuses a Proposal without one.

The Rationale is kept apart from the Proposal's changes, so rewriting it never changes what the Proposal does. It remembers which content it was written for: after the Proposal changes, the person sees it marked out of date, and a rewrite clears that mark. It can be rewritten until the Proposal is applied or closed, and it holds at most 64 KiB.

If the person left a [Comment](cmd:proposal%20comment%20add), a new Rationale is one answer to it. `--author` says what an assistant calls itself, as it does for a Comment; each rewrite is kept, with its author, until the Proposal is decided.

entries.title: Review a Proposal's changes
entries.description: Lists every change in one Proposal in the order to read them: grammar changes first, then word changes. Each entry says whether it has been looked at, and the list carries the Proposal's latest Trial.
entries.helpPage:
# Review a Proposal's changes

`motif proposal review` prints one Proposal's changes as a single list, in the order a person reads them. Grammar changes come first, a change that others depend on before the changes that depend on it; word changes follow.

## When to use it

Use it to see what a Proposal would do before you try or apply it. The window's Review Changes page shows the same list. Without `--proposal` it reads the pending changes.

## Example

```text
motif proposal review --project <project> --proposal <id> --json
```

## What it prints

Each entry has a title, the operations it owns, what it depends on, and `lookedAt`. An entry counts as looked at only while neither the entry nor the Trial it was judged against has changed. Looking at an entry is attention, not approval: applying never requires it. The response also carries the latest Trial and whether its Correctness evidence permits Apply.

## Related commands

See [Apply one Proposal](cmd:apply%20--proposal) to write a reviewed Proposal, and [Apply pending changes](cmd:apply%20--all-pending) for the pending changes.

entries.title: List Proposals
entries.description: Lists every Proposal with what it changes and the numbers its latest Trial measured beside today's. Proposals are grouped by what to do next; applied and set-aside ones are counted unless asked for.
entries.helpPage:
# List Proposals

`proposals` lists every Proposal in a project, grouped by what to do with it, with what each one changes and the numbers its latest [Trial](term:trial) measured beside today's.

## When to use it

Use it to see what is waiting for review, what needs another try, and which changes are your own and not yet applied. The Proposals page in the window reads the same list.

## Example

```powershell
motif proposals --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
motif proposals --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --include-set-aside --json
```

## What it prints

Each Proposal carries its label, status and group: **WaitingForYou** (a complete Trial matches the project and the Proposal as they are now), **NeedsAnotherTry** (the project or the Proposal moved since the Trial, or its latest Trial is running or did not finish), **NotTried** (no Trial exists), **NotAppliedYet** (your own collected changes) or **SetAside** (closed: applied, rejected, superseded or withdrawn). Closed Proposals are counted in `setAsideCount` and listed only with `--include-set-aside`. A deferred Proposal is still open and is grouped by its Trial like a proposed one.

A stored Proposal or Draft whose content cannot be read is left out of the list and named in `unreadable`, with its id, its label when it has one, its draft name when it is a Draft, and why. Motif does not change or delete it. The window says how many could not be read and names them.

A Proposal also lists its change kinds, such as two rules, one allomorph and one approved parse, and the ids of other Proposals that change one of the same words. Its Trial summary pairs five numbers, each as a value before and after: Text Coverage, approved words kept, approved words, parse time on this computer and the warning count. The Trial's parser work, in parser work against the Baseline, is reported beside them, and that is the figure to compare. The window shows it as **Work**, blank when the Trial cannot be compared with today's parse, and adds the time on this computer last. A Trial over only the touched words still pairs the totals: every word it did not measure keeps today's value. Chips count approved words the Trial lost and changes that no longer fit.

## Trying a Proposal again

In the window, **Try again** on a card measures the Proposal on a copy of the project. The copy is thrown away and your FieldWorks project is not changed. A card whose Trial is still running says **Trying…** and offers no second button.

## Related commands

- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) reads one Proposal's Trial with `--proposal`.
- [Delete a closed Proposal](cmd:delete%20--proposal) removes a closed Proposal that never applied.

entries.title: Decline a Proposal
entries.description: Declines a Proposal you do not want. It is kept with its Trials as history, and you can reopen it later.
entries.helpPage:
# Decline a Proposal

`motif reject --proposal <id>` declines a Proposal you do not want. It is kept, with its [Trials](term:trial), as a record of what was suggested; nothing reaches FieldWorks.

## When to use it

Use it after reading a Proposal you will not apply. A Proposal that is still a Draft is finalized first, so what you declined stays readable. Your own pending changes are not declined; take them out on **Review Changes** instead.

## Example

```text
motif reject --proposal <id> --project <project> --json
```

## What it prints

The Proposal's id and its new status, `rejected`. In the window, **Decline** on **Review Changes** does the same while the Proposal is open, and the card moves to **Closed** on **Proposals**.

## Related commands

See [Reopen a Proposal](cmd:reopen%20--proposal) and [Delete a closed Proposal](cmd:delete%20--proposal).

entries.title: Remove Draft operations
entries.description: Removes explicit operations from a Draft while respecting declared dependencies. Revise and measure the content again before Finalize. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove Draft operations

Removes explicit operations from a Draft while respecting declared dependencies. Revise and measure the content again before Finalize. Only a person can Apply.

entries.title: Reopen a Proposal
entries.description: Opens a declined or withdrawn Proposal again as a Draft under the same id, with its history kept. An applied or superseded Proposal is never reopened.
entries.helpPage:
# Reopen a Proposal

`motif reopen --proposal <id>` opens a declined or withdrawn Proposal again as a Draft, under the same id. Its earlier revisions and [Trials](term:trial) are kept.

## When to use it

Use it when you change your mind about a Proposal you declined, or want to take up one its author withdrew. An applied Proposal is final and is refused with `proposal.applied-final`. A superseded Proposal is refused with `proposal.superseded`, which names the Proposal that replaced it.

## Example

```text
motif reopen --proposal <id> --project <project> --json
```

## What it prints

The Proposal's id, the name of its Draft and how many changes it holds. In the window, **Reopen** on a closed card on **Proposals** does the same. Try the Proposal again before applying it.

## Related commands

See [Decline a Proposal](cmd:reject%20--proposal) and [Apply one Proposal](cmd:apply%20--proposal).

entries.title: Read an Assessment report
entries.description: Calculates a named report from an Assessment and project data. Use it to answer a focused question about words, Texts, or grammar without rerunning PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Read an Assessment report

`report` calculates a named Report from one stored Assessment and the project's own data. It answers a focused question about measured evidence without running PanGloss again.

The kind list includes `parsimony`, but `report` reads one stored Assessment. Supplying that Assessment to `report --kind parsimony` is refused because the Parsimony producer needs a frozen Baseline evidence bundle, not an Assessment input. Create the result with [`parsimony --wait`](cmd:parsimony%20--wait) and read it with [`parsimony show`](cmd:parsimony%20show).

## When to use it

Use a Report to inspect counts or findings for words, Texts, or grammar after an Assessment exists. First list the available kinds if you do not know which one matches your question.

## Example

```powershell
motif report --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --assessment <assessmentId> --kind <kind> --json
```

## What it prints

The response contains findings for the requested kind and can be narrowed to a word or Text. `--json` returns structured results. Reports are advisory; they do not decide whether an Apply is allowed.

## Related commands

- [List report kinds](cmd:report%20--list-kinds) shows accepted values for `--kind`.
- [Compare two Assessments](cmd:compare) stores a measured difference between runs.

entries.title: List report kinds
entries.description: Lists the report kinds accepted by report --kind. Run it first when you need to choose a report for stored evidence.
entries.helpPage:
# List report kinds

`report --list-kinds` prints the stable kind codes accepted by `report --kind`.

The list includes `parsimony`, but `report` reads one stored Assessment. Supplying that Assessment to `report --kind parsimony` is refused because the Parsimony producer needs a frozen Baseline evidence bundle, not an Assessment input. Use [`parsimony --wait`](cmd:parsimony%20--wait) to create that Report, then [`parsimony show`](cmd:parsimony%20show) to read it.

## When to use it

Run this when writing a script or choosing a Report and you need to know which kinds Motif supports. The returned codes are machine-readable identifiers; they are not display labels.

## Example

```powershell
motif report --list-kinds
```

## What it prints

The command lists available Report kinds. Add `--json` for a structured list that an AI agent or script can select from without parsing terminal text.

## Related commands

- [Read an Assessment report](cmd:report) runs one of the listed kinds.
- [Inspect parse timing](cmd:timing) reads recorded timing evidence directly.

entries.title: Ask again after a decline
entries.description: Makes a new open Request from the Request a declined Proposal answered, with the same target and note, so an assistant can try again.
entries.helpPage:
# Ask again after a decline

`request ask-again` makes a new open Request from the Request a declined Proposal answered, with the same target and note, so an assistant can try again.

## Example

```text
motif request ask-again <proposalId> --project <fwdata>
```

Give the full id of a declined Proposal that answered a Request. Asking twice returns the new Request while it is still open.

## Related commands

- [List the open Requests](cmd:list%20requests) shows the new one.

entries.title: Ask an assistant to fix this
entries.description: Stores a Request about a word, a Warning or a Compare matrix cell, with an optional note in the linguist's words. An assistant answers it with a Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Ask an assistant to fix this

`request create` stores a Request: something the linguist wants an assistant to fix, about a word, a Warning or a Compare matrix cell. An assistant answers it with a [Proposal](term:proposal).

## Example

```text
motif request create --project <fwdata> --kind word --target <word> --label <word> [--note "Please check the plural"]
```

`--kind` is `word`, `warning` or `matrix-cell`. `--target` is the word, Warning or cell as the window names it, and `--label` is a short name a person can read. The note is optional, at most 2000 characters, and stays the linguist's own words.

A Request is answered when the Proposal that answers it is finalized. It opens again if that Proposal is withdrawn or replaced before anyone decides, and stays answered if the linguist declines it.

## Related commands

- [List the open Requests](cmd:list%20requests) reads them.
- [Withdraw a Request](cmd:request%20withdraw) takes one back.

entries.title: Withdraw a Request
entries.description: Takes back an open Request the linguist no longer wants answered. An answered Request cannot be withdrawn.
entries.helpPage:
# Withdraw a Request

`request withdraw` takes back an open Request the linguist no longer wants answered.

## Example

```text
motif request withdraw <requestId> --project <fwdata>
```

Give the full `requestId` that [list requests](cmd:list%20requests) returns. Only an open Request can be withdrawn; an answered one stays as it is.

entries.title: Retire or merge forms
entries.description: Stages one connected Proposal to retire ordinary prefix or suffix alternates after their references move, or a duplicate stem alternate that nothing refers to; the sound-rule form also stages its natural class and rule. Dry Run shows bundle Morph and copied Form text changes, other references, and deletion together. Missing destinations are refused with counts for distinct unresolved Approved analyses, ad hoc rules, and other references; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Retire or replace a form

Use this command to stage one ordinary prefix or suffix retirement in a Draft. Read the entry with detailed `motif_lexicon` output to copy its form identities and semantic digests. The closed intent names each retired form, its exact surviving form, and every bundle or ad hoc reference that must move.

```sh
motif retire-allomorph --project language.fwdata --draft remove-duplicate --intent '{"format":"motif-retire-allomorph","version":1,"retirement":{...}}'
```

The same standalone intent retires a stem alternate with `"scope":"stem"`, for a root or stem form that an exact duplicate in the same entry makes redundant. The duplicate must have the same morph type, spelling, stem name and environments, and it may be another alternate or the lexeme form. A stem retirement moves no references: if an analysis or restriction still refers to the retired form, or the form owns anything, the command refuses and names the reason. An entry always keeps the surviving duplicate, so its last stem form is never retired. A sound-rule replacement of stems stays refused.

For a listed allomorph replacement with a sound rule, use the `motif-allomorph-retirement` version 2 intent. It names the natural class, rewrite rule, each retired form, every destination, and the operation bindings in the same Proposal:

```sh
motif retire-allomorph --project language.fwdata --draft replace-listed --intent '{"format":"motif-allomorph-retirement","version":2,"naturalClass":{...},"rule":{...},"retirements":[...],"operations":[...]}'
```

The four displayed parts stay in that one Proposal: the sound class and rule; analyses whose bundle Morph moves, including the copied bundle Form alternatives; other references that move; and the retired forms. The dependency graph orders the writes. Dry Run reads back both Morph and native Form effects; no display order changes mutation order, and no part can be applied on its own.

The reference census refuses an incomplete or changed view, an unsupported reference, a form that no longer matches its authored identity, or an owned dependent that deletion would remove. When a destination is missing, the refusal names the number of distinct Approved analyses and ad hoc rules still unresolved, plus other references. Declare every destination and run Dry Run again.

Review the paired before and after reading evidence for every affected Approved reading. The review keeps each FieldWorks Opinion and surface spelling beside its parser result and rule attribution. Missing identity, parser completion, read-back, or rule trace is shown as unavailable; it is never counted as a preserved reading. Check that the detector finding is resolved in the rebuilt after Report, separately from whether a disposition is Suppressed, before a person Applies the whole Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Retire an unused zero affix
entries.description: Stages deletion of one whole, unreferenced zero-affix entry when its only loaded realization is a recognized null marker, it adds no feature or class, every assigned slot is optional, and no assigned slot occurs in a template. Optional slot links are removed first and the slots remain; meaningful, referenced, or parser-distinguishing zeros are refused. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Retire an unused zero affix

Use this command to stage deletion of a complete, unused prefix or suffix entry whose only loaded realization is a recognized null marker such as `^0`, `*0`, `&0`, or `∅`. An optional slot can remain in an inflectional template; deleting the entry removes its zero realization while preserving the slot and the template. The closed intent names the entry by canonical identity.

```sh
motif retire-redundant-zero-affix --project language.fwdata --draft remove-unused-zero --intent '{"format":"motif-retire-redundant-zero-affix","version":1,"retirement":{"entry":"<canonicalId>"}}'
```

The command includes the entry, its senses, analysis, form, and every owned dependent in one delete. It refuses feature, inflection-class, exception, condition, required-slot, or outside-reference contributions. References from the analysis to optional slots are removed before deletion; any template and its optional slot remain. Review the Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Choose a Default Selection
entries.description: Saves which project Texts and words Motif should measure by default. Use it to focus repeated Assessments on material a linguist has chosen.
entries.helpPage:
# Choose a Default Selection

`selection set-default` saves which project Texts and added words Motif measures when a command does not name another Selection. It also saves the Selection's parser work limit and estimated or explicit time policy.

## When to use it

Use this to focus repeatable Assessments on a linguist-chosen set of material. Texts are identified by GUID, not by title, and added words can be included even when they do not occur in a Text.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection set-default --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Verb examples" --texts <textGuid> --add-words "mala,ma" --parser-work-limit 20000000 --time-mode estimated
```

Use `--time-mode explicit --time-limit-ms <positive>` for a chosen time safety net, in milliseconds on this computer. `--time-mode estimated` rejects `--time-limit-ms`; `--parser-work-limit none` stores no step or time cap. To replace an existing Selection, first read its revision with [selection show](cmd:selection%20show) and pass it as `--expected-revision`.

## A word list with counts

`--words-file <path>` takes the added words from a UTF-8 file, in place of `--add-words`. Each line is a word, or a word, a tab and a whole-number count. There is no header line, and the file is at most 8 MiB.

- A plain list of words gives no counts. A word with no count has a count that is not known, which is not the same as zero.
- Words are stored in NFD. A word on several lines has its counts added up.
- Motif stores the file's name and its SHA-256 with the Selection, so you can tell which list the counts came from.
- A later save that names no file keeps the stored list when the Texts and added words are the same, and any other change to the Texts or words drops it.
- A Selection of chosen Texts ranks its words by places in those Texts. A Selection with no Texts ranks them by the file's counts, and the Overview then names its bands By Frequency Band, never Text Coverage.
- The window shows the same count beside each word in the word list of a Selection with no Texts, most often used first. A word the file gave no count has a blank there, and a count of zero shows as zero. Once the words are edited so they are no longer the saved list, the counts are blank until the Selection is saved with a list.

```powershell
motif selection set-default --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Frequent words" --words-file .\frequencies.tsv
```

## What it prints

The command reports the saved Selection name and its settings. Add `--json` to receive the structured Selection response.

## Related commands

- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) reads what was saved.
- [List project Texts](cmd:texts%20list) finds Text GUIDs to select.
- [Set Selection limits](cmd:selection%20set-limits) changes limits without replacing the word list.

entries.title: Set Selection limits
entries.description: Changes only the saved Default Selection's parsing limits when its expected revision still matches. Use it to update the parser work limit or estimated-versus-explicit time policy without replacing the chosen Texts and added words.
entries.helpPage:
# Set Selection limits

`selection set-limits` changes the parsing limits on the project's current Default Selection. The chosen Texts, added words, name, and setup status stay in place.

## When to use it

Use this from Settings or **Analysis options** when you want later Default Selection parses to use a different parser work limit or time policy. Running and saved results keep their own resolved limits.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection set-limits --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Default" --expected-revision 3 --parser-work-limit 20000000 --time-mode estimated
```

Use `--time-mode explicit --time-limit-ms <positive>` to choose a time safety net, in milliseconds on this computer. Estimated mode rejects an explicit millisecond value. Use `--parser-work-limit none` for no step or time limit; an explicit time cap is not allowed with an unbounded parser work limit. Read the current revision with [selection show](cmd:selection%20show); if another write has changed it, read again and retry with the new revision.

## What it prints

The command returns the updated Selection and its new revision. Add `--json` to receive the structured projection.

## Related commands

- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) reads its current revision and policy.
- [Choose a Default Selection](cmd:selection%20set-default) also changes its Texts and added words.
- [Show project configuration](cmd:config%20show) reads named Assessment scopes from the project configuration file.

entries.title: Choose a Parsimony Selection
entries.description: Saves the Texts that Parsimony's Text group reads, apart from the Default Selection. Every Parsimony run reuses this set until you change it.
entries.helpPage:
# Choose a Parsimony Selection

`selection set-parsimony` saves the Texts that Parsimony's Text group reads. Every Parsimony run reuses the set until you change it, so the evidence for judging the grammar stays the same from run to run.

## When to use it

Use this once per project before running the Text group, or when you want different Texts as evidence. The Parsimony Selection is separate from the Default Selection: the Default Selection is what the project parses and times, and may be large, while the Parsimony Selection is the evidence a linguist chose by hand. Changing one never changes the other.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection set-parsimony --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Evidence" --texts <textGuid>,<textGuid>
```

With `--texts` the command saves a Selection of that name. Without `--texts` the name must already be a saved Selection, and the command points Parsimony at it. A name that is the Default Selection is refused when `--texts` is given, because that would change the Default Selection's Texts.

## What it prints

The command prints the Default Selection, if any, and the Parsimony Selection with its Text count. Add `--json` for the structured response.

## Related commands

- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) shows both Selections.
- [List project Texts](cmd:texts%20list) finds Text GUIDs to select.

entries.title: Show the Default Selection
entries.description: Reads the saved Texts, added words, and limits that determine what an Assessment measures when no other Selection is supplied, and the separate Parsimony Selection.
entries.helpPage:
# Show the Default Selection

`selection show` reads the saved Default Selection for a FieldWorks project, and the Parsimony Selection that Parsimony's Text group reads. It reports the chosen Texts, added words, parsing policy, and revision used by later writes.

## When to use it

Use this before an Assessment when you need to know which words Motif will measure by default. Each Assessment keeps the exact words it resolved, so later edits to this setting do not change earlier evidence.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

The command prints the saved Selection name, Text ids, added words, the per-word parser work limit, and whether the time safety net is estimated or explicit. When the added words came from a word-list file with counts, it also names the file, its SHA-256, and how many words have a count. JSON returns the same saved policy and its opaque revision.

## Related commands

- [Choose a Default Selection](cmd:selection%20set-default) changes the saved word list.
- [Choose a Parsimony Selection](cmd:selection%20set-parsimony) saves the Texts Parsimony reads.
- [Set Selection limits](cmd:selection%20set-limits) updates its parsing policy without replacing its chosen words.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) uses it when no explicit source is supplied.

entries.title: Skip project setup
entries.description: Marks first-time Selection setup as skipped for this project. Use it when the project can be opened but a Default Selection should not be chosen yet.
entries.helpPage:
# Skip project setup

`setup skip` records that first-time Selection setup has been skipped for this project.

## When to use it

Use it when a project is ready to open but nobody should choose a Default Selection yet. This records the choice without creating a Selection or measuring any words.

## Example

```powershell
motif setup skip --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

The command confirms the setup choice, or returns it as structured JSON. Later, a Default Selection can still be set explicitly.

## Related commands

- [Choose a Default Selection](cmd:selection%20set-default) records the words to measure.
- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) reads the latest stored project evidence.

entries.title: Show a Proposal
entries.description: Reads one saved Proposal or Draft by id, with its status, label, Rationale, Comments and operations. It does not change the FieldWorks project.
entries.helpPage:
# Show a Proposal

Reads one saved Proposal by its canonical id, or a Draft by name or canonical id, with its status, label, Rationale, Comments and operations. The Rationale shows whether it is out of date and whether you have looked at it; the Comments show whether a person's is newer than the Rationale. It does not change the FieldWorks project.

entries.title: Show a Corpus
entries.description: Reads the provenance, tokeniser, and licence capabilities recorded for one Corpus. Use it to verify what a Corpus allows before using its text as evidence.
entries.helpPage:
# Show a Corpus

`show-corpus` reads the provenance, tokeniser, and licence capabilities recorded for one Corpus.

## When to use it

Use it before relying on Corpus material as evidence, especially when redistribution or derived use matters. The response preserves unknown licence capabilities instead of treating them as permission.

## Example

```powershell
motif show-corpus --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" stories --json
```

## What it prints

The command displays the selected Corpus and its recorded Documents. JSON returns the full detail response, including the three licence capabilities and their recorded basis.

## Related commands

- [List Corpora](cmd:corpora) finds Corpus ids.
- [Add a Corpus Document](cmd:add-document) records another Document's source.

entries.title: List Sources
entries.description: Lists the Sources the project's Motif Sources list holds, with their Context and any reason one cannot be used. Removed Sources are hidden unless asked for.
entries.helpPage:
# List Sources

`source list` reads the project's "Motif Sources" list from the current Baseline and prints one row per Source: its id, name, status, Context, and the reason when the item cannot be used. A bad item never hides the others.

## Example

```text
motif source list --project Koro.fwdata --json
```

Removed Sources are hidden; `--all` shows them. The list does not open the live FieldWorks project, so `isStale` says whether FieldWorks has saved since the Baseline. A project with no such list has no Sources. Two lists with the same name are refused as ambiguous.

## Related commands

- [Show one Source](cmd:source%20show) reads a Source's Context ranges and folder.
- [Place a chapter](cmd:source%20where) says where a chapter sits.

entries.title: Show one Source
entries.description: Reads one Source: its Context as book and chapter ranges, how many chapters that is, its folder on this machine and its status.
entries.helpPage:
# Show one Source

`source show <id>` reads one Source from the current Baseline: its Context as book and chapter ranges, how many chapters that is, its status, and the folder recorded for it on this machine (or none). The id is matched ignoring case. A Removed Source can still be shown.

## Example

```text
motif source show --project Koro.fwdata WEB --json
```

The folder lives in a per-user local file and is never part of the project.

## Related commands

- [List Sources](cmd:source%20list) lists every Source.
- [Place a chapter](cmd:source%20where) says where a chapter sits.

entries.title: Place a chapter in the Sources
entries.description: Says whether a chapter is in each Source's Context, is the Current chapter, or comes later.
entries.helpPage:
# Place a chapter in the Sources

`source where <ref>` says where a chapter such as `MAT 5` sits in a Source: `InContext` when its Context includes it, `Current` when it is outside the Context but is the Current chapter, otherwise `Later`. With no `--source` it answers for every Active Source, one row each.

## Example

```text
motif source where --project Koro.fwdata "MAT 5" --source WEB --json
```

When the Source has a folder on this machine, the Paratext text is opened and a chapter the text does not hold is reported as an error on that row. With no folder, the place comes from the Context and the Current chapter alone.

## Related commands

- [Read the Current chapters](cmd:current%20get) reads the Current chapters.
- [Show one Source](cmd:source%20show) reads a Source.

entries.title: Query parse statistics
entries.description: Forwards statistics options to PanGloss using the grammar and cache recorded for an Assessment. Use it to inspect parser work after an Assessment is available.
entries.helpPage:
# Query parse statistics

`stats` forwards a PanGloss statistics query using the grammar and cache recorded for an Assessment. Motif preserves the PanGloss options after `--` instead of interpreting them. Add `--proposal <id>` to use the per-object statistics recorded by that Proposal's latest Trial.

## When to use it

Use this after an Assessment with statistics when you need a focused count or a JSONL result from PanGloss. Put `--json` before `--` to request structured rows from Motif.

## Example

```powershell
motif stats "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json -- --group word
```

## What it prints

Without `--json`, PanGloss's text output is passed through. With `--json`, Motif returns the selected Assessment, grammar and cache paths, and parsed statistics rows.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records Assessment evidence and statistics.
- [Inspect word analyses](cmd:analyses) reads manual and Assessment-backed analysis evidence.

entries.title: Prune project store
entries.description: Removes older Assessments that are no longer needed by retained evidence. It also reclaims available space in the project store.
entries.helpPage:
# Prune the project store

`store prune` removes older Assessments that are not needed by retained evidence and reclaims available store space.

Motif keeps the newest 20 standalone Assessments of each kind by default (5 for Object Timing, whose per-object tables are large), along with pinned, current, and cited evidence. Set `standalone-assessments-per-kind` in the `[retention]` section of the project configuration to change the count. Unneeded standalone and decided Proposal Assessments older than 90 days are removed, as are all but the newest 30 Assessments of each kind on a decided Proposal. The store targets 100 MB: when it holds more, the oldest evidence that nothing needs goes next, including evidence of Proposals already decided, and never evidence of an open Proposal. Authored and protected evidence may keep a store above the target. A decided Proposal keeps its summary and loses its word detail. When deleted rows leave a large share of the file free, this command rewrites the file to give the space back; the worker does the same once a day for the stores it has open. Motif also prunes after a successful Assessment, without the rewrite.

```powershell
motif store prune --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

A completed Trial holds its Before and After Assessments only while its Proposal is undecided; once the Proposal is applied, withdrawn, declined or superseded, its Trial evidence may go like the rest of that Proposal's evidence. After pruning the store, the command removes this project's run directories that the store no longer names once they are an hour old, and sweeps the per-user data folder with no size limit: every run, project source copy and Baseline that no project store names and that is an hour old goes, unless a parse is reading it.

The result reports the number of Assessments and invocation directories removed and the store file size before and after reclamation. It also reports the store's byte budget and the bytes in use, the kept Assessments counted by reason (such as `openProposal`, `current`, `pinned`, `report`, `openTrial`, `lineage` or `withinLimits`), the kept run directories by reason, and what the per-user data sweep removed and kept. Directories whose ownership cannot be proven are kept; the result reports their count, total size and parent path so they can be inspected. Active readers can postpone reclaiming some space; run the command again after they finish.

entries.title: Upgrade project store
entries.description: Carries authored work into the current store and keeps a backup of the old store. Computed results are discarded and can be recreated.
entries.helpPage:
# Upgrade a project store

`store upgrade` carries authored work from an older Motif store into the current format. Motif keeps the old
store as a versioned backup and discards computed results, which can be recreated. The one computed result it
keeps is the saved Difference summary of each decided or deferred Proposal, because it cannot be recreated once
the Proposal is set aside; the word detail under it is discarded. Summaries are kept from schema 56 on; an upgrade from an
older schema drops them, because they are in a shape this Motif cannot read.

```powershell
motif store upgrade --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

Opening a project also upgrades its older store automatically. The upgrade report beside the store lists the
rows carried, tables discarded, and any Proposal revisions that the current Motif cannot read.

To inspect an older store without changing it, give an existing source and a new output path:

```powershell
motif store upgrade --source old.motif.db --out upgraded.motif.db --json
```

entries.title: List project Texts
entries.description: Lists Text records from the project's current Baseline with their identity and interlinearization data. Use it to find Text ids for a Default Selection or Assessment.
entries.helpPage:
# List project Texts

`texts list` reads Text records from the project's current Baseline and returns their GUIDs, titles, and interlinearization data.

## When to use it

Use this to find Text GUIDs before choosing them for a Default Selection or an Assessment. The command reads the Baseline, so capture one after saving project changes if you need to see newly added Texts. Titles help a person recognize a Text; the GUID is the stable selector.

## Example

```powershell
motif texts list --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Human output lists each Text's title, interlinearization percentage, and GUID. JSON returns those details with a flag showing whether a Baseline was available; without a Baseline, human output asks you to capture one first.

## Related commands

- [Choose a Default Selection](cmd:selection%20set-default) stores Text GUIDs for later runs.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) can measure words from named Texts.

entries.title: Inspect parse timing
entries.description: Reads timing evidence for an Assessment, optionally narrowed to words or grouped by kind or rule. Use it to locate expensive parsing work after an Assessment.
entries.helpPage:
# Inspect parse timing

`timing` reads timing measurements recorded in an Assessment. It can narrow the result to words and group costs by kind or rule. Add `--proposal <id>` to use the latest Trial's measurements.

## When to use it

Use this when an Assessment shows costly parsing and you want to identify which rules or kinds account for the parser's work. Name an Assessment when the project has more than one measurement.

Without `--assessment`, Timing reads the Default Selection's current results, including explicit replacements made with `assess --replaces`. Naming an Assessment reads its original words and measurements. Explicit timing overrides replace only words that run measured; they cannot add other words to it.

## Example

```powershell
motif timing --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --proposal <proposalId> --by rule --top 10
```

## What it prints

The command compares parser work only when the Trial retained a compatible Baseline Assessment for the selected words. It reports the percentage change for the selected scope and individual words. Object changes require complete work counters for the same words and a matching object identity on both sides. A new object, missing detail, a stopped search, a zero Baseline or an incompatible parser makes the affected comparison unavailable; the command gives a reason instead of estimating it.

`--rule` takes `kind:key`, such as `morph_rule:12345678-1234-1234-abcd-123456789abc`. Names are display labels; object identities distinguish rules with the same name. `--json` returns the comparisons as structured data.

JSON identifies each word's producing Assessment, invocation and measurement time. It also records the selected run's Baseline and captured FieldWorks save, when available. Its evidence relationship distinguishes Current, Historical, SavedSince and Unknown; current-project freshness is reported separately, so a new Baseline does not make an old measurement current.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) creates timing evidence.
- [Query parse statistics](cmd:stats) forwards a query to PanGloss for detailed counts.

entries.title: Trace a word
entries.description: Runs PanGloss for one word against the project's current Baseline and returns its diagnostic. Use it to inspect recorded analyses and trace events.
entries.helpPage:
# Trace a word

`trace` runs PanGloss for one word against the project's current Baseline and reads the diagnostic used by Try a Word. Add `--proposal <id>` to trace against that Proposal's Trial copy. It does not change the project or store a new Assessment.

## Trace a word now

```powershell
motif trace --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --word mirusi
```

Add `--json` to get the typed response, including the shared `reading` and the diagnostic's recorded provenance. A clean process exit does not establish that the parser's work limit or time safety net was not reached; when the diagnostic cannot report that, completion is unknown.

If the project has no Baseline, capture one with `motif baseline capture --project <fwdata>` before tracing. Trace uses that saved grammar; it does not inspect unsaved FieldWorks changes.

For an unparsed word, text output names the shape whose recorded lexical lookup found no root and explains recorded refusal codes. A stem that reaches an unapplied required template has a different reason from an attempt that builds the wrong surface. A recorded code can be explained without an owner's detailed explanation; absent details remain unavailable. A trace without recorded reasons says so, and an unfinished search cannot establish that the word has no analysis.

When Motif captures a trace, `hostCapture.lexiconEntryCount` records the number of lexical entries in the exact Baseline or Trial copy used. A completed trace with an empty lexicon names that fact and the word, instead of guessing which affix or spelling is wrong. A missing count is unknown. Saved traces retain this count and their recorded reasons without opening the current project.

## Trace a Trial report case

A report-bound trace selects an exact case and side: `motif proposal trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId> --report <reportId> --case <caseKey> --trace --side after`. Motif uses the recorded parser, grammar and limits or explains that the exact inputs are unavailable. The diagnostic has its own identity and completion; it does not alter the batch report.

## Read a saved trace

```powershell
motif trace --load "C:\Temp\mirusi.trace.json"
```

`--load` reads the saved PanGloss diagnostic without opening a project or running a parser. It uses the same reader as a live trace, so the returned word, analyses, attempts, and recorded tree share one interpretation. Try a Word translates the recorded refusal code into a sentence while retaining the code and the original evidence. A rule or required feature is named only when recorded; neighboring events do not establish which rule caused a failure. The window folds forward building events into Plain and keeps the full parser order in Expert.

## Related commands

- [Load a saved trace](cmd:trace%20--load) reads a diagnostic without a parser.
- [Prepare an AI Handoff](cmd:handoff) writes project context and retained parse evidence.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records parse results for chosen words.

entries.title: Load a saved trace
entries.description: Reads a saved diagnostic without opening a project or starting PanGloss. Use it to inspect earlier trace evidence with the same reader as a live trace.
entries.helpPage:
# Load a saved trace

`trace --load` reads a saved PanGloss diagnostic without opening a project or starting the parser. It uses the same reader as a live trace.

## Example

```powershell
motif trace --load "C:\Temp\mirusi.trace.json"
```

Add `--json` to get the typed response, including its shared `reading` and recorded provenance. Motif keeps the producer diagnostic unchanged; a clean process exit does not establish whether a trace reached its search limit, so completion can remain unknown.

## Related commands

- [Trace a word](cmd:trace) runs PanGloss against a project's current Baseline.
- [Prepare an AI Handoff](cmd:handoff) includes a selected word's trace with its summary.

entries.title: Trial a Proposal
entries.description: Measures a Proposal on a throwaway copy and records review evidence. Read observed red flags, incomplete cases and retained details before deciding what to do.
entries.helpPage:
# Trial a Proposal

A Trial measures a Proposal on a throwaway copy. It records a Dry Run and parser evidence so that you can review changes before deciding what to do.

Run `motif trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId> --wait`, then read the saved report with `motif proposal trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId>`.
