The page shows work by kind and rule when the parser recorded it for every chosen word. A very large run keeps those as totals for the whole run, so they show only for all of its words together. A run stored before Motif kept those totals says the work was not kept and lists the rules without parser work or shares; choose **Parse all words** again to keep them. A chosen part of a very large run says the same without that advice, because parsing again does not keep work for a part. Open **Show counts** to see each kind's recorded count; a kind that does not count says **Not counted**.

The compact word row names PanGloss's outcome as **Same**, **Different**, **No parse**, or **Stopped**. The meaning is separate and hidden in this list; a matching morphology alone does not imply agreement with a Disapproved opinion.

Select a rule row to see its costliest words; open **Inspect** on the row to see its FieldWorks facts and link. When object timing detail is limited, a rule's word list covers only the retained words, so a costlier use may be outside it. When a timing row names a lexical entry, it uses the entry's form and gloss when those facts are available. Long rule titles end with an ellipsis in the side panel; point at or focus the title to read it in full. While the Inspector is open, the rule table uses the available width and hides **Kind**. An amber warning mark appears only when a stored grammar finding names that same item by identity. Choose the mark to open that finding on the Warnings page. The inspector separates words that use a morpheme in a stored analysis from words where the parser tried it. Its word, parser work and counts come from that item’s recorded timers; if none were recorded, it says so. In **Detailed statistics**, a word's parser work keep one shading scale across the selected words. **By word** uses those same words; other groups show the complete parse and say so. The groups for rules and other grammar objects show no parser work column, because the parser's object rows count a different unit; the rule table above gives each rule's parser work.

Choose **Slowest** to inspect timing for the words with the most parser work; each shows its parser work. To read individual word parser work, expand **Detailed statistics** and choose **By word**; Timing does not repeat those words in a separate list beside a rule's costliest words. To measure selected words again, open **Re-run**, choose **Seconds per word** or **Parser work limit**, then choose **Re-run chosen words**. The parser work limit starts at **20,000,000**. **Cancel** stops that rerun. When you retry, raise **Parser work limit** after a stop at the work limit or increase **Seconds per word** after a stop at the time safety net. When the current totals include re-runs, Timing labels the number of separate measurements. Open **Detailed statistics** to load its rows; changing the group loads the new group.

In **Detailed statistics**, **Stopped** counts words recorded as stopping at the work limit or at the time safety net, and the **Completion** column says which. For the work limit, raise **Parser work limit**; PanGloss also raises its derived work limit. The time safety net depends on how fast this computer is, so it is a time, not a count of work; increase **Seconds per word** for it. If the record does not distinguish the two, Timing keeps the reason general. **Analyses** counts words with more than one analysis; sort by that column to find them. A rule's share says how much of the work its steps recorded, not what caused a word to parse or stop.

![Saved parse timings on the Timing page](shot:review-apply-refresh-parse/timing)

A refused word wears **PanGloss can’t read it** and keeps the parser’s reason on its row and card. It is not a completed search that found no analysis; timing shows only measurements the parser recorded. Refused words are left out of **Re-run chosen words** because repeating them cannot produce a parse time.

entries.title: Try a Word
entries.description: Use Try a Word to trace one word through the grammar. The word does not need to appear in a chosen text or exist in the FieldWorks project.
entries.helpPage:
# Try a Word

Use **Try a Word** to trace one word through the grammar. The word does not need to appear in a chosen text or exist in the FieldWorks project.

A live trace belongs to the open project. Switching projects or closing the project cancels a trace in progress and clears its result; open that project again to try the word again.

1. Enter a word in **Type any word...**.
2. Choose **Try it** and wait for the trace. Choose **Cancel** to interrupt a running search.
3. Read the result and whether the search stopped at the work limit or the time safety net. **Search incomplete** takes precedence even if the parser found an analysis; an unfinished search cannot establish that no analysis exists.
4. Read the result summary and analysis cards, then **Recorded trace**. Each summary groups analyses with proven equal morphology. **Recorded twice** counts source records; it does not establish two different derivations. Each card shows the recorded morpheme names even when PanGloss cannot match them to FieldWorks entries. Glosses appear when recorded; absent glosses are not inferred.
5. Select a recorded event to read its explanation. Plain translates recorded reason codes into sentences. Only a missing reason says **PanGloss didn't record why.** An unfamiliar code remains visible.

Choose **Plain** or **Expert** beside **Try it**. The filled control shows the selected view. The installed window remembers your choice. Switching keeps the same recorded attempt, selected event address and open inspector; it does not run the parser again. Addresses identify occurrences within this saved trace, not across newly generated traces.

**Plain** puts **Why It Did Not Parse** and **The Attempt That Got Furthest** or **Attempts That Got Furthest** above the trace. A sentence names a rule or required feature only when PanGloss recorded it; the small code remains visible. The building story starts with the recorded stem form, then forward affix and phonological steps, then the result. Additional events are counted at the end and remain in **Expert**. Selecting a separate recorded event keeps it visible without making it part of that attempt. **Tried** does not establish that an affix was built.

**Expert** keeps event names, subrule indices and input/output shapes in the parser's order, including both recorded passes. Missing input and output values appear blank; focus their tokens to learn that they were not recorded. A subrule appears only when the parser recorded a positive index. Choose **Show one analysis path** and turn off **Every step** to read its recorded ancestors and terminal event. **Showing every step** includes other search context; neighboring events alone never establish attempt membership or a cause. **Phonological rules applied** lists recorded phonological events in the chosen view, with each event's own outcome. **Tried** does not mean **Applied**, and an unchanged shape does not prove application. **Parser record** starts folded and keeps the exact source analyses, producer identifiers, projection details and unprojected morpheme names. FieldWorks morpheme forms appear only when their projections are available; parser names alone do not establish a FieldWorks analysis.

Select an event to read its sentence directly beneath the event row. The selected event's **Parser record** and rejection details start folded. The record preserves unknown producer fields and omits its children from this detail view; saving still keeps the whole diagnostic. Tokens explain themselves on hover or keyboard focus. **Environment notation** keeps the recorded diagnostic operand intact and shows **Authored environment notation unavailable**. Decoding requires the trace to explicitly identify authored environment text; the supported trace formats do not establish it. Strings, structured operands and punctuation such as `/`, `_`, `#`, brackets, parentheses and `?` cannot establish that language by themselves, so they remain raw.

**Reason not recorded**, **Rejection details not recorded**, **Grammar source not recorded**, and **FieldWorks word context unavailable** identify facts the page cannot establish. Missing word context does not mean the word is absent from FieldWorks. The recorded tree shows search context; neighboring events alone do not establish which rule caused an attempt to fail.

**FieldWorks beside the parser** shows every stored analysis for the returned word, whether the trace parsed it or not, with **Approved**, **Disapproved** or **Unknown** beside each analysis. Identical displayed analyses share one interlinear line with counts for each Opinion; this display grouping does not establish identity equality. Each piece shows a trace mark only when an event names its exact identity; otherwise it says **Not in the parser trace**. The result line also names the recorded opinions. A completed parsed search shows **Same** or **Different** when recorded identities establish a comparison; otherwise it shows **Parsed** and the analysis count. A completed search that finds no analysis shows the same meaning as the Matrix, such as **Lost** for an Approved word. An unfinished search cannot establish that an Approved analysis was lost. Save and Baseline times use the computer's local time. **FieldWorks saved since** follows the same freshness evidence as the top bar. A word absent from that Baseline differs from a wordform with no stored analyses. Unknown membership and unavailable context remain explicit.

**No terminal attempt was recorded before the search stopped** marks an interrupted search without a terminal attempt. Its recorded progress remains available in the tree. Recorded terminal attempts show only their returned reasons and attribution. **Steps on this path** lists actual ancestors and the terminal event; **Recorded tree context** shows nearby events whose membership is not established. Event addresses identify repeated occurrences within this saved trace, and the small notation names the recorded pass and outcome.

An earlier parse's parser work appear by rule in a separate block named by the word's recorded measurement time. The block stays hidden when the source time or per-rule work was not recorded. These counts cover that parse's whole search for the word, including stopped attempts, and do not describe steps in this trace. Shares use that parse's total parser work; **Not attributed** is work the parser did not assign to an object.

The trace's effort table shows parser work by category, including **Not attributed**. Those rows add up to the traced word's total parser work. **Segments examined** counts a different unit and does not add up to that total.

Use **Analyze texts**, **Timing**, and **AI Handoff** beside the result. **Analyze texts** opens the returned word in its text, where opinions are changed. These actions keep addressing the displayed result when you edit or clear the input for another Try. **AI Handoff** keeps this diagnostic and the Baseline recorded with it; it does not parse the word again or make a replacement trace. The menu beside **Try it** contains recent words and tools for copying, saving or opening a trace. **Copy for a chat model** includes the instructions, one-line summary, and original diagnostic JSON; review it before sharing because it can contain real project data. **Full derivation** starts folded and provides all recorded steps and filters. Saving keeps the original diagnostic regardless of display filters.

Both views name the Baseline that actually produced the trace, using its capture time in the computer's local time; a timestamp from another day includes its weekday and date. A trace without a recorded Baseline says so. When the earlier parse and the trace record different Baseline identities, the page says **This trace and the earlier parse used different Baselines. Refresh and try again.** That difference does not establish that a grammar change caused a failed search. Capture details keep the source project's save time as well. A Refresh published while a request waits can change which Baseline it uses. An older workspace description cannot relabel the returned evidence.

Recorded details can include the replacement lexical entry for a Blocked event, the template slots a branch applied or skipped, and the completion gate that ended a partial attempt. A completed lookup records how many possible roots it returned; those are not counts of successful analyses. Typed rejection details retain the operands PanGloss actually tested, including any authored environment identity and text. A phonological step with an unavailable reason remains unknown.

A Blocked event records an intermediate result. In the supported parser it means replacement by a compatible entry in the same lexical family; search can continue. Missing reasons, rejection details and grammar sources are shown as not recorded, and unfamiliar reason codes keep their raw notation.


![A word parsed in Try a Word](shot:try-word-typing/trace)

The main analysis cards combine source records only when available projections establish equal ordered allomorph and grammatical information identities, including inflection type. Equal spellings alone do not establish that they are the same analysis. The recorded source list keeps every producer record.

**Why It Did Not Parse** also shows recorded zero-match lexical lookups when there is no terminal attempt. For example, a lookup of `s` may have no matching root, with no affix-building step recorded. This does not establish that `s` is a plural suffix. An invalid-shape refusal reports that PanGloss could not read the word with the project’s phonemes; Motif names specific characters only when the parser’s evidence names them. If the last parse refused the word but the trace searched it, the page labels the refusal **in last parse** and keeps the traced search’s result separate.

The comparison places FieldWorks beside the recorded parser analyses in a wide page and stacks them in a narrow page. Scroll an analysis list to read more; open **Full analysis details** below the attempts for recorded morph details. Expert view also offers the parser record.

entries.title: Warnings
entries.description: Warnings shows findings from a check of the whole grammar and allomorph refusals recorded by Parse all words for the current Baseline and Selection. Findings from the parse are labelled Parse all words and retain the parser's refusal reason. The grammar check and the parse can report different findings. PanGloss may include an explanation or guidance with each finding.
entries.helpPage:
# Warnings

**Warnings** shows findings from a check of the whole grammar and allomorph refusals recorded by **Parse all words** for the current [Baseline](term:baseline) and **Selection**. Findings from the parse are labelled **Parse all words** and retain the parser's refusal reason. The grammar check and the parse can report different findings. PanGloss may include an explanation or guidance with each finding.

PanGloss reports an unreadable phonological environment as a warning. Roots ignore that restriction but keep valid ones; ordinary affixes add an unrestricted pass beside valid passes; an infix with no valid position is skipped.

If the grammar has not been checked for this Baseline, choose **Check the grammar again**. PanGloss reads the whole grammar, so a check can take a minute for a large project. **Refresh** captures a new Baseline and checks the grammar again. Later visits show the stored findings; opening the page does not start a check.

The filter chips count findings by report level. The table has one row per kind. Motif groups the rows by area, a guess from the finding's code and the kinds of FieldWorks item it names: Environments, Phonological rules, Affixes, or otherwise Other findings. The areas keep that fixed order. Each row shows severity, item, problem text and named words; the area heading shows its total finding count. The named words column shows an exact count, **none** when the finding says no Selection word uses the named item, or is blank when an exact count is unavailable; the cell's tooltip says so. Choose **Details** or press Enter on a selected row to read each finding. The **⋯** menu has the same details action and any available follow-up actions. **Touch your words** shows the distinct Selection words matched to named FieldWorks items, when available. Turn it on to show only kinds with those matches. The **Sort** menu orders the rows inside each area by that same count or by the order in the report; it does not reorder the areas.

A finding may have exact word uses, words reached only by membership or spelling, or no word list. Exact uses include analyses held in FieldWorks and analyses the parser returned, including words typed into setup with no Texts. If a word has no analysis, a named allomorph or entry can reach it through a **spelling match**: the word contains the form's spelling. This does not confirm use of that item. Membership and spelling remain labelled because neither confirms an exact use of the named item. **None of your words** means PanGloss named an item but no Selection word has a confirmed identity use. Choose **Details** on the row to see any separately labelled membership or spelling matches. Spelling matches show their distinct word count. When a word count cannot be established, Motif leaves it unavailable instead of showing zero. If Motif cannot follow every named connection, Details retains confirmed words but the table leaves the full count unavailable. If PanGloss names no item, the row says so.

Choose **Details** on a row to read each finding's explanation, **What to do in FieldWorks** guidance, named subjects, and exact parser message. When PanGloss supplied no guidance, the row says **PanGloss gives no advice for this kind yet**. A named entry with a verified destination has an **Open … in Lexicon Edit ↗** link; other subjects open only through the verified destination PanGloss supplied. If a kind no longer appears after **Refresh**, its row says **Gone after Refresh**. Save edits in FieldWorks, refresh Motif, then parse the affected words again to see their current results.

![Grammar findings saved for the current Baseline](shot:warnings-filter/findings)

PanGloss supplies each finding's title, description, explanation and guidance in the report's recorded language. **Learn more** opens its reference when available. Motif displays that text without adding advice of its own.

A missing or unresolved subject has no object link. A project setting has no individual object to open. A named live object opens only through the destination PanGloss supplied; Motif does not infer a destination from the finding's sentence.

entries.title: What Motif does
entries.description: Motif tells you how well the FieldWorks parser handles your words: which ones parse, which of your approved analyses the grammar still builds, how much parser work each word takes, and what the grammar check found. You can also look at one word closely and collect corrections to its analyses.
entries.helpPage:
# What Motif does

Motif tells you how well the FieldWorks parser handles your words: which ones parse, which of your approved analyses the grammar still builds, how much parser work each word takes, and what the grammar check found. You can also look at one word closely and collect corrections to its analyses.

Motif reads your saved FieldWorks project. It writes nothing to it until you open **Review Changes** and choose **Apply to FieldWorks project**. FieldWorks is where you edit the project.

The window uses Andika for its interface text; linguistic text uses the fonts selected in the FieldWorks project's writing systems. Motif includes Andika, Charis SIL, Doulos SIL and Gentium Plus, so a project using one of them does not need a separate font installation.

To start, [install Motif](guide:install), then [open your project](guide:open-a-project).

Motif uses PanGloss to parse words. [Parse all words](term:parse-all-words) keeps the results of each run. The [Overview](term:overview) shows stored results such as Text Coverage, **Approved analyses kept**, timing, and grammar warnings. Opening the window shows the last results; it doesn't parse again.

1. [Open your project](guide:open-a-project) and press **Refresh**.
2. [Choose the words to measure](guide:first-run-setup) and start the first run.
3. Read the [Overview](guide:overview).
4. After your first run, open **Texts**, choose a word that did not parse, and use [Try a Word](guide:try-a-word) to inspect it.
5. In **Texts**, look at words and choose analysis changes.
6. On **Review Changes**, check them, then choose **Apply to FieldWorks project**. See [Applying changes](guide:apply-to-fieldworks) first.
7. After you edit the grammar in FieldWorks, save, press **Refresh**, then **Parse all words**.

For details about individual steps, see the [Refresh](guide:refresh-numbers), [Texts](guide:texts) and [Review Changes](guide:review-changes) guides.

For keyboard navigation and shortcuts, see [Keyboard shortcuts](guide:keyboard-shortcuts).
For window zoom, theme, project parsing limits and Help, see [Settings](guide:settings).

You can also make an **AI Handoff** folder with project context and a question for a chat model. Review the data-sensitivity notice before sharing it: the folder can contain real grammar, lexicon, and text data.

![Motif’s Overview after opening a project](shot:open-project-overview/overview)

entries.title: When a change no longer fits
entries.description: When a pending change is in the No longer fits group, use these steps to check the original choice against the current project.
entries.helpPage:
# When a change no longer fits

When a pending change is in the **No longer fits** group, use these steps to check the original choice against the current project.

1. Open **Review Changes**. Changes that no longer fit are in the **No longer fits** group at the top of the page. Select one to read what changed in FieldWorks in the Inspector. If the Inspector is closed, choose **Details** from the change's **⋯** menu.
2. If you want to keep trying the change, save the project in FieldWorks, then choose **Refresh** in Motif.
3. In the **No longer fits** group, choose **Check again**. Motif checks whether the original identities still fit.
4. If it still says **No longer fits**, choose **Undo all** beside that group, or choose **Undo** beside one change. Return to **Texts** and make a new choice against the current project.

Apply remains blocked while any change no longer fits. The window does not offer a way to force a change that no longer fits.

![Review Changes with a choice marked No longer fits](shot:no-longer-fits/review)

entries.title: When something goes wrong
entries.description: If a command or action is refused, first read the message in Motif. It often explains what needs to change, such as saving in FieldWorks, refreshing the Baseline, or removing a change that no longer fits.
entries.helpPage:
# When something goes wrong

If a command or action is refused, first read the message in Motif. It often explains what needs to change, such as saving in FieldWorks, refreshing the Baseline, or removing a change that no longer fits.

You can open the same report preview from [Settings](guide:settings). It is also available from a refusal or a stalled parse.

For a problem report, choose **Report a Problem** in Settings (or **Report a problem** in the status bar) and review the preview. By default it includes Motif and PanGloss versions, your operating system, the window action, the refusal code, the command's exit status when available, and a stack without file locations. It leaves out project paths and names, words, grammar, and raw parser output. You can choose **Include Local Details** to add the error text and facts, which include everything shown under Details and sometimes more, such as the places Motif looked for a missing PanGloss; those may contain project or language data. Copying the report or opening the issue form happens only after you review the preview, and the issue form is not submitted automatically.

Send feedback through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/sillsdev/motif/issues). If you cannot use GitHub, copy the reviewed report and email it to [john_lambert@sil.org](mailto:john_lambert@sil.org). Review any local details before sharing them.

If Motif says the project store was made by a different version and offers **Delete Motif's store and reopen**, read the confirmation before continuing. That action deletes Motif's store and recreates it; changes not applied yet are lost, but the FieldWorks project is not touched.

If Motif says its file for this project is damaged, close every Motif window. Keep a copy of the matching `.motif.db` file beside the project's `.fwdata` file if support may need it. Remove only that Motif file, then reopen the project; changes not applied yet will be lost, but the FieldWorks project is unchanged. If you cannot confirm the file belongs to Motif, leave it in place and ask for help.

If Motif cannot read its machine store, close every Motif window and keep a copy of the `motif.db` file at the path shown in the recovery instructions. Move or remove that file only if you can confirm it is Motif's machine store, then reopen Motif. Its Known projects and local usage history will be cleared; FieldWorks projects and their pending changes are unchanged. If you cannot confirm the file belongs to Motif, leave it in place and ask for help.

For a parser trace, open **Diagnostic tools** from **Try a Word**. You can save or copy diagnostic information for a particular word. It can include real word forms and morphological details, so review it before sharing.

If the app stops after an error, the separate **Motif Has Stopped** window keeps the full error under **Details** and offers **Report a Problem**. The same preview shows what will be copied or placed in the issue form. The local **Details** may contain project paths or linguistic information; they are added to a report only when you choose **Include Local Details**.

![A recorded parser trace to inspect in Try a Word](shot:try-word-typing/trace)

entries.title: Writing systems in the window
entries.description: Motif uses the writing-system settings saved in the Baseline when it displays project language text. Text keeps its FieldWorks direction and style size in the window.
entries.helpPage:
# Writing systems in the window

Motif uses the writing-system settings saved in the Baseline when it displays project language text. Text keeps its FieldWorks direction and style size in the window.

Most word forms, glosses and interlinear fields use the **Normal** style. A line in **Analyze texts** uses the source paragraph's style. Motif includes Andika, Charis SIL, Doulos SIL and Gentium Plus, and prefers an installed copy of those fonts when it is available. It treats **Charis** and **Charis SIL** as names for the same family. If another requested font is missing, Motif uses an available fallback and shows one quiet notice the first time it draws text in that writing system.

In FieldWorks, change a writing system's font, font features or direction under **Format › Set up Vernacular Writing Systems…** or **Format › Set up Analysis Writing Systems…**. Choose the **Font** or **General** tab. Change style-specific fonts and sizes under **Format › Styles…**.

Capture a new [Baseline](term:baseline) after changing these settings so Motif reads the saved values. [Show writing systems](cmd:writing-systems) lists the values Motif recorded.
